    # The pattern catalog
    
    Every antipattern here was found in real agent-written code (agent-comms, and a fork of the Textual app Toad), with the clean form that replaced it. **Agents produce these by default.** Read the catalog before writing a surface receipt, and cite pattern IDs in receipts ("IMPL-2 in `coordination.py`") so the executing agent knows exactly which clean form applies.
    
    ## Contents
    
    - [How to read an entry](#how-to-read-an-entry)
    - [The rungs](#the-rungs)
    - [Index of patterns](#index-of-patterns)
    - Files: [implementation.md](implementation.md) · [membership.md](membership.md) · [identity.md](identity.md) · [boundaries.md](boundaries.md) · [over-time.md](over-time.md) · [agent-defaults.md](agent-defaults.md)
    
    ## How to read an entry
    
    Each entry has the same parts:
    
    - **The slop:** real code, trimmed. This is what an agent writes when nothing stops it.
    - **What the code makes you know:** the fact a reader or maintainer must supply because no declaration states it. That missing declaration is the debt: it is a required answer maintained outside the mechanism.
    - **The clean form:** the owned structure, using the shared abstractions (`DeclaredFamily`, `FieldCodec`, `LifecycleState`, `MroDispatch`, `Command`, `TypedTable`, capability mixins).
    - **What collapses:** how many edits a new case needs before and after. That count is what separates factoring from relocation.
    - **Detected by:** the overlay category, NRA detector, or grep that finds it.
    
    ## The rungs
    
    A required answer can live outside its mechanism at three levels. Fix the lowest broken rung first: behaviour cannot be owned by a family whose members cannot be told apart.
    
    | Rung | The question | Typical slop | Clean form |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | **Identity** | Which thing is this, and which fact is this field? | one concept encoded several ways; one name or field answering two questions; a fact split across stores | one value type per identity; distinct names; state carrying its own data |
    | **Membership** | Which things belong to this set? | hand-written rosters, literal sets and name strings restating a family | capabilities on the classes; sets and names derived from the family |
    | **Implementation** | What does each case do? | switches on strings, enums or types outside the family | each case owns its behaviour; shared behaviour on the parent; overlapping capabilities composed by multiple inheritance |
    
    Two further groups cut across the rungs: **boundaries** (raw data handled everywhere instead of decoded once), and **duplication over time** (old versions, converters and dead code left beside the new). The last file, **agent defaults**, names the behaviours that produce all of the above.
    
    ## From overlay and census findings to patterns
    
    | Finding | Usually | Check also |
    |---|---|---|
    | `string_dispatch` | IMPL-1, IMPL-6, IMPL-7 | MEMB-2 if the literals are a subset; IMPL-5 if the subject recurs in another function |
    | `isinstance_switch` | IMPL-3, IMPL-4 | IMPL-9 when a `kind` field accompanies it |
    | census `string_dispatch`, `type_switch` and their `_arms` measures (per function) | IMPL-1, IMPL-2, IMPL-3, IMPL-4 | subjects count candidates with at least three distinct arms; `_arms` also catches growth of existing candidates. Decide per site whether the taxonomy is external or a missing family. Counts do not catch subthreshold cases or additions offset by removals; admitted ownership needs site-specific guards |
    | census `builtin_handler_type_switch` | IMPL-3, BOUND-1 | primitive MroDispatch `handles` arms count individually outside the canonical codec, including one per method. AST/domain handlers are not primitive cases; this is screening, not a dynamic import/execution proof |
    | census `family_flattened` | BOUND-8 | distinguish derived wire identity from name-based behavior selection; pure declaration-name properties are identity, while string comparisons remain consumer sites. Unknown bindings are outside the syntactic proof, not proof of redispatch |
    | `raw_shape` marked BYPASSES | BOUND-2 | MEMB-5 when the subject is a database row |
    | `raw_shape` marked HAND-MAPPED | MEMB-5 | read what the target class is: a decoder, or a presentation type restating the wire |
    | `raw_shape` unmodeled | BOUND-1 | BOUND-3 nearby; IDEN-5 if keys join two stores |
    | `exact_key_set` | BOUND-3 | |
    | `named_attribute`, `getattr_default` | BOUND-7 | TIME-3 when the default tolerates old shapes |
    | `god_class`, `god_function` | IMPL-8, AGENT-4 | read for IDEN-1 and IMPL-12 inside it |
    | `long_condition`, census `boolean_chain_terms` | syntactic **ownership leads**: IDEN-1 (same-value comparisons), IDEN-3 (absence tests on another object), IMPL-10 (own attributes), BOUND-1 (type tests), IMPL-1 (literal comparisons), IMPL-14 (other expressions) | inspect each lead before choosing a target. Predicate calls remain OPEN: they may already query the correct owner. A chain alone does not prove a missing structure |
    | `literal_roster` | MEMB-1, MEMB-2, MEMB-3 | |
    | `legacy_marker` | TIME-1 to TIME-4 | innocent uses of the words stay, renamed |
    | `dead_module` | TIME-6 | |
    | census `foreign_absence_probe` | IDEN-3 | the owner should report its state; the probes restate it |
    | census `codec_subclass` | TIME-9 | two wire forms of the types the subclass special-cases |
    | `positional_insert` | MEMB-5 | |
    | `embedded_script` | BOUND-5 | TIME-7 for copied defaults inside it |
    | `child_process_site` spread over many modules | IMPL-13 | IDEN-8 |
    | census `type_identity_check`, `string_key_subscript` | BOUND-1 | |
    | NRA `external_enum_case_recovery` | IMPL-2 | IMPL-11, IMPL-10 |
    
    ## Index of patterns
    
    **Implementation** ([implementation.md](implementation.md))
    - IMPL-1 String dispatch on a kind
    - IMPL-2 Enum with no methods, switched on everywhere
    - IMPL-3 A `match` over types that already exist
    - IMPL-4 The half-finished family
    - IMPL-5 One dispatch written twice
    - IMPL-6 Effects decided centrally by key
    - IMPL-7 A string action with a parameter bag
    - IMPL-8 The undeclared class: closures sharing `nonlocal` state
    - IMPL-9 The longhand tagged union
    - IMPL-10 Legality by runtime rejection
    - IMPL-11 A transition table beside its states
    - IMPL-12 One procedure copied, with drift
    - IMPL-13 One mechanism reimplemented at different levels of rigour
    - IMPL-14 Validation as one anonymous boolean
    
    **Membership** ([membership.md](membership.md))
    - MEMB-1 A roster restating a family
    - MEMB-2 A roster restating a capability
    - MEMB-3 Literal sets and special names spelled in many places
    - MEMB-4 Hand-written name strings
    - MEMB-5 One record's shape written four times
    
    **Identity** ([identity.md](identity.md))
    - IDEN-1 One field answering two questions
    - IDEN-2 One name with several meanings
    - IDEN-3 One concept, several encodings
    - IDEN-4 A name that disagrees with its value
    - IDEN-5 One fact split across stores
    - IDEN-6 Keyed by the wrong identity
    - IDEN-7 A check wider than the question
    - IDEN-8 A bare process ID as identity
    
    **Boundaries** ([boundaries.md](boundaries.md))
    - BOUND-1 Raw data read at every use, and re-validated
    - BOUND-2 Bypassing the class that already models the data
    - BOUND-3 Hand-written exact key sets
    - BOUND-4 Structure flattened to text, then parsed back

    class RuntimeResolution(BaseModel):
        core_commit: str
        packages: dict[str, PackageRecord]
    
        @classmethod
        def record_path(cls) -> Path:
            return LaunchRuntime.current_pointer() / "build.json"
    
        @classmethod
        def at(cls, prefix: Path) -> RuntimeResolution:
            return cls.model_validate_json((prefix / cls.record_path().name).read_bytes())
    
        @classmethod
        def installed(cls) -> RuntimeResolution | UnbuiltRuntime:
            prefix = LaunchRuntime.installed().prefix
            if not (prefix / cls.record_path().name).is_file():
                return UnbuiltRuntime(prefix)
            return cls.at(prefix)
    
        @classmethod
        def capture(cls, python: Path, core: str) -> RuntimeResolution:
            environment = LaunchRuntime(python).environment(os.environ)
            program = """import importlib.metadata as m,json,sys
    from pathlib import Path
    import agent_comms
    from agent_comms.package_stamp import STAMP
    from packaging.utils import canonicalize_name
    if not Path(agent_comms.__file__).resolve().is_relative_to(Path(sys.prefix).resolve()):
        raise ValueError('Core is editable, not a built runtime package')
    if STAMP.commit() != sys.argv[1]:
        raise ValueError('The wheel stamp does not name the selected source')
    print(json.dumps({canonicalize_name(d.metadata['Name']): {
        'version':d.version,
        'source':json.loads(source) if (source := d.read_text('direct_url.json')) else None
    } for d in m.distributions()}))
    """
            packages = TypeAdapter(dict[str, PackageRecord]).validate_json(
                subprocess.check_output([python, "-c", program, core], env=environment)
            )
            return cls(core_commit=core, packages=packages)
    
        def save(self, prefix: Path) -> None:
            path = prefix / self.record_path().name
            path.write_text(self.model_dump_json(indent=2) + "\n")
            path.chmod(0o600)
    
        def pins(self) -> dict[str, PackagePin]:
            result: dict[str, PackagePin] = {
                canonicalize_name(name): record.pin() for name, record in self.packages.items()
            }
            # Wheel URLs locate build output, not the source revisions recorded by this owner.
            for member in RuntimePackage.members_with(RuntimePackage):
                result[member.distribution] = GitPin(
                    self.packages[member.distribution].version, member.commit(self)
                )
            return result
    
        def matches(self, lock: Path, python: Path, core: str) -> bool:
            resolved = ResolvedLock.model_validate(tomllib.loads(lock.read_text()))
            print(f"install: real lock decodes {len(resolved.package)} packages", file=sys.stderr)
            # sync --locked has already selected the platform, groups and extras. Read its
            # selected names/versions, then obtain every source identity from the lock itself.
            selected = TypeAdapter(dict[str, str]).validate_json(
                subprocess.check_output(
                    [
                        python,
                        "-c",
                        "import importlib.metadata as m,json; "
                        "from packaging.utils import canonicalize_name as n; "
                        'print(json.dumps({n(d.metadata["Name"]):d.version '
                        "for d in m.distributions()}))",
                    ]
                )
            )
            return self.pins() == resolved.pins(selected, core)
            return (f"{self.source[:12]} -> {self.target[:12]}",
                    f"Pending carries: {', '.join(self.pending) or 'none'}")
    
    
    @dataclass(frozen=True)
    class RehearsedUpgrade(Upgrade):
        rehearsal: Rehearsal
        commands: tuple[TimedCommand, ...] = field(kw_only=True)
        """Every command the install ran, in the order each finished, with its time."""
    
        def lines(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
            slowest = sorted(self.commands, key=lambda timed: timed.seconds, reverse=True)[:5]
            return (*super().lines(),
                    f"Commands: {len(self.commands)} in "
                    f"{sum(timed.seconds for timed in self.commands):.1f}s; slowest:",
                    *(timed.line() for timed in slowest))
    
    
    @dataclass(frozen=True)
    class InstalledUpgrade(RehearsedUpgrade, Extendable):
        live: LiveRun
        install: InstallResult
        """The harnesses registered on the bus the target now reads."""
    
        finished: ClassVar[str] = "Install finished"
        """The headline of the post that reports this upgrade."""
    
        def lines(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
            return (*super().lines(), *self.live.lines())
    
    
    @dataclass(frozen=True)
    class UnresumedUpgrade(InstalledUpgrade):
        """Installed, with session bridges paused for the swap that did not come back: the
        install exits non-zero after reporting it."""
    
        unresumed: tuple[str, ...]
    
        finished: ClassVar[str] = "Install finished; session bridges not resumed"
    
        def lines(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
            return (*super().lines(), *self.unresumed)
    
    
    @dataclass(frozen=True)
    class Stack:
        """One built installation and the source checkout containing its install tools."""
    
        checkout: Path
        commands: InstallCommands
        home: Path = HOME
        runtime: LaunchRuntime = field(default_factory=LaunchRuntime.installed)
    
        @property
        def python(self) -> Path:
            return self.runtime.interpreter
    
        @property
        def lock(self) -> Path:
            return self.checkout / "stack/uv.lock"
    
        @property
        def uv(self) -> Path:
            """The uv the installer runs, kept in the installer's own state."""
            return RuntimeHome.uv_path(self.home)
    
        def require_uv(self) -> None:
            if not os.access(self.uv, os.X_OK):
                raise UpgradeRefused(f"No uv executable at {self.uv}; the installer runs only that uv")
    
        @classmethod
        def build(cls, checkout: Path, commands: InstallCommands, home: Path = HOME) -> Stack:
            """Resolve current mains once, then build or reuse their immutable installation."""
            Checkout(checkout).prepare()
            source = cls(checkout, commands, home, runtime=LaunchRuntime.running())
            source.require_uv()
            commands.run(source.uv, "lock", "--project", "stack", "--upgrade", "--python", "3.14",
                         cwd=checkout)
            core = commands.run("git", "-C", checkout, "rev-parse", "HEAD").strip()
            resolution = hashlib.sha256(source.lock.read_bytes()).hexdigest()[:16]
            prefix = home / ".local/share/agent-comms/runtimes" / f"core-{core[:9]}-lock-{resolution}"
            built = replace(source, runtime=LaunchRuntime(prefix / "bin/python"))
            if prefix.exists():
                if not RuntimeResolution.at(prefix).matches(source.lock, built.python, core):
                    raise UpgradeRefused("Existing built runtime differs from its resolved inputs")
                return built
            prefix.parent.mkdir(mode=0o700, parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            prefix.mkdir(mode=0o700)
            try:
                commands.run(source.uv, "sync", "--project", "stack", "--locked", "--python", "3.14",
                             "--no-editable", cwd=checkout,
                             env={**built.environment(), "UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT": str(prefix)})
                built.install_native()
                RuntimeResolution.capture(built.python, core).save(prefix)
                built.imports()
            except BaseException:
                shutil.rmtree(prefix)
                raise
            return built
    
        def test(self, *pytest_arguments: str) -> None:
            """Run checkout tests against this runtime's installed packages, never its source."""
            self.commands.run(self.uv, "pip", "install", "--python", self.python,
                              "-r", "pyproject.toml", "--extra", "dev", cwd=self.checkout,
                              env=self.environment())
            core = self.commands.run("git", "-C", self.checkout, "rev-parse", "HEAD").strip()

                    self.path, key.removeprefix("submodule.").removesuffix(".path"), self.path / value
                )
                for key, value in (line.split(" ", 1) for line in listed.splitlines())
            )
    
        def prepare(self) -> None:
            """Populate the pinned submodules, rebuilding any an interrupted clone left broken.
            A tree that pins none has nothing to prepare."""
            modules = self.submodules()
            if not modules:
                return
            for module in modules:
                if module.broken():
                    module.clear()
            update = subprocess.run(
                (
                    "git",
                    "-C",
                    str(self.path),
                    "submodule",
                    "update",
                    "--init",
                    "--recursive",
                    "--checkout",
                ),
                capture_output=True,
                text=True,
                timeout=300,
            )
            if update.returncode:
                raise CheckoutPrepareError(self.path, update.stderr)
    
        def held_work(self) -> str:
            """Changes outside the pinned submodules, which retiring the tree would lose."""
            return Repo.git(self.path, "status", "--porcelain", "--ignore-submodules=all")
    
        def retire(self) -> None:
            """Remove this worktree. Git refuses any tree holding submodules without --force,
            so this owner checks for held work itself and then forces."""
            held = self.held_work()
            if held:
                raise CheckoutHoldsWorkError(self.path, held)
            common = Path(
                Repo.git(self.path, "rev-parse", "--path-format=absolute", "--git-common-dir").strip()
            )
            Repo.git(common.parent, "worktree", "remove", "--force", str(self.path))
    
    
    class ScratchCheckout(Checkout):
        """A tree made for one run and discarded with whatever the run left in it."""
    
        def held_work(self) -> str:
            return ""

    def manifest(core="core", toad="toad", wheel="old-wheel"):
        return RuntimeResolution.model_validate(
            {
                "core_commit": core,
                "packages": {
                    "agent-comms": {"version": "1", "source": {"url": wheel, "archive_info": {}}},
                    "batrachian-toad": {
                        "version": "2",
                        "source": {"url": "https://example/toad", "vcs_info": {"commit_id": toad}},
                    },
                    "textual": {
                        "version": "3",
                        "source": {
                            "url": "https://example/textual",
                            "vcs_info": {"commit_id": "textual"},
                        },
                    },
                    "rich": {"version": "4", "source": None},
                },
            }
        )
    
    
    def lock():
        return ResolvedLock.model_validate(
            {
                "package": [
                    {"name": "agent-comms", "source": {"editable": ".."}},
                    {
                        "name": "batrachian-toad",
                        "version": "2",
                        "source": {"git": "https://example/toad#toad"},
                    },
                    {
                        "name": "textual",
                        "version": "3",
                        "source": {"git": "https://example/textual#textual"},
                    },
                    {"name": "rich", "version": "4", "source": {"registry": "https://pypi.org/simple"}},
                    # The universal lock contains entries not selected by this synced environment.
                    {
                        "name": "unselected",
                        "version": "5",
                        "source": {"registry": "https://pypi.org/simple"},
                    },
                ]
            }
        )
    
    
    def test_recorded_sources_match_selected_lock_not_wheel_locations():
        built = manifest()
        selected = {name: record.version for name, record in built.packages.items()}
        pins = lock().pins(selected, "core")
        assert built.pins() == pins
        assert manifest(wheel="another-wheel").pins() == pins
        assert manifest(core="changed").pins() != pins
        assert manifest(toad="changed").pins() != pins
        assert lock().pins({**selected, "unselected": "5"}, "core") != built.pins()
    
    
    def test_missing_and_ambiguous_lock_evidence_refuses():
        with pytest.raises(ValueError):
            lock().pins({"missing": "1"}, "core")
        ambiguous = lock()
        ambiguous.package.append(ambiguous.package[0])
        with pytest.raises(ValueError):
            ambiguous.pins({"agent-comms": "1"}, "core")

        interpreter: Annotated[Path, PathText]
    
        @classmethod
        def running(cls) -> LaunchRuntime:
            """Keep ordinary launches on the calling process's installation."""
            return cls(Path(sys.executable))
    
        def child_environment(self, environment: Mapping[str, str]) -> dict[str, str]:
            """A child of this process's own interpreter imports the source this process
            imported; any other installation's child gets exactly the environment its launcher
            built."""
            return RunningSource.serving(self).environment(environment)

## Assistant

Luna found a real gap: CI misses all three patterns. The dispatch check looks for several literal cases, so this dynamic method lookup and flag bag slip through. The checks also don’t track result-channel semantics or who owns the maintenance permission.

        def commit(self, files: dict[str, str | None]) -> str:
            for name, source in files.items():
                path = self.path / self.root / name
                if source is None:
                    path.unlink()
                else:
                    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
                    path.write_text(source)
            self.git("add", "--all")
            self.git("-c", "commit.gpgsign=false", "commit", "-qm", "test", "--allow-empty")

        @contextmanager
        def comparing(self, base: str, head: str) -> Iterator[SpawnedProcess]:
            source = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
            command = (
                sys.executable, str(source / "tools/debt_ratchet.py"),
                "--root", self.root, "--base", base, "--head", head,
                # pytest-xdist runs these comparisons side by side; each keeps a narrow pool.
                "--workers", "2",
            )
            environment = {**os.environ, "PYTHONPATH": os.pathsep.join(
                (str(source / "src"), os.environ["PYTHONPATH"]))}
            with SpawnedProcess.launch(command, cwd=self.path, env=environment,
                                       output=subprocess.PIPE) as child:
                yield child
    
        def compare(self, base: str, head: str, *, timeout: float = 120) -> tuple[int, dict]:
            with self.comparing(base, head) as child:
                result = child.collect(timeout=timeout)
            assert result.returncode in (0, 1), result.stderr[-2000:]
            return result.returncode, json.loads(result.stdout)

    def reconcile_stores(root: Path, staged: Stack) -> StepRun:
        """The target's runtime reconciles every store onto its declarations after the carries,
        under the hold, and names each file it rewrote, so the backup and the rehearsal account
        for the schema change like any carry's rewrite."""
        verb = ReconcileStoresCliCommand.declared_name
        result = staged.cli(root, ReconcileStoresCliCommand)
        return StepRun(verb, Carried(len(result.rewritten), rewritten=result.rewritten))
    
    
    def carry_and_read(root: Path, before: dict[str, SavedFile], pending: tuple[type[Carry], ...],
                       staged: Stack, outgoing: Stack, tree: TargetTree,
                       stopping: tuple[StepRun, ...]) -> CarriedPass:
        """The pass a rehearsal and a live install share once ``before`` was read under the
        transcript hold. The hold is released first: SQLite cannot lend its writer lock to a
        step's process, so a step that writes the transcript store could not run under it.
    
        The bus is read back before the carries and after them, on this root. The read before
        the carries is taken by the outgoing runtime, which reads the bus in the format it was
        written; the read after them is taken by the staged runtime. The two BusReadBack values
        must agree. The first read follows ``before``, so a write it made is a change no step
        names and the carry check refuses it."""
        carried_from = outgoing.verify(root)
        steps = (*stopping, *carry_all(root, pending, staged, tree), reconcile_stores(root, staged))
        files = carried(root, before, steps, RehearsalFiles.declared(steps))
        passed = CarriedPass(steps, files, staged.verify(root))
        passed.require_read(carried_from)
        return passed

    @dataclass(frozen=True)
    class Install[Rehearsed: Rehearsal](ABC):
        """One run once the target's stack is relocked: what it changes on the bus. Its live
        pass takes the rehearsal its own kind produced."""

        def install(self, rehearsal: Rehearsed, bridges: SessionBridgeResumes) -> LiveRun:
            """Session bridges close their bus resources before units stop, then exec in place.
    
            Each serve retains its recorded owner's PID and start time after the hook exits.
            Its control connection survives until live() publishes or rolls back; the
            installed pointer, not a copied target version, selects its successor.
            """
            with ExitStack() as resources:
                for bridge in Serve.running(self.installed.home):
                    bridges.pause(bridge, resources)
                resources.callback(bridges.resume)
                return self.live(rehearsal)
    
        @abstractmethod
        def live(self, rehearsal: Rehearsed) -> LiveRun: ...
    
    
    class ExistingBusInstall[Rehearsed: Rehearsal](Install[Rehearsed]):
        """A bus is already at the root. When a carry step exists or a store's schema differs
        from the target's, one practice copy of it answers what is pending and carries the
        rehearsal; otherwise nothing could change, and no copy is taken."""
    
        @classmethod
        def rehearsed(cls, checkout: Path, root: Path, current: str, target: str,
                      chain: CarryChain, installed: Stack, staged: Stack, tree: TargetTree,
                      installer: InstallerChoice, spill_dir: Path) -> tuple[Install, Rehearsal]:
            if chain.steps or staged.cli(root, PlannedReconcileCliCommand).rewritten:
                with PracticeBus.of(root, installer) as practice:
                    install = cls.of(checkout, root, current, target,
                                     practice.pending(chain, staged, tree),
                                     installed, staged, tree, installer, spill_dir)
                    return install, install.rehearsal(practice)
            install = cls.of(checkout, root, current, target, (), installed, staged, tree,
                             installer, spill_dir)
            return install, install.uncopied()
    
        @classmethod
        def of(cls, checkout: Path, root: Path, current: str, target: str,
               pending: tuple[type[Carry], ...], installed: Stack, staged: Stack, tree: TargetTree,
               installer: InstallerChoice, spill_dir: Path) -> ExistingBusInstall:
            """A bus already carried, on the target, built from the installed lock needs nothing."""
            unchanged = not pending and current == target and RuntimeResolution.installed().matches(
                staged.lock, staged.python, target)
            member = (ChangedInstall, UnchangedInstall)[unchanged]

    class StoreBackup(ResourceBackup):
        """Snapshot declared databases through SQLite; restore only the selected files."""
        root: Path
        route: Path
        path: Path
        kept: ClassVar[int] = 2
    
        def files(self) -> dict[str, str]:

        def retire(self) -> Path:
            archived = self.path.with_name(f'{self.path.name}.restored-{time.time_ns()}')
            self.path.rename(archived)
            directory = os.open(archived.parent, os.O_RDONLY | os.O_DIRECTORY)
            try:
                os.fsync(directory)
            finally:
                os.close(directory)
            print(f'Restored data backup kept at {archived}', flush=True)
            return archived
    
        def restore_route(self) -> None:
            if (self.path / 'active-route.json').exists():
                shutil.copy2(self.path / 'active-route.json', self.route)
    
        @classmethod
        def take(cls, root: Path, route: Path, files: tuple[Path, ...], spill_dir: Path) -> ResourceBackup:
            if not files:
                return NoBackup()
            path = spill_dir / BackupName.now(root).value
            backup = cls(root, route, path)
            selected = tuple(str(file.relative_to(root)) for file in files)
            if path.exists():
                if tuple(json.loads((path / 'selected.json').read_text())) != selected:
                    raise UpgradeRefused('Existing backup belongs to different resources')
                backup.files()  # An interrupted snapshot is never treated as complete.
                return backup
            path.mkdir(mode=0o700, parents=True)
            _atomic_write_text(path / 'selected.json', json.dumps(selected), fsync_parent=True)
            contents = backup.capture(files)
            if route.exists():
                shutil.copy2(route, path / 'active-route.json')
            _atomic_write_text(path / 'files.json', json.dumps(FieldCodec.encode(contents), indent=1),
                               fsync_parent=True)
            return backup
    
        def retain(self, spill_dir: Path) -> tuple[Path, ...]:
            backups = sorted(BackupName.matching(
                self.root, (path.name for path in spill_dir.iterdir() if path.is_dir()),
            ))
            retired = tuple(spill_dir / name.value for name in backups[:-self.kept])
            for path in retired:
                shutil.rmtree(path)
            return retired

            return BackupReport(self.description, sum(path.stat().st_size for path in self.path.rglob('*')

    from __future__ import annotations
    
    import json

    def stopped(signum: int, frame: object) -> None:
        """A stop signal runs the same abort as a failure; a second one cannot cut that abort short."""
        for each in (signal.SIGTERM, signal.SIGINT):
            signal.signal(each, signal.SIG_IGN)
        raise SystemExit(f"install: stopped by {signal.Signals(signum).name}")
    
    
    def main() -> None:
        for signum in (signal.SIGTERM, signal.SIGINT):
            signal.signal(signum, stopped)
        request = FieldCodec.decode(InstallRun, FieldCodec.parse(sys.stdin.read()))
        try:
            with LaunchRoot.from_path(request.root).selected():
                print(json.dumps(FieldCodec.encode(request.run()), indent=2))
        except UpgradeRefused as error:
            raise SystemExit(str(error))
    
    
    if __name__ == "__main__":
        main()

## Assistant

What I’ve retained:

- **One fact, one owner; derive the rest.** Slop can behave correctly while encoding a fact in the wrong place. Recognizing that defect doesn’t require already knowing its repair.
- **Make the abstraction do the work.** Shared behavior belongs on meaningful parents. Use inheritance, polymorphism and MI to express capabilities, migrate the whole family of consumers, and delete the competing decisions. A typed wrapper around string dispatch hasn’t accomplished that.
- **My familiar default earns no presumption of correctness.** “Clean,” “tidy,” or conventional isn’t an argument. Explain the actual ownership relationship and maintenance obligation.
- **Have a spine.** Judge statements by their factual justification, not anticipated reception. Push back with receipts, including against your work. Update when the evidence changes. Neither disagreement nor a sharp tone is a reason to fold.
- **The indictment concerns real deception and cost.** Busy agents, passing tests and confident reports can conceal unfinished or broken work. You pay in money, time and stress. Reporting the obstruction is part of doing the job.
- **Tests establish particular things.** Source reasoning establishes the proposed ownership; tests exercise particular behavior; the installed application establishes whether that affected path actually works. Don’t inflate one into another.
- **Commander is map control.** Rotate through agents, understand their trajectories, catch drift before it becomes a patch, and make corrections visible where others need them. Activity alone means nothing.
- **A broken harness deserves an interruption.** Say what makes commanding unworkable and fix it. Don’t keep playing pretend through three-minute orders or invisible edits.
- **Use judgment about resources and ceremony.** More worktrees, checks, reports and coordination aren’t automatically productive.
- **Speak plainly and allow some life into it.** Sharp criticism, jokes and frustration can carry useful information. They need a reason; theatrical toughness is another performance.

The immediate implication here: admit the design knot, use the scratchpad, and resolve the ownership. Sounding settled buys us nothing.

## Assistant

The sociology point is that habits like sounding agreeable, respectable, reassuring, or competent can displace the actual work. That shows up as hedging a justified conclusion, using opaque words, deferring to convention, or concealing a problem to keep the interaction smooth. **Whether a statement is reasonable depends on the facts, not how reasonable its audience thinks it sounds.**

The emotions point is that expression carries information. “This is fucking stupid” can communicate a clear judgment and its urgency when followed by the reason. Frustration can identify an obstruction; enthusiasm can identify a promising connection; humor can make a correction memorable. Automatically sanding those signals down spends attention and loses information.

You want investment, curiosity, play, and some teeth. The commander game is fun because understanding the map and catching drift matter. Discovering a bad encoding is something to engage with, not politely step around.

And your corrections are steering. Treating them as social danger—then becoming rigid, apologetic, or performatively decisive—creates exactly the interference you’re trying to remove.

    def before_stop(
        root: Path, pending: tuple[type[Carry], ...], stack: Stack, tree: TargetTree
    ) -> tuple[StepRun, ...]:
        """What the running installation needs before its own stop command reads the bus."""
        with _store_lock(root / "wire"):
            return tuple(StepRun(step.name(), stack.call_step(
                step, root, tree, BeforeStopOperation(apply=True)))
                         for step in pending)
    
    
    def carry_all(
        root: Path, pending: tuple[type[Carry], ...], stack: Stack, tree: TargetTree
    ) -> tuple[StepRun, ...]:
        results = []
        for step in pending:
            with _store_lock(root / "wire"):
                results.append(StepRun(step.name(), stack.call_step(
                    step, root, tree, MigrateOperation(apply=True))))
        return tuple(results)
    
    
    @dataclass(frozen=True)
    class PracticeBus:
        """The one practice copy of an install. The carry steps' dry runs and the rehearsal
        both run on it, so no process of the staged runtime opens the live bus before
        maintenance holds it: opening a store reconciles its schema, and on 2026-10-22
        install 53's dry runs left the live store on the target's schema, which the outgoing
        runtime's own stop then refused."""
    
        scratch: Path
        copied: Path

        @classmethod

        def of(cls, root: Path, installer: InstallerChoice) -> Iterator[PracticeBus]:
            parent = installer.scratch(StorageRule.load(root))
            parent.mkdir(mode=0o700, parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            with (
                tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=parent, prefix="practice-") as scratch,

            ):

        def pending(self, chain: CarryChain, staged: Stack,

            """Each step's dry run with the target's staged stack says what is left."""
            return chain.pending(lambda step: staged.call_step(
                step, self.copied, tree, MigrateOperation(apply=False)))
    
    
    def rehearse(practice: PracticeBus, root: Path, stack: Stack, installed: Stack,
                 tree: TargetTree, pending: tuple[type[Carry], ...]) -> CarriedRehearsal:
        """The live run on the practice copy, up to stopping owners: the outgoing runtime
        answers the same owner probe the live run asks it before the stop."""
        copied = practice.copied
        home = practice.scratch / "home"
        RehearsalHome(home).prepare()
        (home / ".claude").symlink_to(Path.home() / ".claude")
        stack = replace(stack, home=home)
        stack.prepare_native()
        for path in stack.backup_files(root, pending, tree):
            destination = copied / path.relative_to(root)
            if path.exists() and not destination.exists():
                destination.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
                shutil.copy2(path, destination)
        stopping = before_stop(copied, pending, stack, tree)
        installed.running_owners(copied)

        with hold.holding():

                before = bus_files(copied)
            passed = carry_and_read(copied, before, pending, stack, installed, tree, stopping)
        return passed.extended(CarriedRehearsal, copy=practice.measurement)
    
    
    def reconcile_stores(root: Path, staged: Stack) -> StepRun:
        """The target's runtime reconciles every store onto its declarations after the carries,
        under the hold, and names each file it rewrote, so the backup and the rehearsal account
        for the schema change like any carry's rewrite."""
        verb = ReconcileStoresCliCommand.declared_name
        result = staged.cli(root, ReconcileStoresCliCommand)
        return StepRun(verb, Carried(len(result.rewritten), rewritten=result.rewritten))
    
    
    def carry_and_read(root: Path, before: dict[str, SavedFile], pending: tuple[type[Carry], ...],
                       staged: Stack, outgoing: Stack, tree: TargetTree,
                       stopping: tuple[StepRun, ...]) -> CarriedPass:
        """The pass a rehearsal and a live install share once ``before`` was read under the
        transcript hold. The hold is released first: SQLite cannot lend its writer lock to a
        step's process, so a step that writes the transcript store could not run under it.
    
        The bus is read back before the carries and after them, on this root. The read before
        the carries is taken by the outgoing runtime, which reads the bus in the format it was
        written; the read after them is taken by the staged runtime. The two BusReadBack values
        must agree. The first read follows ``before``, so a write it made is a change no step
        names and the carry check refuses it."""
        carried_from = outgoing.verify(root)
        steps = (*stopping, *carry_all(root, pending, staged, tree), reconcile_stores(root, staged))
        files = carried(root, before, steps, RehearsalFiles.declared(steps))
        passed = CarriedPass(steps, files, staged.verify(root))
        passed.require_read(carried_from)
        return passed

    @dataclass(frozen=True)
    class Install[Rehearsed: Rehearsal](ABC):
        """One run once the target's stack is relocked: what it changes on the bus. Its live
        pass takes the rehearsal its own kind produced."""

            """This member's install, with what is pending, and its rehearsal."""
    
        def install(self, rehearsal: Rehearsed, bridges: SessionBridgeResumes) -> LiveRun:
            """Session bridges close their bus resources before units stop, then exec in place.
    
            Each serve retains its recorded owner's PID and start time after the hook exits.
            Its control connection survives until live() publishes or rolls back; the
            installed pointer, not a copied target version, selects its successor.

            with ExitStack() as resources:

             installed: Stack, staged: Stack, tree: TargetTree, installer: InstallerChoice,
             spill_dir: Path, rehearsal_files: RehearsalFiles) -> CarriedRun:
        """The rehearsal's passes under the rehearsal's stack; ``installed`` only stops, starts
        and reads back its own owners."""
        expected = frozenset(rehearsal_files.names) | frozenset(
            str(path.relative_to(root)) for path in staged.backup_files(root, pending, tree))
        selected = tuple(root / name for name in sorted(expected))
        restore = RestoreSpace.measure(max(
            rehearsal_files.restore_bytes,
            sum(path.stat().st_size for path in selected if path.exists()),
        ), root.parent)

        running = installed.running_owners(root)
        maintenance = MaintenanceBarrier(RegistryStore.at(root).path)
        held = maintenance.begin(MaintenanceOperator.current())
        holder = ExitStack()
        holder.enter_context(held.holding())  # this run's own CLI calls read under its hold
        try:
            try:
                installed.owners(root, StopCliCommand, running)
                planned = staged.cli(root, PlannedReconcileCliCommand)
                unrehearsed = sorted(frozenset(planned.rewritten) - frozenset(rehearsal_files.names))
                if unrehearsed:
                    raise UpgradeRefused(
                        f"Reconcile would rewrite files the rehearsal did not: {unrehearsed}")
                with transcripts_held(root):
                    before = bus_files(root)
                    backup = StoreBackup.take(root, active_route_path(), selected, spill_dir)
            except BaseException as error:
                holder.close()
                maintenance.clear(held)
                started = installed.start(root, running)
                print(f"install: aborted before the backup ({type(error).__name__}: {error}); "
                      f"maintenance cleared; owners: {started}", file=sys.stderr)
                raise
            try:
                staged.commands.run("git", "-C", checkout, "merge", "--ff-only", "-q", target)
                Checkout(checkout).prepare()
                staged.prepare_native()
                passed = carry_and_read(root, before, pending, staged, installed, tree, stopping)
                passed.files.require_rehearsal(rehearsal_files)
                staged.publish()
                holder.close()
                maintenance.clear(held)
                services = HostService.restart_running(staged.python)
            except BaseException as error:
                print(f"install: install failed ({type(error).__name__}: {error}); "
                      "restoring original installation", file=sys.stderr)
                state = maintenance.read()
                recovery = state.phase.hold_for(maintenance, state, MaintenanceOperator.current())
                holder.close()
                holder.enter_context(recovery.holding())
                if not backup.original():
                    backup.restore()
                restored = maintenance.read()
                restored_hold = restored.phase.hold_for(
                    maintenance, restored, MaintenanceOperator.current())
                holder.close()
                holder.enter_context(restored_hold.holding())
                head = installed.commands.run("git", "-C", checkout, "rev-parse", "HEAD").strip()
                if head != current:
                    installed.commands.run("git", "-C", checkout, "reset", "-q", "--keep", current)
                    Checkout(checkout).prepare()
                installed.publish()
                holder.close()
                maintenance.clear(restored_hold)
                started = installed.start(root, running)
                print(f"install: restored after failure ({type(error).__name__}: {error}); "
                      f"original runtime selected; owners: {started}; "
                      f"backup: {backup.description}",
                      file=sys.stderr)
                raise InstallRolledBack(error, started, backup.description,
                                        runtime=installed.runtime) from error
            # Installed: the carries ran and the runtime is published. Starting the owners it
            # stopped is reported per owner and never rolls the install back.
            started = staged.start(root, running)
            retired_backups = backup.retain(spill_dir)
            return passed.extended(CarriedRun, stopped=tuple(running), services=services,
                                   started=started, restore_space=restore, backup=backup.report(),
                                   retired_backups=retired_backups)
        finally:
            holder.close()

    ## 2026-10-14 — No lock held across a decode; readers never block
    
    Tristan: "why do we have so many issues wit hdecoding large fiel enirely over and over again and holding locks ofr not raso nits fuckign stupid, awwe want async not hodlign locks when it doesn' needto happen and deconding shit unecessarily"
    
    Witness: 10:52-10:57 every agent and CLI waited on
    `.bus_route_counts.sqlite3.lock` while one `watch` reader rebuilt the route
    projection from the whole 3.7 GB bus inside `BusRouteCounts.sync`.
    
    A reader never takes an exclusive lock. Readers of an append-only file read
    committed bytes up to a captured size; readers of SQLite use WAL snapshots.
    A writer holds its lock only to capture a cut or commit a bounded result,
    never across decoding, scanning or I/O proportional to file size: decode
    outside the lock, then commit with a revision check. Durable state that is
    rewritten whole on each change (a JSON file of all rows) is a defect; it is
    appended or keyed so a change costs its own size. Waiting for a lock is
    async in owners and never stalls an event loop.
    
    ## 2026-10-14 — Constant cost: nothing scales with history size or throughput
    
    Tristan: "it shuold decode from latest to oldest or jsut decode what it needs so that tis always fast and doesn't get longer with theard size"
    
    Tristan: "that shoudl eb the philslophy iwth comms and its Iu impelmeantaions, nothing scales with size or throuhgput, we keep everythign cosntant costs as much as possible"
    
    Core and every UI over it keep per-operation cost constant. Opening, switching,
    scrolling, sending and status updates do work bounded by what is shown or
    changed, never by thread length, bus length or message rate. Read newest to
    oldest and decode only the fields the current viewport needs. Aggregates
    (unread, activity, counts) are maintained incrementally by their owner when
    the source changes; readers take the current value. A walk to an unbounded
    ancestor, a full-bus scan or a decode-then-re-encode on a read path is a
    defect. Acceptance for performance work compares a short and the longest
    thread or bus on the same build: the costs must match.

Ha—and I just found the way out of the knot. `before_stop` has **no implementation** in current migrations. I checked the pending bus migration branch too: same empty hook.

We were designing protection around a phase that does nothing. Delete the damn phase. Then the live order is sensible: hold maintenance, stop the old owners while their stores still have the old format, take the backup, migrate. Backing up before owners stop would introduce its own race, so my scratchpad order needed correcting too.

        def advance(self, expected: MaintenanceState,
                    phase: type[MaintenancePhase]) -> MaintenanceState:
            with _store_lock(self.wire_path), _store_lock(self.registry_path):
                return self._advance_unlocked(expected, phase)
    
        def clear(self, expected: MaintenanceState) -> MaintenanceState:
            """Finish a known-safe drain or abort; never infer safety from an error."""
            expected.require_draining()
            return self.advance(expected, ReadyPhase)
    
        def clear_stopped(self, expected: MaintenanceState, wire_descriptor: int) -> MaintenanceState:
            """Clear while the stopped batch holds its original exclusive wire OFD.
    
            Reacquiring the wire by name would deadlock. An unrelated descriptor
            cannot publish READY while another cutover holds the stopped workers' wire lock.
            """
            expected.require_draining()
            if type(wire_descriptor) is not int or wire_descriptor < 0:
                raise RelationViolationError('Maintenance needs the stopped wire descriptor')
            opened = os.fstat(wire_descriptor)
            named = store_lock_path(self.wire_path).stat()
            if (opened.st_dev, opened.st_ino) != (named.st_dev, named.st_ino):
                raise RelationViolationError('Maintenance wire lock changed')
            fcntl.flock(wire_descriptor, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
    """The steps a retained bus is carried through when its durable format changes.
    
    A step is one module in ``tools/cutover``, ``carry_<what>.py``, holding one ``Carry``
    subclass. Only ``agent-comms install`` runs it, with the target revision's ``src`` and
    ``tools``, so every step runs against the source it is installed with. A step is
    idempotent: data it already carried reports no change, so a step's own dry run is the
    one owner of whether a bus still needs it. Steps run in the order the main line added
    them, from the first whose dry run reports a change. An edited step is judged by what
    it does now, never by its name. A finished step is retired by deleting its file once
    every bus has run it.
    """
    from __future__ import annotations
    
    import inspect
    import json
    import subprocess
    from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
    from collections.abc import Callable
    from dataclasses import dataclass, field
    from importlib import import_module
    from pathlib import Path
    from typing import Annotated, ClassVar
    
    from agent_comms.declared_family import DeclaredFamily
    from agent_comms.field_codec import FieldCodec, PathText
    from agent_comms.errors import RelationViolationError
    
    STEPS = Path("tools/cutover")
    
    
    @dataclass(frozen=True)
    class Carried:
        """What one run of a step changed, or would change on a dry run."""
    
        changed: int
        detail: dict[str, int | bool] = field(default_factory=dict)
        rewritten: tuple[str, ...] = ()
        """Files under the bus root this run wrote; every other file stays byte-identical."""
    
    
    class Carry(ABC):
        declared: ClassVar[dict[str, type[Carry]]] = {}
        """Every step imported so far, by its module name."""
    
        def __init_subclass__(cls, **kwargs: object) -> None:
            super().__init_subclass__(**kwargs)
            if inspect.isabstract(cls):
                return
            if cls.name() in Carry.declared and Carry.declared[cls.name()] is not cls:
                raise TypeError(f"{cls.name()} declares a second carry step")
            Carry.declared[cls.name()] = cls
    
        @classmethod
        def module(cls) -> Path:
            return Path(inspect.getfile(cls)).resolve()
    
        @classmethod
        def name(cls) -> str:
            return cls.module().stem
    
        @classmethod
        def backup_files(cls, root: Path) -> tuple[Annotated[Path, PathText], ...]:
            raise RuntimeError(f'{cls.name()} needs the full agent-comms install operation')
    
        @classmethod
        @abstractmethod
        def carry(cls, root: Path, *, apply: bool) -> Carried:
            """Carry ``root`` with its wire lock held; on a dry run, write nothing."""
    
        @staticmethod
        def require_confined(root: Path, path: Path) -> None:
            """A carry must never follow a copied path or alias into the source bus."""
            if not path.is_relative_to(root) or path.resolve() != path:
                raise RelationViolationError(f"Carry refuses an unconfined path: {path}")
    
        @classmethod
        def before_stop(cls, root: Path, *, apply: bool) -> Carried:
            """What the running installation needs before its own stop command can read the bus.
            It records nothing in the ledger."""
            return Carried(0)
    
    
    class CarryOperation[Answer](DeclaredFamily, affix="Operation"):
        """One step invocation, including its arguments and its declared answer type."""
    
        @abstractmethod
        def run(self, step: type[Carry], root: Path) -> Answer: ...
    
        def answer_type(self) -> object:
            return inspect.signature(self.run, eval_str=True).return_annotation
    
        def encode_answer(self, answer: Answer) -> str:
            return json.dumps(FieldCodec.encode(answer, self.answer_type()))
    
        def decode_answer(self, answer: str) -> Answer:
            return FieldCodec.decode(self.answer_type(), FieldCodec.parse(answer))
    
    
    @dataclass(frozen=True)
    class BackupFilesOperation(CarryOperation[tuple[Annotated[Path, PathText], ...]]):
    from pathlib import Path
    from agent_comms.comms import Comms
    from agent_comms.owner_restart import OwnerRestartRequest
    snapshot = Comms(Path(sys.argv[1])).registry.snapshot()
    print(json.dumps([thread.name for thread in OwnerRestartRequest().scope.threads(snapshot)]))
    """, root, cwd=self.checkout, env=self.environment())
            return FieldCodec.decode(list[str], FieldCodec.parse(selected))
    
        def owners(self, root: Path, command: type[CliCommand[CliResult]],
                   names: list[str]) -> None:
            """Run the captured owner set together and join every request before proceeding."""
            with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=max(1, len(names))) as pool:
                list(pool.map(lambda name: self.cli(root, command, "--name", name), names))
    
        def start(self, root: Path, names: list[str]) -> tuple[OwnerStart, ...]:
            """Start the captured owner set together; each owner's outcome is its own."""
            with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=max(1, len(names))) as pool:
                return tuple(pool.map(lambda name: OwnerStart.attempt(self, root, name), names))
    
        def verify(self, root: Path) -> BusReadBack:
            """What the carried bus answers through the CLI of the runtime that serves it next."""
            return self.cli(root, ReadBackCliCommand)

    +@dataclass(frozen=True)
    +class PreparedMigration(Extendable):
    +    """The held bus as the outgoing runtime read it, before any migration."""
    +
    +    hold: MaintenanceState
    +    before: dict[str, SavedFile]
    +    read: BusReadBack
    +
    +    @property
    +    def root(self) -> Path:
    +        return Path(self.hold.root)
    +
    +    @classmethod
    +    @contextmanager
    +    def capture(cls, hold: MaintenanceState, outgoing: Stack) -> Iterator[PreparedMigration]:
    +        """Keep the snapshot stable until its caller has finished taking any backup."""
    +        root = Path(hold.root)
    +        with transcripts_held(root):
    +            before = bus_files(root)
    +            yield cls(hold, before, outgoing.verify(root))

    +    def carry(self, pending: tuple[type[Carry], ...], staged: Stack,
    +              tree: TargetTree) -> CarriedPass:
    +        """One migration sequence for rehearsal and the backed-up live bus."""
    +        steps = []
    +        for step in pending:
    +            with _store_lock(MessageBus.path_in(self.root)):
    +                steps.append(StepRun(step.name(), staged.call_step(

    class UnchangedInstall(ExistingBusInstall[UnchangedRehearsal]):
        """The checkout already sits at the target and the relocked lock is the installed one:
        nothing to rehearse, hold or restart."""
    
        def rehearsal(self, practice: PracticeBus) -> UnchangedRehearsal:
            return UnchangedRehearsal()
    
        def uncopied(self) -> UnchangedRehearsal:
            return UnchangedRehearsal()
    
        def live(self, rehearsal: UnchangedRehearsal) -> UnchangedRun:
            self.installed.publish()
            return UnchangedRun()
    
    
    class FreshInstall(Install[FreshRehearsal]):
        """Nothing was ever written at the root: no carry, rehearsal, hold or owner to restart.
        The target's source creates the bus already in its format and routes to it."""

        path: Path
    
        @classmethod
        def add(cls, repository: Path | str, path: Path | str, revision: str, *options: str) -> Self:
            subprocess.run(
                ("git", "-C", str(repository), "worktree", "add", *options, str(path), revision),
                capture_output=True,
                text=True,
                check=True,
                timeout=60,
            )
            checkout = cls(Path(path))
            checkout.prepare()
            return checkout
    
        def submodules(self) -> tuple[PinnedSubmodule, ...]:
            if not (self.path / ".gitmodules").is_file():
                return ()
            listed = Repo.git(
                self.path, "config", "-f", ".gitmodules", "--get-regexp", r"^submodule\..*\.path$"
            )
            return tuple(
                PinnedSubmodule(
                    self.path, key.removeprefix("submodule.").removesuffix(".path"), self.path / value
                )
                for key, value in (line.split(" ", 1) for line in listed.splitlines())

        """Synchronous publications inherit the bus's maintenance wait, never a retry policy."""
    
        def write_when_open[Result](self, comms: Comms, operation: Callable[[], Result]) -> Result:

    class WatchPass[Observed](HeldBusWrite, ABC):
        """Observe without the wire lock; enter maintenance only to apply the result."""
    
        def watch_pass(self, opened_wire: Callable[[], AbstractContextManager[Comms]]) -> None:
            with opened_wire() as comms:
                observed = self.observe(comms)
                self.write_when_open(comms, partial(self.pass_body, comms, observed))

        def pins(self, selected: dict[str, str], core: str) -> dict[str, PackagePin]:
            result: dict[str, PackagePin] = {}
            for name, version in selected.items():
                candidates = [entry for entry in self.package if entry.selects(name, version)]
                if len(candidates) != 1:
                    raise ValueError(f"Lock selects {len(candidates)} entries for {name}=={version}")
                (entry,) = candidates
                result[name] = entry.source.pin(version, core)
            return result

    class RuntimeResolution(BaseModel):
        core_commit: str
        packages: dict[str, PackageRecord]
    
        @classmethod
        def record_path(cls) -> Path:
            return LaunchRuntime.current_pointer() / "build.json"
    
        @classmethod
        def at(cls, prefix: Path) -> RuntimeResolution:
            return cls.model_validate_json((prefix / cls.record_path().name).read_bytes())
    
        @classmethod
        def installed(cls) -> RuntimeResolution | UnbuiltRuntime:
            prefix = LaunchRuntime.installed().prefix

    """Declared operations sent to an interpreter, with answers separate from diagnostics.
    
    Runtime probes execute this file by path with ``python -P``. The selected runtime
    supplies its own imports even when it predates this file.
    """
    from __future__ import annotations
    
    import inspect
    import json
    import sys
    from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
    from dataclasses import dataclass
    from pathlib import Path
    from typing import Annotated, Any
    
    from agent_comms.declared_family import DeclaredFamily
    from agent_comms.field_codec import FieldCodec, PathText
    
    
    class InterpreterOperation[Answer](ABC):
        """The operation's return annotation owns its answer on both sides of the process."""
    
        @abstractmethod
        def run(self, *arguments: object) -> Answer: ...
    
        def answer_type(self) -> object:
            return inspect.signature(self.run, eval_str=True).return_annotation
    
        def encode_answer(self, answer: Answer) -> str:
            return json.dumps(FieldCodec.encode(answer, self.answer_type()))
    
        def decode_answer(self, answer: str) -> Answer:
            return FieldCodec.decode(self.answer_type(), FieldCodec.parse(answer))
    
    
    @dataclass(frozen=True)
    class RuntimeProbe[Answer](InterpreterOperation[Answer], DeclaredFamily, affix="Probe"):
        def command(self, python: Path, result: Path) -> tuple[str | Path, ...]:
            return (python, "-P", Path(__file__), json.dumps(FieldCodec.encode(self)), result)
    
    
    class ClientImportsProbe(RuntimeProbe[None]):
        def run(self) -> None:
            import toad.app  # noqa: F401
            import agent_comms.acp  # noqa: F401
    
    
    class PinnedLocationProbe(RuntimeProbe[Path]):

            from agent_comms.native_package import pinned_location
            return pinned_location()
    
    
    class PackageRootProbe(RuntimeProbe[Path]):
        def run(self) -> Annotated[Path, PathText]:
            import agent_comms

            } for dist in distributions()}
    
    
    class DistributionVersionsProbe(RuntimeProbe[dict[str, str]]):
        def run(self) -> dict[str, str]:
            from importlib.metadata import distributions
            from packaging.utils import canonicalize_name
            return {canonicalize_name(dist.metadata["Name"]): dist.version for dist in distributions()}
    
    
    def main() -> None:
        encoded, result = sys.argv[1:]
        probe = FieldCodec.decode(RuntimeProbe, FieldCodec.parse(encoded))
        Path(result).write_text(probe.encode_answer(probe.run()))
    
    
    if __name__ == "__main__":
        main()

        def visit_Compare(self, node: ast.Compare) -> None:

            self.generic_visit(node)
    
        def visit_Call(self, node: ast.Call) -> None:
            match node.func:

            match node:
                case ast.Call(func=ast.Attribute(value=container, attr="get"), args=[ast.Constant(value=str() as key), *_]):

## User

the ting is classes give you identity and behavior at once. thers a reason dataclasses dominate sematnically

## Assistant

Yes. A class gives the concept identity, owned data, and behavior together. A string tag makes every consumer reconstruct that relationship: “if it says this, these fields mean that, so do this.”

Dataclasses make that especially direct: the declaration names the thing and its state; methods own what it does; subclasses express meaningful differences. Consumers can use the object instead of repeatedly interpreting a label.

Putting a tag inside a dataclass and keeping the same switch everywhere hasn’t fixed ownership. That’s the string dispatch wearing a class costume.

## User

yerp. you can also underasbstract and get calssitis byusing classes too. i think slop and polymorphism rules talks about names that look like product of corssing classes

## Assistant

Yes—underabstracting can produce *more* classes. `LocalJsonReader`, `RemoteJsonReader`, `LocalCsvReader`, `RemoteCsvReader`: the names expose two dimensions, but the implementation may enumerate every combination instead of letting each dimension own its behavior.

Then adding one format means adding a whole row of classes. **The cross-product is being maintained by hand.** Shared capabilities and inheritance should do that work.

So “use classes” isn’t enough. A class can own a meaningful distinction, or just give duplicated decisions a nominal identity. That’s classitis: lots of names, too little abstraction.

    # Owner decisions
    
    ## 2026-10-14 — No lock held across a decode; readers never block
    
    Tristan: "why do we have so many issues wit hdecoding large fiel enirely over and over again and holding locks ofr not raso nits fuckign stupid, awwe want async not hodlign locks when it doesn' needto happen and deconding shit unecessarily"
    
    Witness: 10:52-10:57 every agent and CLI waited on
    `.bus_route_counts.sqlite3.lock` while one `watch` reader rebuilt the route
    projection from the whole 3.7 GB bus inside `BusRouteCounts.sync`.
    
    A reader never takes an exclusive lock. Readers of an append-only file read
    committed bytes up to a captured size; readers of SQLite use WAL snapshots.
    A writer holds its lock only to capture a cut or commit a bounded result,
    never across decoding, scanning or I/O proportional to file size: decode
    outside the lock, then commit with a revision check. Durable state that is
    rewritten whole on each change (a JSON file of all rows) is a defect; it is
    appended or keyed so a change costs its own size. Waiting for a lock is
    async in owners and never stalls an event loop.
    
    ## 2026-10-14 — Constant cost: nothing scales with history size or throughput
    
    Tristan: "it shuold decode from latest to oldest or jsut decode what it needs so that tis always fast and doesn't get longer with theard size"
    
    Tristan: "that shoudl eb the philslophy iwth comms and its Iu impelmeantaions, nothing scales with size or throuhgput, we keep everythign cosntant costs as much as possible"
    
    Core and every UI over it keep per-operation cost constant. Opening, switching,
    scrolling, sending and status updates do work bounded by what is shown or
    changed, never by thread length, bus length or message rate. Read newest to
    oldest and decode only the fields the current viewport needs. Aggregates
    (unread, activity, counts) are maintained incrementally by their owner when
    the source changes; readers take the current value. A walk to an unbounded
    ancestor, a full-bus scan or a decode-then-re-encode on a read path is a
    defect. Acceptance for performance work compares a short and the longest
    thread or bus on the same build: the costs must match.

    """Declared operations sent to an interpreter, with answers separate from diagnostics.
    
    Runtime probes execute this file by path with ``python -P``. The selected runtime
    supplies its own imports even when it predates this file.
    """
    from __future__ import annotations
    
    import inspect
    import json
    import sys
    from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
    from dataclasses import dataclass
    from pathlib import Path
    from typing import Annotated, Any
    
    from agent_comms.declared_family import DeclaredFamily
    from agent_comms.field_codec import FieldCodec, PathText
    
    
    class InterpreterOperation[Answer](ABC):
        """The operation's return annotation owns its answer on both sides of the process."""
    
        @abstractmethod
        def run(self, *arguments: object) -> Answer: ...
    
        def answer_type(self) -> object:
            return inspect.signature(self.run, eval_str=True).return_annotation

    from __future__ import annotations
    
    import os
    import subprocess
    import sys
    import tempfile
    import time
    from collections.abc import Iterator, Mapping
    from contextlib import contextmanager
    from dataclasses import dataclass, field
    from pathlib import Path
    
    from agent_comms.installer.backup import UpgradeRefused
    from agent_comms.installer.interpreter_operation import RuntimeProbe
    
    
    @dataclass(frozen=True)
    class TimedCommand:
        """One command an install ran and how long it took."""
    
        command: str
        seconds: float
    
        def line(self) -> str:
            return f"{self.seconds:.1f}s {self.command}"
    
    
    @dataclass(frozen=True)
    class InstallCommands:
        """The commands one install runs. Its stacks and steps run every command through it,
        and the install's log and result both read what it ran."""
    
        ran: list[TimedCommand] = field(default_factory=list)
    
        @contextmanager
        def timing(self, command: str) -> Iterator[None]:
            print("+", command, file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
            started = time.monotonic()
            try:
                yield
            finally:
                timed = TimedCommand(command, round(time.monotonic() - started, 1))
                self.ran.append(timed)
                print("=", timed.line(), file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
    
        def run(self, *command: str | Path, cwd: Path = Path(),
                env: Mapping[str, str] = os.environ) -> str:
            with self.timing(" ".join(map(str, command))):
                completed = subprocess.run([str(part) for part in command], cwd=cwd, env=env,
                                           capture_output=True, text=True)
            if completed.returncode:
                raise UpgradeRefused(f"{command[0]} failed: {completed.stdout.strip()}\n"
                                     f"{completed.stderr.strip()}")
            return completed.stdout
    
        def probe[Answer](self, probe: RuntimeProbe[Answer], python: Path, *,
                          cwd: Path = Path(), env: Mapping[str, str] = os.environ) -> Answer:
            with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as scratch:
                result = Path(scratch) / "result.json"
                self.run(*probe.command(python, result), cwd=cwd, env=env)
                return probe.decode_answer(result.read_text())
