    from agent_comms.field_codec import boundary_decoder
    from agent_comms.installer.backup import UpgradeRefused
    from agent_comms.launch_runtime import LaunchRuntime
    from agent_comms.locked_store import RegistryFile, RootFile, SQLiteFile
    from agent_comms.registry_store import RegistryStore
    from agent_comms.store_files import SharedLock, _store_lock
    from agent_comms.maintenance_barrier import MaintenanceBarrier
    from agent_comms.storage_rules import StorageRule
    from agent_comms.wire_log import WireLog
    
    
    @dataclass(frozen=True)
    class PracticeMeasurement:
        bytes: int
        seconds: float
    
        @classmethod
        def of(cls, copy: Path, seconds: float, floor: float) -> PracticeMeasurement:
            """Refuse a copy without room for the rehearsal's second copy above the disk floor. The
            free space is what a copy can cost; a fixed byte cap beside it refused a 3.01 GiB bus
            with 29 GiB free and stopped install 45."""
            size = sum(path.stat().st_size for path in copy.rglob("*") if path.is_file())
            if shutil.disk_usage(copy.parent).free < 2 * size + floor:
                raise UpgradeRefused(f"Insufficient free space for rehearsal of {size} copied bytes")
            return cls(size, seconds)
    
    
    @dataclass(frozen=True)
    class RuntimeHome(ABC):
        """A private home a runtime build runs in; its kind declares its runtime link and uv."""
    
        path: Path
    
        @staticmethod
        def uv_path(home: Path) -> Path:
            return home / ".local/state/agent-comms/upgrade-bus/uv"
    
        @property
        @abstractmethod
        def uv(self) -> Path: ...
    
        def prepare(self) -> None:
            source = self.uv
            self.path.mkdir(mode=0o700, parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            uv = self.uv_path(self.path)
            uv.parent.mkdir(mode=0o700, parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            uv.unlink(missing_ok=True)
            uv.symlink_to(source)
            cache = Path(subprocess.run(["npm", "config", "get", "cache"], capture_output=True,
                                        text=True, check=True).stdout.strip())
            if not (self.path / ".npm").exists() and cache.is_dir():
                (self.path / ".npm").symlink_to(cache, target_is_directory=True)
            elif not (self.path / ".npm").exists():
                (self.path / ".npm").mkdir(mode=0o700)
    
    
    class RehearsalHome(RuntimeHome):
        """The live install's rehearsal borrows the installed runtime and the installer's uv,
        both resolved strictly before the home is touched, so a broken installation refuses
        the rehearsal instead of rehearsing on PATH."""
    
        @property
        def uv(self) -> Path:
            return self.uv_path(Path.home()).resolve(strict=True)
    
        def prepare(self) -> None:
            installed = LaunchRuntime.current_pointer()
            selected = installed.resolve(strict=True)
            super().prepare()
            pointer = self.path / installed.relative_to(Path.home())
            pointer.parent.mkdir(mode=0o700, parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            pointer.unlink(missing_ok=True)
            pointer.symlink_to(selected)
    
    
    class TestHome(RuntimeHome):
        """A source checkout's test build: no installed runtime, the uv its caller put on PATH."""
    
        @property
        @boundary_decoder
        def uv(self) -> Path:
            executable = shutil.which("uv")
            if executable is None:
                raise UpgradeRefused("A private test runtime home requires uv on PATH")
            return Path(executable)
    
    
    def _copy_database(source: Path, copy: Path) -> None:
        """Copy one database's committed state through SQLite's backup; its companions never."""
        copy.parent.mkdir(mode=0o700, parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        with (closing(sqlite3.connect(f"file:{source}?mode=ro", uri=True)) as original,
              closing(sqlite3.connect(copy)) as copied):
            original.backup(copied)
        shutil.copymode(source, copy)  # SQLite creates the copy under the umask
    
    
    def _copy_file(source: Path, copy: Path) -> None:
        copy.parent.mkdir(mode=0o700, parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        shutil.copy2(source, copy)
    
    
    @contextmanager
    def practice_copy(root: Path, into: Path) -> Iterator[tuple[Path, PracticeMeasurement]]:
        """Copy the bus as files, so no runtime's code reads it to build the copy: the outgoing
        runtime's bugs cannot block the install of their fix, and the target cannot read a
        format its carries have not run on yet. The copy is the declared owners' files and
        nothing else: every SQLite owner's database copies through SQLite's backup, and its
        -wal, -shm and journal never; the log's and the registry's cut_paths copy together
        under each one's lock; every other declared file byte for byte.
        The maintenance witnesses stay behind: the rehearsal holds its copy itself. Stored
        paths keep naming the live bus, and every step writes only inside the root it is given."""
        floor = StorageRule.load(root).floor_gib * 2**30
        into.parent.mkdir(mode=0o700, parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        if shutil.disk_usage(into.parent).free < floor:
            raise UpgradeRefused("Insufficient free space before building the practice copy")
        started = time.monotonic()
        witnesses = set(MaintenanceBarrier(RegistryFile.path_in(root)).witness_paths)
        log = WireLog(WireLog.path_in(root))
        registry = RegistryStore.at(root)
        files = RootFile.existing_in(root)
        into.mkdir(mode=0o700)
    
        def copy(path: Path) -> None:
            owner = files.get(path, RootFile)
            (_copy_database if issubclass(owner, SQLiteFile) else _copy_file)(
                path, into / path.relative_to(root))
    
        # The log's own file lock, never WireLog.locked(): that checks the index with the
        # target's code, which refuses a bus whose carries have not run yet. Each group is one
        # cut, its paths read under its lock: a writer advancing the log between its copy and
        # its checkpoint's would leave a checkpoint past the end of the copied log, and a turn
        # claimed after the declared files were listed would leave the registry naming a
        # missing turn.
        locked_copies = ((_store_lock(log.path), log), (registry.locked(mode=SharedLock()), registry))
        copied: set[Path] = set()
        for lock, owner in locked_copies:
            with lock:
                for path in owner.cut_paths:
                    if path.exists():
                        copy(path)
                        copied.add(path)
        for path in files.keys() - copied - witnesses:
            copy(path)
        yield into, PracticeMeasurement.of(into, time.monotonic() - started, floor)
    """Run source-checkout tests in a private built runtime.
    
    Usage: python -m agent_comms.installer.test_runtime [--home DIR] PYTEST_ARGS
    The default home is disposable; --home retains the private test build for inspection.
    Neither path publishes a runtime or changes the live installation.
    """
    
    from __future__ import annotations
    
    import argparse
    import tempfile
    from pathlib import Path
    
    from agent_comms.installer.practice import TestHome
    from agent_comms.installer.commands import InstallCommands
    from agent_comms.installer.upgrade import Stack
    from agent_comms.storage_rules import StorageRule
    
    
    def main() -> None:
        scratch = StorageRule().scratch_base
        scratch.mkdir(mode=0o700, parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=scratch, prefix="test-runtime-") as temporary:
            parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, allow_abbrev=False)
            parser.add_argument(
                "--home",
                type=Path,
                default=Path(temporary) / "home",
                help="private runtime home to retain for inspection",
            )
            options, arguments = parser.parse_known_args()
            home = options.home.expanduser().resolve()
            if home == Path.home().resolve():
                parser.error("--home must not name the live home")
            TestHome(home).prepare()
            Stack.build(Path.cwd(), InstallCommands(), home).test(*arguments)
    
    
    if __name__ == "__main__":
        main()

    """Upgrade a retained bus and the checkout that runs it: what ``agent-comms install`` runs.
    
    ``agent-comms install`` checks out the target revision and runs this package from that
    revision's ``src`` (``python -m agent_comms.installer``), so its steps are the
    target's. The target's stack is built into its own runtime, relocked to the latest
    OpenHCSDev mains, and must import Toad and the ACP client. Each carry step's dry run
    on the bus says whether it is pending; each runs with the target's
    ``src`` and ``tools`` (``agent_comms.installer.carry``). Every run first rehearses on a
    copy of the bus: the steps, then ``who``, ``threads`` and ``history`` reads, and
    every file no step names as rewritten must be unchanged by saved-file size,
    nanosecond mtime and inode, and the installed runtime answers the owner probe the live
    run asks before its stop. ``--rehearse`` stops there.
    
    A live run then stops the running agent owners with the installed CLI, backs up only
    files the rehearsal changed, moves the checkout, prepares native Pi, carries the bus,
    reads it back, publishes the built runtime and starts only the owners it stopped. A
    failure after the backup restores the original runtime and data. No saved input is
    replayed: owners start by the normal start path. The installer reports its

    """One install, run from the target revision's own source in a session of its own.
    
    The installed CLI only fetches, resolves the target and checks its tree out; the install
    itself runs that tree's ``src`` (``python -m agent_comms.installer``), so its carries,
    rehearsal and harness setup are the target's, never the outgoing runtime's.
    """
    from __future__ import annotations
    
    import glob
    import json
    import os
    import shutil
    import subprocess
    import sys
    import tempfile
    from dataclasses import dataclass, replace
    from pathlib import Path
    from typing import Annotated, ClassVar, TextIO
    
    import agent_comms.installer
    from agent_comms.bus_publication import AgentOrigin
    from agent_comms.channel_targets import CommsTag
    from agent_comms.cli_commands import InstallCliCommand, InstallResult
    from agent_comms.comms import client_wire
    from agent_comms.field_codec import FieldCodec, Id128Text, PathText
    from agent_comms.installer.backup import StoreBackup, UpgradeRefused
    from agent_comms.installer.commands import InstallCommands
    from agent_comms.installer.upgrade import (
        InstalledUpgrade,
        TargetTree,
        Upgrade,
        upgrade,
    )
    from agent_comms.messages import InfoKind, Message
    from agent_comms.service_sender import ServiceSender
    from agent_comms.storage_rules import StorageRule
    
    
    @dataclass(frozen=True)
    class InstallReport(ServiceSender):
        """Publish the install's own typed result, never an interpretation of its logs."""
    
        sender: ClassVar[str] = "installer"
        root: Path
    
        def post(self, lines: tuple[str, ...]) -> Message:
            with client_wire(self.root) as comms:
                self.register(comms.registry)
                return comms.bus.publisher.publish_ordinary(
                    Message(sender=self.sender, target=CommsTag.channel(),
                            body="\n".join(lines),
                            type=InfoKind), origin=AgentOrigin())
    
        def starting(self, upgrade: Upgrade) -> Message:
            return self.post(("Install starting", *upgrade.lines()))
    
        def finished(self, upgrade: InstalledUpgrade) -> Message:
            return self.post((upgrade.finished, *upgrade.lines()))
    
        def failed(self, error: UpgradeRefused) -> Message:
            return self.post(error.lines())
    
    
    @dataclass(frozen=True)
    class InstallLogs:
        """Each install's diagnostics beside the bus, kept as long as its data backups are."""
    
        root: Path
    
        @property
        def prefix(self) -> str:
            return f".{self.root.name}.installer-"
    
        def minted(self) -> Path:
            """A new install's own directory; older ones past the backups' count are retired."""
            logs = self.root.parent / f"{self.prefix}{Id128Text.mint()}"
            logs.mkdir(mode=0o700)
            self.retire()
            return logs
    
        def retire(self) -> tuple[Path, ...]:
            """The names carry no time, so age is each directory's own modification time."""
            logs = sorted((path for path in self.root.parent.glob(f"{glob.escape(self.prefix)}*")
                           if path.is_dir()), key=lambda path: path.stat().st_mtime)
            retired = tuple(logs[:-StoreBackup.kept])
            for path in retired:
                shutil.rmtree(path)
            return retired
    
    
    @dataclass(frozen=True)
    class InstallRun:
        command: InstallCliCommand
        root: Annotated[Path, PathText]
        scratch: Annotated[Path, PathText]
        target: str
    
        @classmethod
        def start(cls, command: InstallCliCommand, root: Path) -> InstallRun:
            checkout = command.checkout.resolve()
            commands = InstallCommands()
            commands.run("git", "-C", checkout, "fetch", "-q", "origin")
            target = commands.run("git", "-C", checkout, "rev-parse", "--verify",
                         f"{command.to}^{{commit}}").strip()
            parent = command.installer.scratch(StorageRule.load(root))
            parent.mkdir(mode=0o700, parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            scratch = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(dir=parent, prefix="install-"))
            TargetTree(checkout, scratch, target).add()
            # Paths resolve here: the install child runs in the target tree, not the caller's cwd.
            return cls(replace(command, checkout=checkout, project=command.project.resolve(),
                               repos=command.repos.resolved()),
                       root, scratch, target)
    
        def launch(self, output: TextIO) -> int:
            """The install outlives its caller: a new session, its output in files beside the bus.
            Retiring the caller's process group must not cut an install short."""
            tree = TargetTree(self.command.checkout, self.scratch, self.target)
            logs = InstallLogs(self.root).minted()
            result, errors = logs / "result.json", logs / "stderr.log"
            with result.open("xb") as stdout, errors.open("xb") as stderr:
                process = subprocess.Popen(
                    [sys.executable, "-m", agent_comms.installer.__name__], cwd=tree.path,
                    env={**os.environ, "PYTHONPATH": os.pathsep.join(map(str, tree.source_paths()))},
                    stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=stdout, stderr=stderr, start_new_session=True,
                )
            print(f"install: pid {process.pid} runs {self.target[:12]}; diagnostics {errors}",
                  file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
            process.communicate(json.dumps(FieldCodec.encode(self)).encode())
            if process.returncode:
                print(f"install failed ({process.returncode}): {errors.read_text().strip()}",
                      file=sys.stderr)
            else:
                output.write(result.read_text())
            return process.returncode
    
        def run(self) -> Upgrade:
            command = self.command
            return upgrade(command.checkout, self.root, self.target, command.installer,
                           command.rehearse, command.retire, command.spill_dir, self.scratch,
                           self.harnesses, InstallReport(self.root))
    
        def harnesses(self) -> InstallResult:
            with client_wire(self.root) as comms:
                return self.command.apply(comms)
    """The install child: reads its ``InstallRun`` from stdin and prints the report."""
    from __future__ import annotations
    
    import json
    import signal
    import sys
    
    from agent_comms.field_codec import FieldCodec
    from agent_comms.installer.backup import UpgradeRefused
    from agent_comms.installer.launch import InstallRun
    from agent_comms.launch_root import LaunchRoot
    
    
    def stopped(signum: int, frame: object) -> None:
        """A stop signal runs the same abort as a failure; a second one cannot cut that abort short."""
        for each in (signal.SIGTERM, signal.SIGINT):
            signal.signal(each, signal.SIG_IGN)
        raise SystemExit(f"install: stopped by {signal.Signals(signum).name}")
    
    
    def main() -> None:
        for signum in (signal.SIGTERM, signal.SIGINT):
            signal.signal(signum, stopped)
        request = FieldCodec.decode(InstallRun, FieldCodec.parse(sys.stdin.read()))
        try:
            with LaunchRoot.from_path(request.root).selected():
                print(json.dumps(FieldCodec.encode(request.run()), indent=2))
        except UpgradeRefused as error:
            raise SystemExit(str(error))
    
    
    if __name__ == "__main__":
        main()

    async def run(arguments):

        posts, connections = [], set()
        provider_end = asyncio.Event()
    
        async def provider(reader, writer):
            task = asyncio.current_task(); connections.add(task)
            try:
                header = await reader.readuntil(b"\r\n\r\n")
                length = next(int(line.split(b":", 1)[1]) for line in header.split(b"\r\n")
                              if line.lower().startswith(b"content-length:"))
                body = json.loads(await reader.readexactly(length))
                count = len(posts)
                record = {"request": count, "dispatch_received_ns": time.monotonic_ns(),
                          "input_bytes": len(json.dumps(body)), "kind": "delayed_headers" if count == 0 else "blocked_subscriber"}
                posts.append(record)
                assert count < 2, "Unexpected provider retry or input replay"
                if count == 0:
                    await asyncio.sleep(2)
                writer.write(b"HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Type: text/event-stream\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n")
                await writer.drain(); record["headers_written_ns"] = time.monotonic_ns()
                text = "WAIT_NATIVE_OK_" + str(count) + " "
                for index in range(80 if count == 0 else 700):
                    content = text + "native controlled response " * (1 if count == 0 else 32)
                    packet = {"id": "wait-" + str(count), "object": "chat.completion.chunk",
                              "created": int(time.time()), "model": "fixture",
                              "choices": [{"index": 0, "delta": {"role": "assistant", "content": content}, "finish_reason": None}]}
                    writer.write(("data: " + json.dumps(packet) + "\n\n").encode())
                    await writer.drain()
                packet["choices"] = [{"index": 0, "delta": {}, "finish_reason": "stop"}]
                packet["usage"] = {"prompt_tokens": 300, "completion_tokens": 500, "total_tokens": 800}
                writer.write(("data: " + json.dumps(packet) + "\n\ndata: [DONE]\n\n").encode())
                await writer.drain(); record["stream_written_ns"] = time.monotonic_ns()
                if count == 1: provider_end.set()
            finally:
                writer.close(); await writer.wait_closed(); connections.remove(task)
    
        server = await asyncio.start_server(provider, "127.0.0.1", 0)
        port = server.sockets[0].getsockname()[1]
        (config / "models.json").write_text(json.dumps({"providers": {"wait-local": {

    """Merge observation closes the real stored order, without a completion request."""
    from agent_comms.repository_name import RepositoryName
    import subprocess
    
    import pytest
    
    from agent_comms.repo import Repo
    from test_order_progress import git
    
    
    def test_failed_git_is_not_a_negative_ancestry_result(tmp_path):
        with pytest.raises(subprocess.CalledProcessError):
            Repo(checkout=tmp_path / 'missing', github=RepositoryName.from_wire('test/repo')).contains('a' * 40)
    
    
    def test_a_merge_made_after_the_last_fetch_is_fetched_then_answered(tmp_path):
        origin, installed = tmp_path / 'origin', tmp_path / 'installed'
        origin.mkdir()
        git(origin, 'init', '-q', '-b', 'main')
        git(origin, '-c', 'user.name=t', '-c', 'user.email=t@t', 'commit', '-q', '--allow-empty', '-m', 'base')
        git(tmp_path, 'clone', '-q', str(origin), str(installed))
        git(origin, '-c', 'user.name=t', '-c', 'user.email=t@t', 'commit', '-q', '--allow-empty', '-m', 'merged later')
        sha = git(origin, 'rev-parse', 'HEAD')
        repo = Repo(checkout=installed, github=RepositoryName.from_wire('test/repo'))
    
        assert not repo.contains(sha)
        assert repo.contains(sha, 'origin/main')
        assert not repo.contains('b' * 40)

        @classmethod
        def take(cls, root: Path, route: Path, files: tuple[Path, ...], spill_dir: Path) -> ResourceBackup:
            if not files:
                return NoBackup()
            path = spill_dir / BackupName.now(root).value
            backup = cls(root, route, path)
            selected = tuple(str(file.relative_to(root)) for file in files)
            if path.exists():
                if tuple(json.loads((path / 'selected.json').read_text())) != selected:
                    raise UpgradeRefused('Existing backup belongs to different resources')

                return backup

            _atomic_write_text(path / 'selected.json', json.dumps(selected), fsync_parent=True)
            contents = backup.capture(files)
            if route.exists():
                shutil.copy2(route, path / 'active-route.json')
            _atomic_write_text(path / 'files.json', json.dumps(FieldCodec.encode(contents), indent=1),
                               fsync_parent=True)
            return backup
    
        def retain(self, spill_dir: Path) -> tuple[Path, ...]:
            backups = sorted(BackupName.matching(
                self.root, (path.name for path in spill_dir.iterdir() if path.is_dir()),
            ))
            retired = tuple(spill_dir / name.value for name in backups[:-self.kept])
            for path in retired:
                shutil.rmtree(path)
            return retired
    
        def report(self) -> BackupReport:

        @staticmethod

            return (CoordinationStore.digest(path) if CoordinationStore.is_database(path)
                    else hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest())
    
        @staticmethod
        def copy_file(source: str | Path, target: str | Path) -> Path:
            """Copy one store through its SQLite snapshot, never through live WAL bytes."""
            source, target = Path(source), Path(target)
            if CoordinationStore.is_database(source):
                with closing(CoordinationStore.read_snapshot(source)) as reader:
                    with closing(sqlite3.connect(target)) as writer:

            else:

        @classmethod
        def copy_tree(

            """Copy committed files; their owners declare transient names before any stat."""
    
            def transient(directory: str, names: list[str]) -> set[str]:
                omitted: set[str] = set()
                for name in sorted(names):
                    path = Path(directory) / name
                    if name in omitted or path in excluded or LockedStore.is_staging(path):
                        omitted.add(name)

                    if stat.S_ISSOCK(path.lstat().st_mode):
                        omitted.add(name)
                    elif (

                    ):

                        )

            shutil.copytree(

            )
    
        def capture(self, files: tuple[Path, ...]) -> dict[str, str]:
            contents = {}
            for source in files:
                if not source.exists():

                name = str(source.relative_to(self.root))
                target = self.data_root / name
                target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
                self.copy_file(source, target)
                with target.open('rb') as ready:
                    os.fsync(ready.fileno())
                contents[name] = self.digest(target)
                directory = os.open(target.parent, os.O_RDONLY | os.O_DIRECTORY)

                finally:
                    os.close(directory)
            return contents
    
        def original(self) -> bool:
            if not (self.path / 'files.json').exists():
                return False
            saved = self.files()
            for name in json.loads((self.path / 'selected.json').read_text()):
                target = self.root / name
                if name not in saved:
                    if target.exists():
                        return False
                elif not target.exists() or self.digest(target) != saved[name]:
                    return False
            return True
    
        def restore(self) -> None:
            saved = self.files()
            for name in json.loads((self.path / 'selected.json').read_text()):
                target = self.root / name
                if name in saved:
                    descriptor, temporary = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix='.restore-', dir=target.parent)
                    os.close(descriptor)
                    stage = Path(temporary)
                    try:
                        shutil.copy2(self.data_root / name, stage)
                        with stage.open('rb') as ready:
                            os.fsync(ready.fileno())
                        os.replace(stage, target)
                    finally:
                        stage.unlink(missing_ok=True)
                else:
                    target.unlink(missing_ok=True)
                for companion in CoordinationStore.files(target)[1:]:
                    companion.unlink(missing_ok=True)
            directory = os.open(self.root, os.O_RDONLY | os.O_DIRECTORY)
            try:
                os.fsync(directory)
            finally:
                os.close(directory)
            if not self.original():
                raise UpgradeRefused('Selected stores differ after backup restoration')
            self.restore_route()
    
    
    class NoBackup(ResourceBackup):
        """A runtime-only install owns no files, paths or snapshot operations."""
    
        def retain(self, spill_dir: Path) -> tuple[Path, ...]:
            return ()
    
        def original(self) -> bool:
            return True
    
        def restore(self) -> None:
            pass
    
        def report(self) -> BackupReport:
            return BackupReport(self.description, 0)
    
        @property
        def description(self) -> str:
            return 'none'

    """Toad through Core's ACP server to a real native owner: queue, saved history, reattach, restart.
    
    The model is the controlled loopback provider; everything else is the real path.
    """
    
    import asyncio
    import json
    from pathlib import Path
    
    import psutil

    def answered(native, text):
        return text in native.ui.painted(native.ui.conversation.window)
    
    
    async def send_first_input_and_hold_its_reply(native):
        ui, provider = native.ui, native.provider
        provider.hold_next_request()
        await ui.until_agent_ready()
        await ui.write_draft("FIRST_NATIVE_INPUT")
        await ui.press("enter")
        await ui.until(provider.entered.is_set, seconds=30, why="the first input at the provider")
    
    
    async def queue_behind_the_held_turn(native):
        ui, agent = native.ui, native.agent
        await asyncio.wait_for(agent.send_prompt(
            "QUEUED_NATIVE_INPUT", request=QueuePromptRequest("QUEUED_NATIVE_INPUT", True)), 10)
        view = ui.conversation
        await ui.until(lambda: bool(view.submissions.queue_projection.items), seconds=20, why="the queued input")
        queued = [row.input_id for row in view.submissions.queue_projection.items]
        assert len(queued) == 1
        assert "QUEUED_NATIVE_INPUT" in view.query_one(QueueSummary).render().plain
        return queued[0]
    
    
    async def finish_both_turns(native):
        ui, agent = native.ui, native.agent
        native.provider.release()
        await ui.until(lambda: agent.presentation.prompt_in_flight == 0, seconds=25, why="the prompt to finish")
        await ui.until(lambda: not native.executing, seconds=20, why="the owner to finish its turns")
        await ui.step()
        assert len(native.provider.requests) >= 2, "The queued input never reached the provider"
        assert not ui.conversation.submissions.queue_projection.items
        await ui.until(lambda: answered(native, "NATIVE_RESPONSE_2"), seconds=20, why="the second answer on screen")
    
    
    async def test_owner_is_attached_and_navigable(workspace, native_package):
        from toad.navigation_preparation import ThreadNavigationRequest
    
        async with native_session(workspace, native_package) as native:
            owner = native.comms.registry.require("beta")
            assert owner.process_identity is not None and owner.process_alive
            navigation = await asyncio.to_thread(
                ThreadNavigationRequest(native.comms, "beta", native.project, ()).read)
            assert navigation.attachable and navigation.thread.process_alive

            await ui.until(lambda: not native.executing, seconds=20, why="the owner to finish")

        async with native_session(workspace, native_package) as native:
            ui, agent, comms = native.ui, native.agent, native.comms

            assert view.agent.configuration.model.current == "selected-offline/fixture"

            assert agent.queue_attachment is queue

            assert "QUEUED_NATIVE_INPUT" in view.query_one(QueueSummary).render().plain

    """Message journeys through a native session that more than one native test walks."""
    
    from __future__ import annotations
    
    import asyncio
    from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
    
    from agent_comms.channel_targets import ChannelTarget, ThreadTarget
    from agent_comms.input_disposition import InputDispositions
    from toad.conversation_kind import ChannelConversation, DmConversation
    from toad.core import input_events

    from support.textual_steps import refresh_chat
    
    
    def rows_with(chat, predicate):
        return [fragment.message for fragment in chat.message_history.fragments_in_range
                if predicate(fragment.message)]
    
    
    def feedback_of(chat, sent) -> NotificationStatus:
        """The notification status drawn under the one message showing `sent`."""
        shown = [fragment.shown.status for fragment in chat.message_history.fragments_in_range
                 if fragment.message.reference == sent.reference]
        assert len(shown) == 1, (sent.reference, len(shown))
        return shown[0]
    
    
    async def direct_reply_feedback(native, owner_tab: str, *, hold: bool, target: str = "beta",
                                    body: str = "DIRECT_NATIVE_MESSAGE",
                                    reply_prefix: str | None = "NATIVE_RESPONSE_") -> None:
        """Send one direct message and follow it: responding while open, settled while hidden,
        answered exactly once on return, and once again after closing and reopening the tab.
    
        With `hold` the provider's reply waits until the tab is hidden.
        """
        ui, comms, provider = native.ui, native.comms, native.provider
        app, _pilot = ui.textual
        user = comms.messaging.user_identity(str(native.project)).name
        navigation = NavigationContext(app, owner_tab, native.project, user)
        await DirectTarget(target).open(navigation)
        screen = app.selected_session
        await screen.wait_content_ready()
        chat = screen.query_one(CommsChatView)
        assert chat.conversation == DmConversation(ThreadTarget(target))
        assert not rows_with(chat, lambda message: message.body == body)
        if hold:
            provider.hold_next_request()
        await chat.submit_input(input_events.UserInputSubmitted(body))
        if hold:
            await ui.until(provider.entered.is_set, seconds=30, why="the direct message at the provider")
        await ui.until(lambda: rows_with(chat, lambda message: message.body == body), seconds=20,
                       why="the sent message in the chat")
        sent_rows = rows_with(chat, lambda message: message.body == body)
        assert len(sent_rows) == 1
        sent = sent_rows[0]
        assert sent.sender == user and sent.target == target
        await ui.until(lambda: "Responding" in str(feedback_of(chat, sent).title), seconds=20,
                       why="'Responding' under the sent message")
        assert comms.registry.require(target).executing
    
        await ui.select_tab(owner_tab)
        assert app.selected_session is not screen
        provider.release()
        await ui.until(lambda: not comms.registry.require(target).executing, seconds=20,
                       why="the reply turn to finish while the chat is hidden")
        assert app.selected_session is not screen
    
        def replies():
            return rows_with(chat, lambda message: message.sender == target and message.seq > sent.seq
                             and (reply_prefix is None or message.body.startswith(reply_prefix)))
    
        await DirectTarget(target).open(navigation)
        assert app.selected_session is screen, "Returning replaced the open direct-message tab"
        await ui.until(replies, seconds=20, why="the reply in the chat")
        assert len(replies()) == 1
        reply = replies()[0]
        assert reply.target == user and reply.reference != sent.reference
        await ui.until(lambda: "Responded" in str(feedback_of(chat, sent).title), seconds=20,
                       why="'Responded' under the sent message")
        outcomes = await asyncio.to_thread(comms.views.message_notifications, (sent,))
        assert any(item.recipient == target and item.state == "Responded"
                   for item in outcomes[sent.seq, sent.message_id])
        if not hold:
            from agent_comms.input_origin import WireInputOrigin
    
            recipient = comms.registry.require(target)
            native_input = InputDispositions(comms.root / InputDispositions.filename).read().lookup(
                InputDispositions.bus_key(sent, recipient))
            assert native_input.has_started and native_input.matches_owner(recipient.incarnation)
            assert isinstance(native_input.origin, WireInputOrigin)
            assert native_input.origin.reference == sent.reference
    
        await ui.close_tab(screen.id)
        await DirectTarget(target).open(navigation)
        reopened = app.selected_session
        assert reopened is not screen and reopened.id != screen.id
        await reopened.wait_content_ready()
        fresh = reopened.query_one(CommsChatView)
        assert fresh.conversation == DmConversation(ThreadTarget(target))
        await ui.until(lambda: all(
            sum(fragment.message.reference == reference
                for fragment in fresh.message_history.fragments_in_range) == 1
            for reference in (sent.reference, reply.reference)), seconds=20,
            why="the message and its reply once each after reopening")
        await ui.until(lambda: "Responded" in str(feedback_of(fresh, sent).title), seconds=20,
                       why="'Responded' after reopening")
    """How Toad's tests run: app tests get a process and private roots each; coroutine tests just run."""
    
    from __future__ import annotations
    
    import asyncio
    import inspect
    import json
    import os
    from pathlib import Path
    import shutil
    import sys
    
    import pytest
    
    from support.agents import AppAgents
    from support.requirements import Requirement
    from support.roots import ATTEMPT, Roots
    from support.workspace import Workspace
    
    RESULT = "TOAD_TEST_RESULT"
    OPEN_DEFECTS = Path(__file__).with_name("open_defects.toml")
    
    
    def open_defects() -> dict[str, tuple[str, bool]]:
        """Test id -> (why it is expected to fail, whether it only fails some of the time)."""
        import tomllib
    
        return {test: (f"open defect {name} ({entry['owner']}): {entry['defect']}", entry.get("intermittent", False))
                for name, entry in tomllib.loads(OPEN_DEFECTS.read_text()).items() for test in entry["tests"]}
    
    
    def pytest_addoption(parser):
        parser.addoption("--test-timeout", type=float, default=165,
                         help="Wall seconds one app test may take, once (no retries)")
    
    
    @pytest.fixture
    def app_agents(tmp_path) -> AppAgents:
        """Agents of an app built on the test's own directory and never run."""
        return AppAgents.unrun(tmp_path)
    
    
    @pytest.fixture
    def workspace() -> Workspace:
        """A private project and wire; asking for it gives the test its own process."""
        return Workspace(Roots.of_this_process())
    
    
    for _requirement in Requirement.__subclasses__():
        globals()[_requirement.fixture] = pytest.fixture(name=_requirement.fixture)(_requirement.require)
    
    
    class OwnProcessTest(pytest.Item):
        """Runs one collected test in a fresh interpreter that owns disposable roots.
    
        The app keeps process-wide state (render workers, the comms route, settings
        paths, frozen heap), so two app tests never share an interpreter.
        """
    
        def runtest(self):
            from agent_comms.child_process import BoundedRun
            from support.processes import stop_test_children
    
            roots = Roots.create()
            result = roots.attempt / "result.jsonl"
            env = roots.environment(dict(os.environ)) | {RESULT: str(result)}
            command = (sys.executable, "-m", "pytest", self.nodeid, "-p", "no:cacheprovider",
                       "-q", "--no-header", "--tb=short", "--color=no")
    
            async def run():
                try:
                    return await BoundedRun.run(command, timeout=self.config.getoption("--test-timeout"),
                                                cwd=self.config.rootpath, env=env)
                finally:
                    # Closing the app leaves owners and helpers running; stop the ones this test started.
                    await stop_test_children(str(roots.attempt))
    
            child = asyncio.run(run())
            reports = [json.loads(line) for line in result.read_text().splitlines()] if result.exists() else []
            output = child.stdout.decode(errors="replace")[-12000:] + child.stderr.decode(errors="replace")[-4000:]
            failed = not child.outcome.successful or not reports
            if (defect := open_defects().get(self.nodeid)) is not None:
                reason, intermittent = defect
                shutil.rmtree(roots.attempt, ignore_errors=True)
                if failed:
                    pytest.xfail(reason)
                if intermittent:
                    return
                pytest.fail(f"{self.nodeid} passes; remove it from tests/open_defects.toml", pytrace=False)
            if failed:
                pytest.fail(f"{child.outcome!r}\n{output}\nRoots kept: {roots.attempt}", pytrace=False)
            shutil.rmtree(roots.attempt)
            for report in reports:
                if report["outcome"] == "skipped":
                    pytest.skip(report["reason"])
    
        def reportinfo(self):
            return self.path, None, self.name
    
    
    def pytest_collection_modifyitems(config, items):
        if ATTEMPT in os.environ:
            return  # This is the process a test was given.
        defects = open_defects()
        unknown = set(defects) - {item.nodeid for item in items}
        if unknown and not config.args_source == config.ArgsSource.ARGS:
            raise pytest.UsageError(f"tests/open_defects.toml names tests that do not exist: {sorted(unknown)}")
        for item in items:
            if item.nodeid in defects and "workspace" not in getattr(item, "fixturenames", ()):
                reason, intermittent = defects[item.nodeid]
    def _first_wins(started):
        """Construct with the arguments bound here taking precedence over the caller's."""
        def construct(**given):
            return started.func(**{**given, **started.keywords})
        return construct
    
    
    @asynccontextmanager
    async def native_session(workspace, package: Path, *, provider: ControlledProvider | None = None,
                             settings: dict | None = None, prepare=None, size: tuple[int, int] = (160, 44),
                             application: type | None = None, attached: bool = True):
        """Start Toad on a declared native thread ``beta`` whose model is the controlled provider.
    
        `prepare(comms, project, provider)` may arrange wire state before the app starts.
        `attached=False` expects the session to settle without a connection.
        """
    
        provider = provider or ControlledProvider()
        with provider.serving() as base_url:
            comms = start_private_native_wire(workspace.roots.wire, package)
            configure_provider(base_url, settings=settings)
            comms.registry.declare(comms.registry.new_thread("beta", frozenset({"team"}), str(workspace.project),
                                          model=MODEL, thinking_level="off"))
            try:
                if prepare is not None:
                    await prepare(comms, workspace.project, provider)
                async with attached_app(workspace, comms, "beta", size=size, application=application,
                                        attached=attached) as (ui, agent):
                    yield NativeSession(ui, agent, comms, provider, workspace.project)
                    assert not provider.failures, provider.failures
            except BaseException as error:
                if provider.failures:
                    error.add_note(f"Controlled provider failures: {provider.failures}")
                raise
            finally:
                provider.release()
    
    
    def without_provider(models: str = "test/model") -> None:
        """Configure native owners with a model nothing serves, for tests that must never ask one."""
        os.environ.update(AGENT_COMMS_AGENT_BIN="pi", AGENT_COMMS_AGENT_ARGS="", AGENT_COMMS_AGENT_MODELS=models)
    
    
    def owner_server(comms, package: Path, *, provider: str = "openrouter", model: str = "fake"):
        """Core's ACP server object in this process, able to start native owners on the private wire."""
        from agent_comms.acp import CommsAgent
    
        return CommsAgent(
            comms, agent_bin="pi", agent_args=["--provider", provider, "--model", model],

    """A private project with its own comms wire, and Toad started on it."""
    
    from __future__ import annotations
    
    from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
    from functools import cached_property
    import os
    from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
    
    from support.agents import AppAgents
    from support.roots import Roots
    from support.ui import TextualUi
    
    if TYPE_CHECKING:
        from agent_comms.comms import Comms
        from toad.agent_schema import AgentDefinition
    
    
    class Workspace:
        """Everything a test of the running app starts from."""
    
        def __init__(self, roots: Roots) -> None:
            from agent_comms.launch_root import LaunchRoot
    
            self.roots = roots
            self.project = roots.project
            self.project.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            LaunchRoot.from_path(roots.wire).install()
    
        @cached_property
        def comms(self) -> Comms:
            """The test's own wire, as Core serves it."""
            from agent_comms.comms import wire
    
            return wire(self.roots.wire)
    
        @property
        def viewer(self) -> str:
            """The name the user of this project sends as."""
            return self.comms.messaging.user_identity(str(self.project)).name
    
        def thread(self, name: str, *tags: str, running: bool = False, title: str | None = None):
            """Declare a thread on the wire; a running thread is owned by this process."""
            from agent_comms.child_process import NoProcess, ProcessIdentity
            from agent_comms.thread_text import ThreadText
    
            identity = ProcessIdentity.capture(os.getpid()) if running else NoProcess()
            self.comms.registry.declare(self.comms.registry.new_thread(
                name, frozenset(tags), str(self.project), title=ThreadText.external(title), process_identity=identity))
            return self.comms.registry.require(name)
    
        def child_processes(self, marker: str) -> list:
            """This test's live child processes whose command line mentions `marker`."""
            import psutil
    
            found = []
            for process in psutil.Process().children(recursive=True):
                try:
                    if process.status() != psutil.STATUS_ZOMBIE and any(marker in part for part in process.cmdline()):
                        found.append(process)
                except psutil.NoSuchProcess:
                    continue
            return found
    
        def received(self) -> list[dict]:
            """Everything the scripted agent recorded, oldest first (see ``support/peers/base.py``)."""
            import json
    
            record = self.project / "peer-received.jsonl"
            return [json.loads(line) for line in record.read_text().splitlines()] if record.exists() else []
    
        def release(self, name: str) -> None:
            """Let the scripted agent past its ``{"wait": name}`` step."""
            (self.project / f"released-{name}").touch()
    
        def steps_done(self) -> list[dict]:
            """The steps the scripted agent has finished, in order."""
            return [fact["done"] for fact in self.received() if "done" in fact]
    
        def prompts_received(self) -> list[str]:
            return [fact["prompt"] for fact in self.received() if "prompt" in fact]
    
        @cached_property
        def agents(self) -> AppAgents:
            return AppAgents.unrun(self.project)
    
        @asynccontextmanager
        async def app(self, *, size: tuple[int, int] = (120, 40), agent: AgentDefinition | None = None,
                      application: type | None = None, session: bool = True, resume: str | None = None):
            """Start Toad headless on this project; yields once its first session is shown.
    
            Toad itself starts with no tab open unless the launch names a session
            to resume (``resume``); ``session=False`` yields what it started with.
            """
            from toad.app import ToadApp
    
            launch = {} if resume is None else {"agent_session_id": resume}
            app = (application or ToadApp)(agent_data=agent, project_dir=str(self.project), **launch)
            async with app.run_test(size=size) as pilot:
                ui = TextualUi(app, pilot)
                if session:
                    if not app.session_navigation.members:
                        await ui.new_session()
                    await app.selected_session.wait_content_ready()
                await ui.step()
                yield ui
                if (error := ui.failure()) is not None:
                    raise error

    """Select the interpreter running this module as the published runtime.
    
    The installer runs ``python -m agent_comms.installer.publication`` with the runtime
    it built: console launchers and harness links move to it, then ``current`` does.
    """
    from __future__ import annotations
    
    import sys
    from dataclasses import dataclass
    from importlib.metadata import distribution
    from pathlib import Path
    from typing import Annotated
    
    import agent_comms
    from agent_comms.field_codec import PathText
    from agent_comms.harness_install import Harness, replace_link
    from agent_comms.installer.runtime_resolution import (
        ConsoleScriptPackage,
        RuntimePackage,
        RuntimeResolution,
    )
    from agent_comms.launch_runtime import LaunchRuntime
    
    
    @dataclass(frozen=True)
    class RuntimePublication:
        runtime: Annotated[Path, PathText]
        links: dict[Annotated[Path, PathText], Annotated[Path, PathText]]
    
        @classmethod
        def installed(cls) -> RuntimePublication:
            binary = Path(sys.executable).parent.resolve(strict=True)
            if not Path(agent_comms.__file__).resolve().is_relative_to(binary.parent):
                raise ValueError("Editable Core cannot publish a runtime; build the selected source")
            RuntimeResolution.at(binary.parent)
            packages = tuple(
                member.distribution for member in RuntimePackage.members_with(ConsoleScriptPackage))
            links = {
                Path.home() / '.local/bin' / entry.name: binary / entry.name
                for package in packages
                for entry in distribution(package).entry_points.select(group='console_scripts')
            }
            links |= Harness.published_links(Path.home())
            for link, target in links.items():
                target.stat()
                if link.exists() and not link.is_symlink():
                    raise FileExistsError(f'Publication cannot replace a regular file: {link}')
            return cls(binary.parent, links)
    
        def published_target(self, current: Path, target: Path) -> Path:
            """Runtime-owned links follow current; user-owned paths remain where declared."""
            if target.is_relative_to(self.runtime):
                return current / target.relative_to(self.runtime)
            return target
    
        def publish_links(self) -> None:
            """Refresh the declared installation, including an already-current runtime."""
            current = LaunchRuntime.current_pointer()
            selected = self.runtime.resolve(strict=True)
            RuntimeResolution.at(selected)

    def upgrade(checkout: Path, root: Path, target: str, installer: InstallerChoice, rehearse_only: bool,
                retire: bool, spill_dir: Path, scratch: Path,
                harnesses: Callable[[], InstallResult], report: InstallReport) -> Upgrade:
        """``scratch`` holds the target's worktree the launcher runs this source from; this
        run owns it and removes it. A live run ends by registering the ``harnesses``."""
        commands = InstallCommands()
        current = commands.run("git", "-C", checkout, "rev-parse", "HEAD").strip()
        tree = TargetTree(checkout, scratch, target)
        try:
            ancestry = ["git", "-C", str(checkout), "merge-base", "--is-ancestor", current, target]
            with commands.timing(" ".join(ancestry)):
                answer = subprocess.run(ancestry)
            if answer.returncode:
                raise UpgradeRefused(f"{target[:12]} does not follow the checkout's {current[:12]}")
            if commands.run("git", "-C", checkout, "status", "--porcelain",
                            "--untracked-files=no").strip():
                raise UpgradeRefused("The checkout has local changes")
            try:
                chain = CarryChain.at(tree.path)
            except ValueError as error:
                raise UpgradeRefused(str(error)) from None
            member = Install.member(root, retire)
            installed = Stack(checkout, commands)
            installed.require_uv()
            if not installed.python.exists():
                raise UpgradeRefused(f"No installed stack at {installed.python}")
            staged = Stack.build(tree.path, commands)
            install, rehearsal = member.rehearsed(checkout, root, current, target, chain,
                                                  installed, staged, tree, installer, spill_dir)
            names = tuple(step.name() for step in install.pending)
            if rehearse_only:
                return RehearsedUpgrade(current, target, root, names, rehearsal,
                                        commands=tuple(commands.ran))
            install.announce(report)

    class Stack:
        """One built installation and the source checkout containing its install tools."""
    
        checkout: Path
        commands: InstallCommands
        home: Path = HOME
        runtime: LaunchRuntime = field(default_factory=LaunchRuntime.installed)
    
        @property
        def python(self) -> Path:
            return self.runtime.interpreter
    
        @property
        def lock(self) -> Path:
            return self.checkout / "stack/uv.lock"
    
        @property
        def uv(self) -> Path:
            """The uv the installer runs, kept in the installer's own state."""
            return RuntimeHome.uv_path(self.home)
    
        def require_uv(self) -> None:
            if not os.access(self.uv, os.X_OK):
                raise UpgradeRefused(f"No uv executable at {self.uv}; the installer runs only that uv")
    
        @classmethod
        def build(cls, checkout: Path, commands: InstallCommands, home: Path = HOME) -> Stack:
            """Resolve current mains once, then build or reuse their immutable installation."""
            Checkout(checkout).prepare()
            source = cls(checkout, commands, home, runtime=LaunchRuntime.running())
            source.require_uv()
            commands.run(source.uv, "lock", "--project", "stack", "--upgrade", "--python", "3.14",
                         cwd=checkout)
            core = commands.run("git", "-C", checkout, "rev-parse", "HEAD").strip()
            resolution = hashlib.sha256(source.lock.read_bytes()).hexdigest()[:16]
            prefix = home / ".local/share/agent-comms/runtimes" / f"core-{core[:9]}-lock-{resolution}"
            built = replace(source, runtime=LaunchRuntime(prefix / "bin/python"))
            if prefix.exists():
                if not RuntimeResolution.at(prefix).matches(source.lock, built.python, core, commands):
                    raise UpgradeRefused("Existing built runtime differs from its resolved inputs")
                return built
            prefix.parent.mkdir(mode=0o700, parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            prefix.mkdir(mode=0o700)
            try:
                commands.run(source.uv, "sync", "--project", "stack", "--locked", "--python", "3.14",
                             "--no-editable", cwd=checkout,
                             env={**built.environment(), "UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT": str(prefix)})
                built.install_native()
                RuntimeResolution.capture(built.python, core, commands).save(prefix)
                built.imports()
            except BaseException:
                shutil.rmtree(prefix)
                raise
            return built

    Each harness declares where it reads skills and what it needs to reach the bus;
    runtime publication links and configures it, and install registers its bus threads.

    from __future__ import annotations

    def replace_link(link: Path, target: Path) -> None:
        """Point `link` at `target` atomically; a regular file there is someone's own and is refused."""
        if link.exists() and not link.is_symlink():
            raise FileExistsError(f'Install cannot replace a regular file: {link}')
        link.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        temporary = link.with_name(f'.{link.name}.{uuid.uuid4().hex}')
        try:
            temporary.symlink_to(target)
            os.replace(temporary, link)
            directory = os.open(link.parent, os.O_RDONLY | os.O_DIRECTORY | os.O_NOFOLLOW)
            try:
                os.fsync(directory)
            finally:
                os.close(directory)
        finally:
            temporary.unlink(missing_ok=True)
    
    
    def merge_json(path: Path, merge) -> None:
        """Rewrite a harness's JSON config through its owner, keeping unrelated settings."""
        document = json.loads(path.read_text()) if path.exists() else {}
        merge(document)
        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        path.write_text(json.dumps(document, indent=2) + '\n')
    
    
    @dataclass(frozen=True)
    class Harness(DeclaredFamily, affix="Harness"):
        home: Path
    
        executable: ClassVar[str]
        skills_dir: ClassVar[str]
        # External threads install registers for this harness; a harness that registers itself has none.
        bus_threads: ClassVar[tuple[str, ...]] = ()
    
        @classmethod
        def present(cls, home: Path) -> tuple[Harness, ...]:
            return tuple(member(home) for member in cls.members_with(cls) if shutil.which(member.executable))
    
        @staticmethod
        def bin(name: str) -> Path:
            return Path(sys.executable).parent / name
    
        def links(self) -> dict[Path, Path]:
            """Every packaged skill, linked where this harness looks for skills."""
            skills = Path(str(files('agent_comms') / 'skills'))
            return {self.home / self.skills_dir / skill.name: skill for skill in skills.iterdir() if skill.is_dir()}
    
        @abstractmethod
        def configure(self) -> tuple[Path, ...]:
            """Write this harness's own config in its own format; returns the files written."""
    
        def register(self, comms: Comms, project: Path) -> tuple[str, ...]:
            """Declare this harness's bus threads; publication already linked and configured it."""
            names = comms.registry.snapshot()
            registered = tuple(name for name in self.bus_threads if not names.taken(name))
            for name in registered:
                comms.registry.declare(comms.registry.new_thread(name=name, tags=frozenset(), worktree=str(project),
                                                                    execution=ExternalThreadExecution))
            return registered
    
        @classmethod
        def published_links(cls, home: Path) -> dict[Path, Path]:
            """Refresh present harnesses and retain links of previously installed harnesses."""
            available = {type(harness) for harness in cls.present(home)}
            return {link: target for member in cls.members_with(cls)
                    for link, target in member(home).links().items()
                    if member in available or link.is_symlink()}

        def configure(self) -> tuple[Path, ...]:
            settings = self.home / '.claude/settings.json'
    
            def reconcile_hooks(document: dict) -> None:
                events = document.setdefault('hooks', {})
                for event, entries in events.items():
                    events[event] = [
                        entry for entry in entries if not ClaudeHookProgram.owns_entry(entry)
                    ]
                for program in ClaudeHookProgram.members():
                    for event in program.events:
                        events.setdefault(event, []).append(program.entry())
            merge_json(settings, reconcile_hooks)
            return (settings,)

    """Durable, default-off wire-root maintenance phase.
    
    A one-time upgrade from code lacking this gate must drain those original workers
    before it can rely on the phase. Subsequent cutovers set Draining before
    fleet drain and clear it only after known-safe publication or abort. The enabled
    witness is never removed: a lost/corrupt state denies instead of returning OFF.
    """
    
    from __future__ import annotations
    
    import fcntl
    import json
    import os

    from .store_files import (

    )
    
    
    class MaintenanceHeldError(RelationViolationError, ToolRefusedError):
        """The bus is in maintenance: its readers close and wait for READY."""
    
    
    class MaintenanceNotHeldError(RelationViolationError):
        """Work only this root's maintenance holder may do, attempted by a process that does not
        hold it."""
    
        @classmethod
        def unheld(cls, change: str) -> MaintenanceNotHeldError:
            return cls(f"{change} needs this root's maintenance hold, and no install holds it: "
                       "only agent-comms install changes it")
    
    
    class HeldSends:
        @staticmethod
        @contextmanager
        def open(delegate, *args):
            yield HeldSend()
    
        @staticmethod
        def pending() -> bool: return True
    
        @staticmethod
        def require_open():
            raise MaintenanceHeldError("Maintenance holds ingress: the bus is under maintenance")
    
    
    class GrantedSends:
        @staticmethod
        @contextmanager
        def open(delegate, *args):
            if delegate is None:
                yield GrantedSend()
            else:
                with delegate(*args) as outcome:
                    yield outcome
    
        @staticmethod
        def pending() -> bool: return False
    
        @staticmethod
        def require_open():
            pass
    
    
    class MaintenancePhase(DeclaredFamily, LifecycleState, affix="Phase"):
        new_sends = running_sends = HeldSends
    
        @classmethod
        def holder_dead(cls, state: MaintenanceState) -> bool:
            return not state.operator.alive()
    
        @classmethod
        def hold_for(cls, barrier: MaintenanceBarrier, state: MaintenanceStatus,
                     operator: MaintenanceOperator) -> MaintenanceState:
            raise MaintenanceHeldError('Another maintenance operation holds this root')
    
        @classmethod
        def require_held_by(cls, state: MaintenanceState, holder: str, change: str) -> None:
            if holder != state.nonce:
                raise MaintenanceNotHeldError(
                    f"{change} needs this root's maintenance hold; another process holds it")
    
        @classmethod
        def send_new(cls, delegate, *args):
            return cls.new_sends.open(delegate, *args)
    
        @classmethod
        def send_running(cls, delegate, *args):
            return cls.running_sends.open(delegate, *args)
    
        @classmethod
        def hold_restore(cls, barrier: MaintenanceBarrier, operator: MaintenanceOperator,
                         drained: Callable[[], None]) -> None:
            """A failed upgrade's restore runs under the hold it began, still in place here."""
    
    
    class DrainingPhase(MaintenancePhase):
        running_sends = GrantedSends
    
        @classmethod
        def hold_for(cls, barrier: MaintenanceBarrier, state: MaintenanceState,
                     operator: MaintenanceOperator) -> MaintenanceState:
            if state.operator != operator:
                raise MaintenanceHeldError('Another maintenance operation holds this root')
            return state
    
        @classmethod
        def successors(cls):
            # A wire-compatible cutover clears directly; format migrations may
            # proceed through Paused and Installing before they become READY.
            return (PausedPhase, ReadyPhase)
    
    
    class PausedPhase(MaintenancePhase):
        @classmethod
        def successors(cls):
            return (InstallingPhase,)
    
    
    class InstallingPhase(MaintenancePhase):
        @classmethod
        def successors(cls):
            return (ReadyPhase,)
    
    
    class ReadyPhase(MaintenancePhase):
        new_sends = running_sends = GrantedSends
    
        @classmethod
        def require_held_by(cls, state: MaintenanceState, holder: str, change: str) -> None:
            raise MaintenanceNotHeldError.unheld(change)
    
        @classmethod
        def holder_dead(cls, state: MaintenanceState) -> bool:
            return False
    
        @classmethod
        def hold_for(cls, barrier: MaintenanceBarrier, state: MaintenanceStatus,
                     operator: MaintenanceOperator) -> MaintenanceState:
            return barrier.begin(operator)
    
        @classmethod
        def successors(cls):
            return (DrainingPhase,)
    
        @classmethod
        def hold_restore(cls, barrier: MaintenanceBarrier, operator: MaintenanceOperator,
                         drained: Callable[[], None]) -> None:
            """The round trip failed on the reopened bus: hold it again and wait for its readers
            to drain; the restored bus brings back the upgrade's own hold."""
            barrier.begin(operator)
            drained()
    
    
    class DeadHolderReleasedPhase(ReadyPhase):
        """The stored operator is the dead incarnation whose hold this record released."""

    Keep this ABC registry-free: DeclaredFamily roots own membership, and mixing it
    into a root must never start a second registry for the same lifecycle.

    from __future__ import annotations

    class LifecycleState(LifecycleCapability, ABC):
        declared_name: ClassVar[str]
    
        @classmethod
        @abstractmethod
        def successors(cls) -> tuple[type[LifecycleState], ...]:
            """States reachable by an ordinary transition (including self, if allowed)."""
    
        def may_become(self, nxt: LifecycleState) -> bool:
            return isinstance(nxt, self.successors())
    
        @classmethod
        @abstractmethod
        def members_with(cls, capability: type) -> tuple[type[Self], ...]:
            """Supplied by DeclaredFamily in each domain root."""
    
        @classmethod
        def transition_table(cls) -> dict[str, frozenset[str]]:
            return {
                member.declared_name: frozenset(
                    state.declared_name
                    for successor in member.successors()
                    for state in cls.members_with(successor)
                )
                for member in cls.members_with(cls)
            }

    A test asks for the requirement's fixture. Where the thing is absent the test is
    skipped with the requirement's reason; it never fails on a missing variable.
    """
    
    from __future__ import annotations

    from typing import ClassVar
    
    import pytest
    
    
    class Requirement:
        fixture: ClassVar[str]
        reason: ClassVar[str]
    
        @classmethod
        def find(cls) -> object | None:
            """The required thing, or None when this machine does not have it."""
            raise NotImplementedError
    
        @classmethod
        def require(cls) -> object:
            found = cls.find()
            if found is None:
                pytest.skip(cls.reason)
            return found

                verify_native_package(Path(value))

    """The install launch path, run the way an owner runs it, before any merge lands.
    
    0765a002c broke every ``agent-comms install`` without ``--repos``, and install 21
    refused because the target's owner probe asked the outgoing runtime for a method it no
    longer had (fixed in #2419); every required check passed both, because nothing ran the
    installer. This rehearses a real bus through the CLI under test, with the merge base's
    build installed as the outgoing runtime: launch, target tree, staged stack build,
    carried practice copy and the outgoing runtime's owner probe.
    """
    from __future__ import annotations
    
    import os
    import sqlite3
    import subprocess
    import sys
    from contextlib import closing
    from pathlib import Path
    
    import pytest
    
    from agent_comms.field_codec import FieldCodec
    from agent_comms.installer.backup import bus_files
    from agent_comms.installer.practice import TestHome
    from agent_comms.installer.upgrade import (
        CarriedRehearsal,
        RehearsedUpgrade,
        UncopiedRehearsal,
        Upgrade,
    )
    from agent_comms.repo import Checkout, ScratchCheckout
    from agent_comms.typed_table import ReconciledFile
    from conftest import declare_test_bus, publish_initial
    
    REPOSITORY = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
    
    
    def git(*arguments: str) -> str:
        return subprocess.run(["git", "-C", REPOSITORY, *arguments], check=True,
                              capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
    
    
    @pytest.fixture(scope="module")
    def installed_home(tmp_path_factory) -> dict[str, str]:
        """A home holding what an installed machine has: the installer's uv, and as the
        installed runtime a build of the merge base this change lands on. Both cases share
        it, so the second reuses the staged runtime the first built, as a second install
        would. Package caches stay shared."""
        home = tmp_path_factory.mktemp("installed-home")
        uv = home / ".local/state/agent-comms/upgrade-bus/uv"
        uv.parent.mkdir(parents=True)
        uv.symlink_to(TestHome(home).uv)
        caches = subprocess.run([uv, "cache", "dir"], check=True, capture_output=True, text=True)
        environment = {**os.environ, "HOME": str(home), "UV_CACHE_DIR": caches.stdout.strip(),
                       "npm_config_cache": str(Path.home() / ".npm")}
        environment.pop("PYTHONPATH", None)
        # The checkout owner adds the tree with its pinned submodules; `git archive` drops them.
        base = ScratchCheckout.add(REPOSITORY, home / "outgoing-source",
                                   git("merge-base", "HEAD", "origin/main"), "--detach")
        runtime = home / ".local/share/agent-comms/runtimes/outgoing"
        try:
            subprocess.run([uv, "venv", "-q", "--python", sys.executable, runtime], check=True,
                           env=environment)
            subprocess.run([uv, "pip", "install", "-q", "--python", runtime / "bin/python", base.path],
                           check=True, env=environment)
        finally:
            base.retire()
        (home / ".local/share/agent-comms/current").symlink_to(runtime, target_is_directory=True)
        return environment
    
    
    def drop_one_index(root: Path) -> None:
        """One declared store's schema drifts from both runtimes' declarations."""
        for path in sorted(ReconciledFile.existing_in(root)):
            with closing(sqlite3.connect(path)) as db:
                index = db.execute("SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='index'"
                                   " AND sql IS NOT NULL ORDER BY name LIMIT 1").fetchone()
                if index:
                    db.execute(f'DROP INDEX "{index[0]}"')
                    db.commit()
                    return
        raise AssertionError("No declared store has an index to drop")
    
    
    @pytest.mark.timeout(280)
    @pytest.mark.parametrize("repos, rehearsal", (
        ((), UncopiedRehearsal), (("--repos",), CarriedRehearsal),
    ), ids=("kept-repos-nothing-to-carry", "given-repos-drifted-store"))
    def test_install_rehearses_without_changing_the_bus(private_comms, installed_home, tmp_path,
                                                        repos, rehearsal):
        """A bus with nothing to carry is rehearsed without a copy; one store whose schema
        drifted makes the rehearsal copy the bus and carry it. Neither changes the bus."""
        comms = private_comms
        declare_test_bus(comms, channels=("comms",), threads=(
            comms.registry.new_thread(name="worker", tags=frozenset(), worktree=str(tmp_path)),))
        publish_initial(comms, "worker", "#all", "One message before the install")
        if rehearsal is CarriedRehearsal:
            drop_one_index(comms.root)
        checkout = tmp_path / "checkout"
        subprocess.run(["git", "clone", "-q", REPOSITORY, checkout], check=True)
        Checkout(checkout).prepare()
        before = bus_files(comms.root)
        given = (*repos, str(checkout)) if repos else ()
        installed = subprocess.run(
            [Path(sys.executable).with_name("agent-comms"), "--root", comms.root, "install",
             "--rehearse", "--checkout", checkout, "--to", "HEAD", "--project", checkout, *given],
            cwd=checkout, env={**installed_home, "PYTHONPATH": os.environ.get("PYTHONPATH", "")},
            capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=270)
        assert installed.returncode == 0, installed.stderr
        result = FieldCodec.decode(Upgrade, FieldCodec.parse(installed.stdout))
        assert isinstance(result, RehearsedUpgrade) and type(result.rehearsal) is rehearsal
        assert bus_files(comms.root) == before

I spent reasoning on the assertions and too little on factoring the work. Then the scratch script accumulated its own setup and even an invented API call. Calling it temporary made that shortcut easier to excuse.

I can describe that sequence from the work you saw. I can’t inspect my weights and establish the internal cause. But the correction is concrete: find the existing owner before writing the executable—even when it’s “just a script.”
