        @staticmethod
        async def attach_saved_owner(agent, *, project, session):
            """Restore this saved declaration before acquiring its live process."""
            def acquire():
                comms = agent._comms
                owned = agent.sessions.declare_thread(str(project))
                return comms.threads.attach_session(owned, str(session), process=owned.process_identity)
    
            thread = await Coordination.run_worker(acquire)
            await agent.sessions.bind_owned(thread, thread.name)
            agent.inputs.ensure_live_drain(thread.name)
            return thread.name
    
        async def bind_saved_owner(self, agent, *, project, session):
            """Acquire the restored SDK source's original attested native child."""
            session_id = await self.attach_saved_owner(agent, project=project, session=session)
            original = await Coordination.run_worker(partial(agent._comms.registry.require, session_id))
            await agent.turns.backend_for(session_id, original).prepare(original)
            child = agent.turns.persistent_backends[session_id].child_state.child
            self.children.append(child)
            return session_id
    
        @staticmethod
        def native_arguments(options=("--no-tools",)):
            """One external native argument declaration for saved/ACP consumers."""
            return ("--provider", "response-local", "--model", "fixture", "--thinking", "off",
                    "--offline", "--no-extensions", "--no-skills", "--no-context-files",
                    "--no-prompt-templates", *options)
    
        @asynccontextmanager
        async def open_owner(self, *, runtime_enabled=False, auto_wake=False,
                             native_options=("--no-tools",), client=None):
            """Acquire the real saved ACP owner and attested idle native child."""
            agent = canonical_agent(
                Comms(self.root), auto_wake=auto_wake, runtime_enabled=runtime_enabled, agent_bin=GivenBinary("pi"),
                agent_args=GivenArguments(tuple(self.native_arguments(native_options))),
            )
            agent.on_connect(client)
            try:
                await agent._runtime.start()
                session_id = await self.bind_saved_owner(agent, project=self.project, session=self.session)
                yield agent, session_id
            finally:
                await agent.shutdown()
                assert not agent.turns.turn_tasks and not any(state.turn_open() for state in agent.inputs.drained.values())
                assert not agent.turns.persistent_backends
    
        @asynccontextmanager
        async def original_input(self, agent, session_id, text):
            """Reserve and acquire through the same input/turn owners as ACP dispatch."""
            async with AsyncExitStack() as resources:
                async with InitialInput.reserve(
                    agent.inputs, session_id, agent.sessions.require(session_id),
                    text=text, prompt=text, echo=True, images=(), controller=None,
                ) as reservation:
                    item = reservation.item
                    resources.push_async_callback(reservation.release().aclose)
                # Native acquisition begins after the wire reservation ends; its
                # rollback actions remain with this turn until acquisition finishes.
                turn = OwnedTurn(
                    agent.turns, session_id, agent.sessions.require(session_id), text,
                    original_keys=(item.key,), initial_display_text=text,
                    original_owner_input=True, original_goal_id=item.context.active_goal_id,
                )
                async with AsyncExitStack() as permits:
                    assert await turn.acquire(resources, permits)
                    yield turn
    
        async def force_reopen(self):
            """Retire this fixture's actual attested child; the next turn opens the saved session."""
            self.persistent.child_state.child.attestation.require_identity()
            await self.persistent.close_idle()
    
        def started(self, public_id, native_id, text):
            self.starts.append((public_id, native_id, text))
            child = backend.TurnSession.active[asyncio.current_task()].native
            # Cleanup already belongs to the saved-session owner at native input start;
            # there is no later copy from transient TurnSession process fields.
            assert self.persistent.child_state.child is child
            assert self.persistent.child_state.child.reader is not None
            if child not in self.children:
                self.children.append(child)
            return True
    
        async def run(self, text, *, followup=None, queue=None, **options):
            queue = queue if queue is not None else TurnInbox()
            result = []
            async with asyncio.timeout(25):
                async for event in backend.stream_agent_events(
                    "pi",
                    self.native_arguments(),
                    text,
                    str(self.project),
                    root=self.root, owner=self.participant, session_file=str(self.session),
                    persistent_session=self.persistent,
                    package=self.package,
                    tool_mode=NoSelectedTools(),
                    steering_queue=queue,
                    native_start=self.started,
                    **options,
                 session_directory=self.root):
                    result.append(event)
                    self.observed.append(event)
                    if followup is not None and isinstance(event, events.InputStarted):
                        queue.put_nowait(InputRequest(
                            input_id=InputId("queued"),
                            content=InputContent(text=followup),
                            when_busy=WhenBusy.STEER,
                        ))
                        followup = None
            return result
    
        def saved_inputs(self):
            rows = map(json.loads, self.session.read_text().splitlines())
            return [
                row["message"]
                for row in rows
                if row.get("type") == "message" and row["message"].get("role") == "user"
            ]

        def environment(self, inherited: dict[str, str]) -> dict[str, str]:
            """The environment of a process that may only touch these roots."""
            env = {key: value for key, value in inherited.items()
                   if not key.startswith("AGENT_COMMS_") and key != "NO_COLOR"}
            env.update({
                ATTEMPT: str(self.attempt),
                "AGENT_COMMS_ROOT": str(self.wire),
                "XDG_CONFIG_HOME": str(self.attempt / "config"),

                "TERM": "xterm-256color",
                "COLORTERM": "truecolor",
                "FORCE_COLOR": "1",
            })
            return env

        name: str

        @classmethod
        def from_task(cls, *, task: str = "", **values) -> NewThreadSpec:
            return cls(task=TaskLaunchInput(task) if task else LaunchInput(), **values)
    
        def declaration(self, project: str, registry: Registration) -> Thread:
            return registry.new_thread(name=self.name, task=self.task.thread_text(), tags=self.tags.for_new(),
                          worktree=project, model=self.model, thinking_level=self.thinking_level)
    
        @contextmanager
        def prepared(self, threads: ThreadManagement, pi_bin: str, runtime: LaunchRuntime) -> Iterator[Thread]:
            project = Path(self.project).expanduser().resolve(strict=True)
            thread = self.declaration(str(project), threads.registry)
            threads.registry.require_declaration_available(thread)
            location = thread.runtime.new_location(threads.root, project)
            with _store_lock(threads._wire_lock_path):
                yield replace(thread, session_file=SavedSessionFile(location.read_key))
    
    
    @dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True, kw_only=True)
    class ForkSpec(NewThreadSpec):
        """A fork differs only in its parent-derived source and inherited settings."""
    
        parent: str
    
        def _parent(self, threads: ThreadManagement) -> Thread:
            parent = threads.registry.require(self.parent)
            parent.execution.require_native()
            parent.runtime.require_forkable()
            return parent
    
        def child(self, parent: Thread, runtime: RuntimeLocation, registry: Registration) -> Thread:
            return replace(self.declaration(self.project, registry), parent=ForkedParent(parent.name),
                           tags=self.tags.for_child(parent.tags),
                           backend=parent.backend, session_file=SavedSessionFile(runtime.read_key))
    
        @contextmanager
        def prepared(self, threads: ThreadManagement, pi_bin: str, runtime: LaunchRuntime) -> Iterator[Thread]:
            # Copy saved history outside the wire lock, retaining writer→wire order.
            parent = self._parent(threads)
            threads.registry.require_declaration_available(self.child(parent, parent.runtime, threads.registry))
            location = asyncio.run(parent.backend.fork(parent, pi_bin, runtime))
            with _store_lock(threads._wire_lock_path):
                current = self._parent(threads)
                if current.incarnation != parent.incarnation or current.runtime != parent.runtime:
                    raise RelationViolationError(
                        f"Parent thread {self.parent!r} changed its saved session during the fork; "
                        f"the created fork {location} was not registered."
                    )
                yield self.child(current, location, threads.registry)

        def create(self, spec: NewThreadSpec) -> Thread:
            """Prepare the session, then register and launch the thread with its task as first input."""
            resolved_bin = ConfiguredBinary().configured()
            runtime = LaunchRuntime.running()
            with spec.prepared(self, resolved_bin, runtime) as child:
                child = self.registry._declare_unlocked(child)
                try:
                    owned = self.owners._launch_owner_unlocked(
                        child, resolved_bin, initial_input=spec.task, launch_runtime=runtime,
                    )
                    spec.task.record_first_input(
                        partial(InputDispositions(self.root).record, owner=owned.name, target=owned.name,
                            claim_scope=self.registry.snapshot().claim_generation(owned.name),
                        ))
                    return owned
                except OSError:
                    self.registry.remove(spec.name)
                    raise
    
        def adopt_current(self) -> Thread:
            """Declare and register the current process's thread from env."""
            thread = current_thread(self.registry)
            return self.registry.declare(thread)

    async def attached_app(workspace, comms, thread: str, *, size: tuple[int, int] = (160, 44),
                           application: type | None = None, attached: bool = True, project: Path | None = None):
        """Start Toad on declared thread `thread` through Core's ACP server; yields (ui, agent) once
        the session has settled. Stops the agent and every owner on the wire afterwards."""
        from toad.app import ToadApp
    
        agent = None
        started = partial(application or ToadApp, agent_session_id=thread)
        if project is not None:
            started = partial(started, project_dir=str(project))
        try:
            async with workspace.app(size=size, agent=comms_agent(), application=_first_wins(started)) as ui:
                await ui.until(lambda: ui.conversation.agent is not None, seconds=20, why="the agent object")
                agent = ui.conversation.agent
                await ui.until(agent.session.settled.is_set, seconds=30, why="the ACP session to settle")
                assert agent.session.connected is attached, "Unexpected ACP attachment outcome"
                yield ui, agent
        finally:
            if agent is not None:
                await agent.stop()
            for name in comms.registry.all_threads():
                await asyncio.to_thread(comms.owners.stop, name)
    
    
    def _first_wins(started):
        """Construct with the arguments bound here taking precedence over the caller's."""
        def construct(**given):
            return started.func(**{**given, **started.keywords})
        return construct
    
    
    @asynccontextmanager
    async def native_session(workspace, *, provider: ControlledProvider | None = None,
                             settings: dict | None = None, prepare=None, size: tuple[int, int] = (160, 44),
                             application: type | None = None, attached: bool = True):
        """Start Toad on a declared native thread ``beta`` whose model is the controlled provider.
    
        `prepare(comms, project, provider)` may arrange wire state before the app starts.
        `attached=False` expects the session to settle without a connection.
        """
    
        provider = provider or ControlledProvider()
        with provider.serving() as base_url:
            comms = start_private_native_wire(workspace.roots.wire)
            configure_provider(base_url, settings=settings)
            comms.registry.declare(comms.registry.new_thread("beta", frozenset({"team"}), str(workspace.project),
                                          model=MODEL, thinking_level="off"))
            try:
                if prepare is not None:
                    await prepare(comms, workspace.project, provider)
                async with attached_app(workspace, comms, "beta", size=size, application=application,
                                        attached=attached) as (ui, agent):
                    yield NativeSession(ui, agent, comms, provider, workspace.project)
                    assert not provider.failures, provider.failures
            except BaseException as error:
                if provider.failures:
                    error.add_note(f"Controlled provider failures: {provider.failures}")
                raise
            finally:
                provider.release()
    
    
    def without_provider(models: str = "test/model") -> None:
        """Configure native owners with a model nothing serves, for tests that must never ask one."""
        os.environ.update(AGENT_COMMS_AGENT_BIN="pi", AGENT_COMMS_AGENT_ARGS="", AGENT_COMMS_AGENT_MODELS=models)
    
    
    def owner_server(comms, *, provider: str = "openrouter", model: str = "fake"):
        """Core's ACP server object in this process, able to start native owners on the private wire."""
        from agent_comms.acp import CommsAgent
        from agent_comms.native_arguments import GivenArguments
    
        return CommsAgent(
            comms, agent_args=GivenArguments(("--provider", provider, "--model", model)),
            runtime_enabled=True, auto_wake=False)
            await ui.until(lambda: bool(view.submissions.queue_projection.items), seconds=20,
                           why="the queued input in the returned view")
            assert "QUEUED_NATIVE_INPUT" in view.query_one(QueueSummary).render().plain
            assert ui.draft() == "unsent local draft"
            await finish_both_turns(native)
            assert ui.draft() == "unsent local draft"
    
    
    async def test_direct_message_is_answered_once_and_marked_responded(workspace, native_package):
        async with native_session(workspace) as native:
            await direct_reply_feedback(native, native.ui.selected_tab, hold=True)
    
    
    async def test_channel_message_the_thread_declines_is_marked_checked(workspace, native_package):
        async with native_session(workspace) as native:
            await channel_message_feedback(native, native.ui.selected_tab)
            assert len(native.provider.requests) == 1, native.provider.requests

    MAX_DEPTH = 32
    
    
    class NativePackageError(ValueError):
        """Package bytes or filesystem shape are not the pinned native artifact."""
    
    
    def _resource_root() -> Path:
        module = Path(__file__).resolve()
        # A checkout owns its resources in stack/, even if build artifacts exist
        # beside the source. Only an installed package owns _native resources.
        if module.parent.name == "agent_comms" and module.parent.parent.name == "src":
            return module.parents[2] / "stack"
        packaged = module.with_name("_native")
        if packaged.is_dir():
            return packaged
        raise NativePackageError("Installed native package resources are unavailable")
    
    
    MANIFEST = _resource_root() / "pi-native.sha256"
    OWNER_INSTRUCTIONS = _resource_root() / "APPEND_SYSTEM.md"
    # Derived from OWNER_INSTRUCTIONS and the commander's packaged sources at preparation.
    UNIT_INSTRUCTIONS = _resource_root() / "UNIT_SYSTEM.md"
    
    
    PACKAGE_LAYOUT = "node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent"
    
    
    def pin_id() -> str:
        return hashlib.sha256(MANIFEST.read_bytes()).hexdigest()[:16]
    
    
    def pinned_package_in(root: Path) -> Path:
        """Where this pin's built package sits under a root laid out as stack/ is."""
        return root / f".pi-native-{pin_id()}" / PACKAGE_LAYOUT
    
    
    def pinned_location() -> Path:
        return pinned_package_in(MANIFEST.parent)
    
    
    def pinned_native_package() -> Path:
        if not (package := pinned_location()).is_dir():
            raise NativePackageError(f"Pinned native package directory is missing: {package}")
        return package
    
    
    def package_tree_digest(root: Path) -> str:

    Nothing here reaches a real model: the native agent is configured with one
    provider, a loopback HTTP endpoint in this process that answers what the test

    def last_user_texts(request: dict) -> tuple[str, ...]:
        message = request["messages"][-1]
        if message["role"] != "user":
            return ()
        content = message["content"]
        return (content,) if isinstance(content, str) else tuple(
            block["text"] for block in content if block["type"] == "text")
    
    
    def selected_triage_reply(request: dict, decision=None) -> dict | None:
        """The answer to Core's "should this thread respond" question, when `request` is one."""
        from agent_comms.field_codec import FieldCodec
        from agent_comms.selected_triage import IgnoreSelectedTriage, SelectedTriage
        from agent_comms.turn_context import InstructionFile
    
        texts = last_user_texts(request)
        output = InstructionFile.read("selected-triage-output.md").render(SelectedTriage.output_values()).strip()
        if not any(text.rstrip().endswith(output) for text in texts):
            return None
        return {"role": "assistant", "content": json.dumps(FieldCodec.encode(
            IgnoreSelectedTriage() if decision is None else decision))}
    
    
    def wire_reply(request: dict, answer: str) -> dict | None:
        """The answer to a wire message, in the form Core asks for: its example records with `answer` as text."""
        from agent_comms.turn_context import InstructionFile
    
        placeholder = InstructionFile.read("selected-response-example.md").content
        marker = "Declared Message examples: "
        for text in last_user_texts(request):
            if marker in text:
                examples, _end = json.JSONDecoder().raw_decode(text[text.index(marker) + len(marker):])
                records = json.loads(json.dumps(examples).replace(json.dumps(placeholder), json.dumps(answer)))
                return {"role": "assistant", "content": json.dumps(records)}
        return None

        @contextmanager
        def serving(self):
            """Serve on a free loopback port; yields the base URL."""
            provider = self
    
            class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
                def do_POST(self):
                    provider.answer(self)
    
                def log_message(self, *_args):
                    pass
    
            server = ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), Handler)
            threading.Thread(target=server.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()
            try:
                yield f"http://127.0.0.1:{server.server_port}/v1"
            finally:
                self.release()
                server.shutdown()
                server.server_close()
    
    
    def start_private_native_wire(root: Path):
        """Create a private root; Core derives its root identity and reviewed package."""
        from agent_comms.comms import Comms
    
        comms = Comms(root)
        comms.messaging.initialize_private_initial_protocol()
        os.environ["AGENT_COMMS_ROOT"] = str(comms.root)
        for key in ("PI_PROMPT", "PI_PARENT_ID", "PI_AGENT_ID"):
            os.environ.pop(key, None)
        return comms
    
    
    def configure_provider(base_url: str, *, settings: dict | None = None) -> None:
        """Point the native agent at the controlled provider, in this test's Pi settings directory."""
        config = Path(os.environ["PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR"])
        config.mkdir(mode=0o700, parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        (config / "models.json").write_text(json.dumps({"providers": {PROVIDER: {
            "baseUrl": base_url, "api": "openai-completions",
            "models": [{"id": "fixture", "name": "Offline fixture", "reasoning": True,
                        "contextWindow": 32768, "maxTokens": 2048}],
        }}}))
        (config / "auth.json").write_text(json.dumps({PROVIDER: {"type": "api_key", "key": KEY}}))
        if settings is not None:
            (config / "settings.json").write_text(json.dumps(settings))
        os.environ.update(
            AGENT_COMMS_AGENT_BIN="pi",
            AGENT_COMMS_AGENT_ARGS=f"--provider {PROVIDER} --model fixture --no-extensions --no-skills --no-context-files",
            AGENT_COMMS_AGENT_MODELS=MODEL,
        )

    """The model a thread declares: a provider/model name, or none, left to its runtime."""
    
    from __future__ import annotations
    
    from abc import abstractmethod
    from dataclasses import dataclass
    from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
    
    from agent_comms.field_codec import SubclassUnion, boundary_decoder
    from agent_comms.native_arguments import ModelArgument, NativeArguments, ProviderArgument, SelectedModel
    from agent_comms.native_failures import NativePiUnavailable
    from agent_comms.thread_text import AbsentText, GivenText, TextChoice
    
    if TYPE_CHECKING:
        from agent_comms.pi_commands import SetModel
    
    
    class ThreadModel(SubclassUnion, TextChoice, affix="Model"):
        """A thread's declared model; an undeclared one is observed from its runtime."""
    
        @staticmethod
        @boundary_decoder
        def reported(name: str | None) -> ThreadModel:
            """The model an external producer reports by name, or none."""
            return ThreadModel.from_wire(name)
    
        @staticmethod
        @boundary_decoder
        def selected_by(arguments: NativeArguments) -> ThreadModel:
            """The model a launch's native arguments select, or none."""
            selected = arguments.value(ModelArgument)
            provider = arguments.value(ProviderArgument)
            if selected is None or provider is None:
                return ThreadModel.reported(selected)
            return DeclaredModel(SelectedModel(provider, selected.removeprefix(provider + "/")).qualified)
    
        @staticmethod
        @boundary_decoder
        def from_choice(choice: tuple[str, str] | None) -> ThreadModel:
            """A saved session's provider and model, or none."""
            return UndeclaredModel() if choice is None else DeclaredModel("/".join(choice))
    
        @abstractmethod
        def native(self, arguments: NativeArguments) -> NativeArguments:
            """The native arguments selecting this model."""
    
        @abstractmethod
        def applied(self, previous: ThreadModel) -> ThreadModel:
            """An undeclared model takes the previous or observed one; a declared one keeps itself."""
    
        @abstractmethod
        def set_model(self, command: type[SetModel]) -> SetModel: ...
    
        @abstractmethod
        def require_reported(self) -> DeclaredModel:
            """A native runtime's configuration report must name its model."""
    
    
    @dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
    class DeclaredModel(GivenText, ThreadModel):
        text: str
    
        def __post_init__(self) -> None:
            if not self.text.strip():
                raise ValueError("Thread model cannot be empty.")
    
        def native(self, arguments: NativeArguments) -> NativeArguments:
            return arguments.with_model(self.text)
    
        def applied(self, previous: ThreadModel) -> DeclaredModel:
            return self
    
        def set_model(self, command: type[SetModel]) -> SetModel:
            selected = SelectedModel.decode(self.text)
            return command(provider=selected.provider, model_id=selected.model)
    
        def require_reported(self) -> DeclaredModel:
            return self
    
    
    @dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
    class UndeclaredModel(AbsentText, ThreadModel):
        def native(self, arguments: NativeArguments) -> NativeArguments:
            return arguments
    
        def applied(self, previous: ThreadModel) -> ThreadModel:
            return previous
    
        def set_model(self, command: type[SetModel]) -> SetModel:
            return command()
    
        def require_reported(self) -> DeclaredModel:
            raise NativePiUnavailable("Native configuration did not report a model")
        @classmethod
        @abstractmethod
        def wire_value(cls) -> str | None:
            raise NotImplementedError("Abstract thinking choices have no wire value.")
    
        @classmethod
        @abstractmethod
        def require_reported(cls, refusal: Exception) -> type[ThinkingLevel]:
            """The level a native report named; no override raises ``refusal``."""
    
    
    class ThinkingLevel(ThinkingChoice, DeclaredFamily, affix="ThinkingLevel"):
        ordinary_choice = True
    
        @classmethod
        def native_arguments[T](cls, argument: Callable[[type[ThinkingLevel]], T]) -> tuple[T, ...]:
            return (argument(cls),)
    
        @classmethod
        def wire_value(cls) -> str:
            return cls.declared_name
    
        @classmethod
        def require_reported(cls, refusal: Exception) -> type[ThinkingLevel]:
            return cls
    
    
    class NoThinkingOverride(ThinkingChoice):
        @classmethod
        def native_arguments[T](cls, argument: Callable[[type[ThinkingLevel]], T]) -> tuple[T, ...]:
            return ()
    
        @classmethod
        def applied(cls, current: type[ThinkingChoice]) -> type[ThinkingChoice]:
            return current
    
        @classmethod
        def observed(cls, level: type[ThinkingChoice]) -> type[ThinkingChoice]:
            return level
    
        @classmethod
        def wire_value(cls) -> None:
            return None
    
        @classmethod
        def require_reported(cls, refusal: Exception) -> type[ThinkingLevel]:
            raise refusal
    
    
    class ThinkingLevelValue(AcceptsNull, FieldRepresentation):
    
        @classmethod
        def decode(cls, value: object) -> type[ThinkingChoice]:
            if value is None:
                return NoThinkingOverride
            return ThinkingLevel.member_named(FieldCodec.decode(str, value))
    
        @classmethod
        def encode(cls, value: object) -> str | None:
            if isinstance(value, type) and issubclass(value, ThinkingChoice):
                return value.wire_value()
            raise ValueError("Thinking level requires a thinking choice declaration.")
    
        @classmethod
        def schema(cls) -> dict[str, object]:
            return FieldCodec.value_schema(type[ThinkingLevel] | None)
    
    
    ThinkingLevelField = Annotated[type[ThinkingChoice], ThinkingLevelValue]

    class ConversationSessionBinding(WorkspaceHosted, ThreadStatusOwner, containers.Vertical):
        """Source-bound state and reusable rich-surface lifecycle shared by conversations."""
    
        thread_presentation = None
        """The agent thread's latest settled presentation."""
    
        _thread_read = NoPendingThreadRead()
        """The source state the next observed presentation settles against."""
    
        _unpublished_presentation = None
        """An observed presentation whose transcript refresh waits for this view to be shown."""
    
        @property
        def operational_sources(self):
            from toad.screens.session_view import SessionView
    
            return self.query_ancestor(SessionView).presentation.sources
    
        def transcript_scope(self) -> tuple[str, str] | None:
            """The native session identity whose canonical transcript this view shows."""
            from toad.screens.session_view import SessionView
    
            origin = self.query_ancestor(SessionView).origin
            return origin.transcript_scope() if origin is not None else None
    
        def status_thread(self) -> StatusThread:
            scope = self.transcript.binding.thread_scope
            if scope is None:
                return NoStatusThread()
            root, name = scope
            return StatusThread.for_root(Path(root), name, self.app.coordination_access)
    
        def arm_thread_read(self) -> None:
            """Capture turn token and client authority for the next observed presentation."""
            self._thread_read = self.agent_binding.thread_read()
    
        def thread_observed(self, event: core_events.ThreadRowsChanged) -> None:
            """Consume this thread's one observed presentation."""
            presentation = self.app.coordination_access.thread_status.open(self.status_thread().name).presentation
            read = self._thread_read
            self.arm_thread_read()
            read.settle(presentation).present(self.thread_presented)
    
        def foreign_thread_read(self, presentation) -> None:
            self.thread_presented(presentation)
    
        def thread_presented(self, presentation) -> None:
            """A settled presentation refreshes the transcript source of the shown view."""
            from toad.screens.session_view import SessionView
    
            self.thread_presentation = presentation
            self._update_model_info()
            if presentation is None or not self.transcript.readable:
                return
            if self.query_ancestor(SessionView).is_current:
                from toad.transcript_publication import ObservedSourcePublication
                self._unpublished_presentation = None
                self.transcript.source_requests.request(ObservedSourcePublication, presentation)
            else:
                self._unpublished_presentation = presentation
    
        @handles(core_events.SessionSelected)
        async def _thread_view_selected(self, event: CoreEventMessage) -> None:
            from toad.screens.session_view import SessionView
    
            if not self.query_ancestor(SessionView).is_current:
                return
            self.refresh_thread_status()
            self.goal_observation.invalidate()
            presentation = self._unpublished_presentation
            if presentation is not None:
                from toad.transcript_publication import ObservedSourcePublication
                self._unpublished_presentation = None
                self.transcript.source_requests.request(ObservedSourcePublication, presentation)
    
        @handles(core_events.ObservedServiceChanged)
        async def _thread_route_observed(self, event: CoreEventMessage) -> None:
            self.refresh_thread_status()
    
        def bind_agent(self, agent: AgentBinding) -> None:
            self.agent_binding = agent
            agent.attach_view(self)
    
        def apply_bound_agent(self, agent: AgentBase) -> None:
            self._update_model_info()
            self.status = agent.context_measurement.status()
            if agent.ready:
                self.session_ready()
                self.call_later(self.goal_observation.invalidate)
                self.call_later(self.delivery_observation.invalidate)
    
        def agent_connected(self, agent: AgentBase) -> None:
            self.flash(Content.assemble(agent.get_info(), " connected"), style="success")
            if self._agent_data is not None:
                self.app.application.usage.publish("agent-session-begin", agent=self._agent_data.identity)
    
        async def cancel_bound_turn(self, agent: AgentBase) -> None:
            self.flash("Cancelling agent turn…")
            self.turns.describe("Cancelling…")
            if self._loading is not None and self._loading.is_attached:
                self._loading.update("Cancelling…")
            if await agent.cancel():
                self.flash("Turn cancelled", style="success")
            else:
                self.flash("Agent declined to cancel. Please wait.", style="error")

        @abstractmethod

        @abstractmethod

            """Open another session tab on the project and return its identity."""
    
        @abstractmethod

            """Open a channel or direct-message tab for `actor` and return its identity."""
    
        @abstractmethod

            """Open the direct-message history between `actor` and `thread` and return its tab identity."""
    
        @abstractmethod

        @abstractmethod

        @abstractmethod

        @abstractmethod

        @abstractmethod

        def visible_text(self) -> str:
            return "\n".join(self.visible_lines())
    
        def shows(self, text: str) -> bool:
            return text in self.visible_text()
    
        async def type(self, text: str) -> None:
            await self.press(*("space" if char == " " else char for char in text))
    
        async def until(self, condition: Callable[[], object], *, seconds: float = 10, why: str = "") -> None:
            """Wait until `condition()` is true (it may be a coroutine function)."""
            try:
                async with asyncio.timeout(seconds):
                    while True:
                        result = condition()
                        if inspect.isawaitable(result):
                            result = await result
                        if result:
                            return
                        await self.step(0.02)
            except TimeoutError:
                raise NotShown(f"{why or 'condition'} not reached in {seconds}s; screen:\n{self.visible_text()}") from None
    
        async def until_agent_ready(self, *, seconds: float = 30) -> None:
            await self.until(self.agent_ready, seconds=seconds, why="the agent to accept input")
    
        async def until_shows(self, text: str, *, seconds: float = 10) -> None:
            await self.until(lambda: self.shows(text), seconds=seconds, why=f"{text!r} on screen")
    
    
    class TextualUi(AppAgents, Ui):
        """Toad drawn by Textual, driven headless through Textual's pilot; its agents attach to that app."""
    
        def __init__(self, app: ToadApp, pilot: Pilot) -> None:

        @property

            """The Textual app and pilot, for tests of Textual-owned behaviour only."""
            return self.app, self.pilot
    
        def visible_lines(self) -> list[str]:
            return [strip.text for strip in self.app.screen._compositor.render_strips()]
    
        def tabs(self) -> tuple[Tab, ...]:
            from toad.widgets.session_tabs import SessionLabel, SessionsTabs
    
            return tuple(Tab(label.id, label.render().plain)

        def selected_tab(self) -> str:

            widget = self.app.focused
            return "" if widget is None else (widget.id or type(widget).__name__)
    
        @property
        def conversation(self):
            """The selected session's conversation widget."""
            from toad.widgets.conversation import Conversation
    
            return self.app.selected_session.query_one(Conversation)
    
        def painted(self, widget) -> str:
            """The text drawn inside one widget's region of the screen."""
            region = widget.region
            return "\n".join(strip.crop(region.x, region.right).text
                             for strip in self.app.screen._compositor.render_strips()[region.y:region.bottom])
    
        @property
        def _prompt(self):
            from toad.widgets.prompt import Prompt
    
            return self.app.selected_session.query_one(Prompt)
    
        def draft(self) -> str:
            return self._prompt.text
    
        async def write_draft(self, text: str) -> None:

            self._prompt.focus()
            await self.step()
    
        def attach_agent(self, agent) -> None:

            self.conversation.bind_agent(agent)
    
        def status(self) -> str:
            return self.conversation.status.plain
    
        def agent_ready(self) -> bool:
            return self._prompt.agent_ready
    
        async def press(self, *keys: str) -> None:
            await self.pilot.press(*keys)
            await self.step()
    
        def _cell_of(self, text: str, occurrence: int) -> tuple[int, int]:
            """The screen cell where the nth drawn `text` starts."""
            from rich.cells import cell_len
    
            places = [(cell_len(line[:line.find(text)]), y)
                      for y, line in enumerate(self.visible_lines()) if text in line]
            if len(places) <= occurrence:
                raise NotShown(f"{text!r} is not on screen:\n{self.visible_text()}")
            return places[occurrence]
    
        async def click(self, text: str, *, occurrence: int = 0) -> None:
            assert await self.pilot.click(offset=self._cell_of(text, occurrence)), f"the click on {text!r} left the screen"
            await self.step()
    
        def link_at(self, text: str, *, occurrence: int = 0) -> tuple[str, tuple] | None:
            return self.app.screen.get_style_at(*self._cell_of(text, occurrence)).meta.get("@click")
    
        def hyperlink_at(self, text: str, *, occurrence: int = 0) -> str | None:
            return self.app.screen.get_style_at(*self._cell_of(text, occurrence)).link
    
        async def resize(self, width: int, height: int) -> None:
            await self.pilot.resize_terminal(width, height)
            await self.step()
    
        async def select_tab(self, identity: str) -> None:
            await self.app.select_session(identity)
            await self.step()
    
        async def close_tab(self, identity: str) -> None:
            await self.app.session_navigation.close(identity)
            await self.step()
    
        async def new_session(self) -> str:

    # Owner decisions
    
    ## 2026-10-14 — No lock held across a decode; readers never block
    
    Tristan: "why do we have so many issues wit hdecoding large fiel enirely over and over again and holding locks ofr not raso nits fuckign stupid, awwe want async not hodlign locks when it doesn' needto happen and deconding shit unecessarily"
    
    Witness: 10:52-10:57 every agent and CLI waited on
    `.bus_route_counts.sqlite3.lock` while one `watch` reader rebuilt the route
    projection from the whole 3.7 GB bus inside `BusRouteCounts.sync`.
    
    A reader never takes an exclusive lock. Readers of an append-only file read
    committed bytes up to a captured size; readers of SQLite use WAL snapshots.
    A writer holds its lock only to capture a cut or commit a bounded result,
    never across decoding, scanning or I/O proportional to file size: decode
    outside the lock, then commit with a revision check. Durable state that is
    rewritten whole on each change (a JSON file of all rows) is a defect; it is
    appended or keyed so a change costs its own size. Waiting for a lock is
    async in owners and never stalls an event loop.
    
    ## 2026-10-14 — Constant cost: nothing scales with history size or throughput
    
    Tristan: "it shuold decode from latest to oldest or jsut decode what it needs so that tis always fast and doesn't get longer with theard size"
    
    Tristan: "that shoudl eb the philslophy iwth comms and its Iu impelmeantaions, nothing scales with size or throuhgput, we keep everythign cosntant costs as much as possible"
    
    Core and every UI over it keep per-operation cost constant. Opening, switching,
    scrolling, sending and status updates do work bounded by what is shown or
    changed, never by thread length, bus length or message rate. Read newest to
    oldest and decode only the fields the current viewport needs. Aggregates
    (unread, activity, counts) are maintained incrementally by their owner when
    the source changes; readers take the current value. A walk to an unbounded
    ancestor, a full-bus scan or a decode-then-re-encode on a read path is a
    defect. Acceptance for performance work compares a short and the longest
    thread or bus on the same build: the costs must match.

    class ConversationSessionBinding(WorkspaceHosted, ThreadStatusOwner, containers.Vertical):
        """Source-bound state and reusable rich-surface lifecycle shared by conversations."""
    
        thread_presentation = None
        """The agent thread's latest settled presentation."""
    
        _thread_read = NoPendingThreadRead()
        """The source state the next observed presentation settles against."""
    
        _unpublished_presentation = None
        """An observed presentation whose transcript refresh waits for this view to be shown."""
    
        @property
        def operational_sources(self):
            from toad.screens.session_view import SessionView
    
            return self.query_ancestor(SessionView).presentation.sources
    
        def transcript_scope(self) -> tuple[str, str] | None:
            """The native session identity whose canonical transcript this view shows."""
            from toad.screens.session_view import SessionView
    
            origin = self.query_ancestor(SessionView).origin
            return origin.transcript_scope() if origin is not None else None
    
        def status_thread(self) -> StatusThread:
            scope = self.transcript.binding.thread_scope
            if scope is None:
                return NoStatusThread()
            root, name = scope
            return StatusThread.for_root(Path(root), name, self.app.coordination_access)
    
        def arm_thread_read(self) -> None:
            """Capture turn token and client authority for the next observed presentation."""
            self._thread_read = self.agent_binding.thread_read()
    
        def thread_observed(self, event: core_events.ThreadRowsChanged) -> None:
            """Consume this thread's one observed presentation."""
            presentation = self.app.coordination_access.thread_status.open(self.status_thread().name).presentation
            read = self._thread_read
            self.arm_thread_read()
            read.settle(presentation).present(self.thread_presented)
    
        def foreign_thread_read(self, presentation) -> None:
            self.thread_presented(presentation)
    
        def thread_presented(self, presentation) -> None:
            """A settled presentation refreshes the transcript source of the shown view."""
            from toad.screens.session_view import SessionView
    
            self.thread_presentation = presentation
            self._update_model_info()
            if presentation is None or not self.transcript.readable:
                return
            if self.query_ancestor(SessionView).is_current:
                from toad.transcript_publication import ObservedSourcePublication
                self._unpublished_presentation = None
                self.transcript.source_requests.request(ObservedSourcePublication, presentation)
            else:
                self._unpublished_presentation = presentation
    
        @handles(core_events.SessionSelected)
        async def _thread_view_selected(self, event: CoreEventMessage) -> None:
            from toad.screens.session_view import SessionView
    
            if not self.query_ancestor(SessionView).is_current:
                return
            self.refresh_thread_status()
            self.goal_observation.invalidate()
            presentation = self._unpublished_presentation
            if presentation is not None:
                from toad.transcript_publication import ObservedSourcePublication
                self._unpublished_presentation = None
                self.transcript.source_requests.request(ObservedSourcePublication, presentation)
    
        @handles(core_events.ObservedServiceChanged)
        async def _thread_route_observed(self, event: CoreEventMessage) -> None:
            self.refresh_thread_status()
    
        def bind_agent(self, agent: AgentBinding) -> None:
            self.agent_binding = agent
            agent.attach_view(self)
    
        def apply_bound_agent(self, agent: AgentBase) -> None:
            self._update_model_info()
            self.status = agent.context_measurement.status()
            if agent.ready:
                self.session_ready()
                self.call_later(self.goal_observation.invalidate)
                self.call_later(self.delivery_observation.invalidate)
    
        def agent_connected(self, agent: AgentBase) -> None:
            self.flash(Content.assemble(agent.get_info(), " connected"), style="success")
            if self._agent_data is not None:
                self.app.application.usage.publish("agent-session-begin", agent=self._agent_data.identity)
    
        async def cancel_bound_turn(self, agent: AgentBase) -> None:
            self.flash("Cancelling agent turn…")
            self.turns.describe("Cancelling…")
            if self._loading is not None and self._loading.is_attached:
                self._loading.update("Cancelling…")
            if await agent.cancel():
                self.flash("Turn cancelled", style="success")
            else:
                self.flash("Agent declined to cancel. Please wait.", style="error")
    
        @abstractmethod
        def _turn_changed(self, owner: TurnOwner) -> None:
            """Publish the concrete conversation's changed turn projection."""
            raise NotImplementedError
    
        busy_count = var(0)

    class AgentBase(AgentBinding):
        """Base class for an 'agent'."""
    
        def __init__(self, project_root: Path) -> None:
            self.project_root_path = project_root
            self.events = CoreEventStream(self)
            self.presentation = LocalAgentPresentation(self)
            from toad.acp.agent_configuration import AgentConfiguration
            self.configuration = AgentConfiguration(self)
    
        ready = False
    
        def attach_view(self, view) -> None:
            from toad.agent_surface import AttachedSurfaceBinding
            from toad.core.events import SessionAgentAttached
            self.attach_surface(AttachedSurfaceBinding(view, self.events))
            view.publish_core(SessionAgentAttached())
    
        def matches_agent(self, agent) -> bool:
            return self is agent
    
        def cancel_allowed(self, turn):
            return turn.can_cancel
    
        def matches_session(self, session_id):
            return self.session_id == session_id
    
        def borrowed_processes(self):
            return (self.process,)
    
        async def reconnect_session(self, source, plan):
            await self.session.reconnect(plan)
    
        async def change_project(self, view, path):
            project = await self.update_project(str(path))
            view.flash(Content(f"Project changed to {project}"), style="success")
    
        def request_compaction(self, view, instructions):
            view.compact_context(instructions)
    
        def begin_submission(self, owner, submission):
            return owner.start(submission, self)
    
        def accepts_failed_input(self, message):
            if message.publisher is not self or message.event.session_id != self.session_id:
                return False
            return (self.queue_attachment.accepts_request(message.event.queue_scope)
                    if message.event.recover_draft else True)
    
        def send_now(self, owner):
            return owner.send_bound_now(self)
    
        def invalidate_observation(self, observation):
            observation.schedule(self)
    
        @property
        def automatic_titles(self):
            return self.observed_thread() is None
    
        async def project_changed(self, path) -> None:
            from toad.db import DB
            self.project_root_path = path
            if (session_pk := self.session.pk) is not None:
                await DB().session_update_project(session_pk, path)
    
        def refresh_context(self, view) -> None:
            view.status = self.context_measurement.status()
    
        async def compact_context(self, instructions) -> None:
            await self.controller.compact_context(instructions)
    
        async def cancel_turn(self, view) -> None:
            await view.cancel_bound_turn(self)
    
        def accepts_message(self, message) -> bool:
            return message.publisher is self and message.event.session_id == self.session_id
    
        def refresh_projection(self, view) -> None:
            view.status = self.context_measurement.status()
            view.turns.bound()
            view.submissions.publish_pending()
            view.delivery_observation.invalidate()
    
        def start_session(self, view) -> None:
            if self.ready:
                view.session_ready()

    # Refactor audit
    
    Measure a codebase's structural debt, verify every finding in the code, map it into refactoring **surfaces**, and write a plan package that agents execute in parallel: binding rules, an index, shared abstractions, coordination, and one decision receipt per surface, written just in time.
    
    The per-decision method (census, required relation, owners, new-case test) belongs to the **nra-refactoring** skill; read it when writing receipts. This skill covers everything around it.
    
    **The pattern catalog (`references/patterns/`) is the heart of this skill.** It shows 43 antipatterns that agents produce by default, each as real slop beside its clean polymorphic form: what fact the code forces its reader to supply, which rung is broken (identity, membership, implementation), how families, capabilities composed by multiple inheritance, and derived single sources of truth collapse the duplication, and how many edits a new case needs before and after. Read its README before classifying findings, and cite pattern IDs in every receipt.
    
    ## Why the method looks like this
    
    - **The codebase is the prompt.** Agents copy the code around them far more than they follow instructions. Two versions of one mechanism in the tree teach the next agent whichever has more call sites, usually the old one. So the plans delete aggressively and build exemplars; instructions alone never win against the majority of the tree.
    - **Numbers lie in specific, repeatable ways.** A parser that can't read some files skips them silently. A file that "stopped churning" may have moved to another repo. A module named like a feature may be refactor output. Every surprising number is checked in the code before it is written down, and a wrong claim is corrected plainly the moment evidence contradicts it.
    - **The owner's attention is the scarcest resource.** Plans batch every owner-level question with a default, run peer to peer with no coordinator agent, and report status in one line.
    
    ## Workflow
    
    ### 0. Orient
    
    - Fetch and pin the heads you audit (`git fetch`, note the SHA and the PR number). Every document names its head, because `main` moves under plans quickly.
    - List open PRs and the files they touch; they block or collide with surfaces.
    - Check what CI exists. A repository with none gets a CI surface first.
    - Find the project's Python (`requires-python`) and run every script with it: `uv python install 3.x`, then `uv run --python 3.x …` or the interpreter `uv python find 3.x` prints.
    - For a fork, find its upstream and the merge-base; note whether upstream still moves.
    
    ### 1. Measure
    
    Run from the target repository (scripts are in this skill's `scripts/`):
    
    ```
    debt_census.py --repo . --root src/pkg                                  # snapshot
    debt_census.py --repo . --root src/pkg --base <old-sha>                 # what changed since
    debt_census.py --repo . --root src/pkg --upstream upstream/main --exclude tools/   # fork versus upstream
    overlay.py     --repo . --root src/pkg [--upstream upstream/main]       # what NRA cannot see
    attribute_origin.py --repo . --root src/pkg --since <old-sha> --foundation src/pkg/<abstraction>.py
    merge_review.py --repo . --root src/pkg --since <old-sha>                # the debt each merged PR added
    ```
    
    - **`debt_census.py`** reports densities per 1,000 code lines. The headline is `type(x) is` checks + boolean chains of four or more + string-keyed subscripts. `boolean_chain_terms` weighs each chain by its terms, so one eleven-term validity check counts eleven, not one. The overlay classifies the syntax of every term of every long chain and reports the dominant kind as an ownership lead, not a diagnosis. Predicate calls may already query the correct owner; inspect their declarations before choosing a target. Use `--exclude` for debugging scripts: they are not product code.
    - **`overlay.py`** finds string dispatch, `isinstance` switches, raw record shapes (and whether an existing class already models them), hand-written exact key-set checks, attribute access by name, god classes and functions, repeated literal sets, legacy markers, dead modules, positional inserts, JavaScript embedded in strings, and child-process sites. With `--upstream`, each finding is tagged with its origin.
    - **`merge_review.py`** measures every merged pull request since a revision, after minus before over the files it changed, and lists the merges that added the most debt and every merge that added dispatch. Use it for progress reviews and to find cleanup targets: a merge that added candidate debt is a cleanup plan's first witness. Parse failures name the merge and file, withhold rankings, and exit nonzero; never treat an incomplete review as zero debt.
    - **`attribute_origin.py`** classifies new modules by the pull request that created them, which is the only reliable way to say who introduced debt and whether it predates the abstractions it should use.
    - **Every script warns when files fail to parse.** Treat that warning as a stop: re-run with the right Python.
    - The scripts are themselves written to the catalog's standard (measures, findings, checks and modes are families in `scripts/audit/`). When you extend them, add a class; never add a branch. `references/patterns/agent-defaults.md` (AGENT-8) shows what their first version looked like, and why tooling is not exempt.
    
    Then run NRA's complete scan with the same Python (`python -m nominal_refactor_advisor src/pkg --json`) and confirm `complete: true` and zero omitted detectors. NRA keys on declared families, so a codebase that keeps its states in strings, booleans and `None` shows few findings; that is a blind spot, not health. The overlay covers it.
    
    ### 2. Verify before writing anything down
    
    Read the code behind every number you intend to state. Real corrections this method has produced:
    
    | The number said | The code showed |
    |---|---|
    | A god file dropped to 0% churn after a refactor | It moved to another repository through five paths; its churn followed it |
    | A child is killed with SIGKILL only, so descendants leak | It runs as PID 1 in a PID namespace; the whole tree dies |
    | Two compaction pipelines, so one is a copy | Different performers, authorities and records: two operations |
    | Modules named per phase, so a lifecycle split by phase | Pipeline roles in sound layers; the lifecycle was already a state family |
    | New modules are dense, so agents ignore the rules | 37 of 39 were written before the abstractions existed on `main` |
    | A snippet looked unmerged work | It was in no branch or PR, so it was in an agent's unpushed worktree |
    
    When a measurement surprises you, the next step is reading code, and when evidence contradicts something you already wrote, correct it in the document and say so.
    
    ### 3. Classify
    
    Map every finding to a pattern in the catalog (the catalog's README maps overlay categories to patterns), and give it these labels before it becomes work:
    
    - **External contract or ours.** Formats owned by others (a protocol spec, a library's API, a terminal standard, SQLite itself) are honored exactly. Formats both of whose ends you control change freely, in lockstep.
    - **Live or dead.** Dead code is deleted, never refactored.
    - **Legacy or innocent.** "Fallback" choosing the previous tab is innocent; a reader of an old format is legacy.
    - **Durable or runtime state,** which decides whether a store is reset at cutover or carried across once.
    - **Origin:** upstream or fork; refactor-created or feature-created.
    
    ### 4. Map surfaces
    
    - **Organize by owned concept, not by origin or file,** and at boundaries by boundary: decode-once happens where data enters.
    - **Run a crossing analysis:** which surfaces share files. Disjoint surfaces run in parallel; shared ones are sequenced, or the shared file gets one owner.
    - **Extract a shared abstraction only when several surfaces need the same mechanism** (roughly three or more instances). Reject candidates the evidence does not support, and say why. Each shared abstraction has exactly one builder, a wave, and a list of users; users request extensions from the builder and never fork it.
    - **Follow every family to its boundaries.** A family can own a fact perfectly inside its module and still be flattened into a string or booleans by the event, record or return value that carries it out (BOUND-8). Each consumer then re-decides the fact, and recurring fixes across consumers are the symptom. For every owned family, check what crosses its boundary.
    - **Enforce polymorphism codebase-wide, not only per surface.** A surface's guards protect that refactor's result and nothing else. Use the census's `string_dispatch` and `type_switch` to count candidate subjects, and `string_dispatch_arms` and `type_switch_arms` to catch growth within an existing candidate. All four use a three-distinct-arm threshold per function. Verify ownership at each site: syntax cannot distinguish an external taxonomy from a missing family. These counts are screening ratchets, not complete no-new-case guards; subthreshold cases and additions offset by removals can escape them. Enforce admitted ownership decisions with site-specific guards. Seal mechanisms that must not be adapted (TIME-9).
    - **Do not hide primitive switches in decorated methods.** `builtin_handler_type_switch` counts each dict/list/str/int/float/bool/tuple arm declared through the imported MroDispatch `handles` decorator, including a single arm on a method. It uses the same collector in the audit and receiving Core command. Only the canonical `field_codec.py` boundary is admitted; naming another module `*_codec.py` is not admission. Domain and Python AST classes are not primitive arms. Import aliases are read from the module AST; dynamic Python rebinding is outside this screening count's proof scope. PR421's real ACP failure source grows from zero to six such arms even though the older per-function type-switch counts do not catch that relocation.
    - **Order:** CI and the ratchet first when missing; then abstraction builders; then surfaces in parallel waves; god-class decomposition last, since other surfaces shrink those classes first.
    
    ### 5. Write the package
    
    Read `references/package-templates.md` and `references/rules-template.md`. A package holds:
    
    - `README.md`: contents and reading order;
    - `00-RULES.md`: the binding rules (from the template, with project specifics);
    - `01-INDEX.md`: evidence, surfaces, order, crossings, decisions with defaults;
    - `02-SHARED-ABSTRACTIONS.md` when two or more surfaces share mechanisms;
    - `03-COORDINATION.md`: agents, status line, cutover, decisions, the prompt addendum;
    - surface receipts, one per prompt, just in time.
    
    ### 6. Write surface receipts just in time
    
    Read `references/surface-receipt.md`. For each surface, at dispatch time:
    
    - **Re-measure at today's head.** If most of the surface already landed, write a short closure note instead of a full receipt, so no agent redoes finished work.
    - Fill the receipt: boundary, witnesses with file:line and numbers, findings (each citing its pattern ID), required questions, ownership, target sketch (the pattern's clean form, adapted), new-case experiments, migration, guards, tests, done-when, dispatch.
    - **Record every reassignment in the receiving surface's file,** not only in the one giving it away.
    - Update the index, run `check_package.py DIR --zip OUT.zip`, and fix every broken link and every disagreement between the abstraction table and surface headers before presenting.
    
    ### 7. Review progress, and close the loop
    
    Re-run the census and overlay at the new head against the last audited head, attribute changes by originating PR, and separate "the refactor worked where applied" from "new debt arrived elsewhere." Report both plainly, with production-code numbers.
    
    Then close the loop. **Any violation class seen twice becomes a mechanical check in the same review:** a ratchet measure, a sealed mechanism, or a guard. Agents follow the structure around them and route around prose, so whatever stays prose keeps eroding. Before shipping a new measure, **prove it tracks the violation on real history**: run it at the heads where the violation grew, and confirm it grew too. Plausible measures often don't (see principle 14).
    
    ## The rules every plan carries
    
    Summarized; the full text is in `references/rules-template.md`.
    
    1. **No backwards compatibility.** One format per thing; no converters, aliases, re-exports, fallbacks or "for now" paths. External contracts are honored exactly, which is correctness, not compatibility.
    2. **Hard cutover.** Runtime state is reset; durable state is carried across once by a tool outside `src/` that is deleted before the surface is done.
    3. **Delete aggressively,** including dead code on sight; report lines deleted first.
    4. **Finish the job.** Done means the guards pass with zero exceptions. Dual paths end with one path.

    class CoordinationStore(CarriedWriter, ReconciledFile):
        """Own SQLite read snapshots and the shared writer busy policy."""
    
        filename = "coordination.sqlite3"
        writer_timeout = 5.0
    
        @classmethod
        def table_schema(cls) -> type[CoordinatorTable]:
            return CoordinatorTable
    
        @staticmethod
        def writer(
            path: str | os.PathLike[str], contention: StoreContention = DEFAULT_STORE_CONTENTION,
            **options: object,
        ) -> sqlite3.Connection:
            """Open a writer through the store family's typed busy behavior."""
            return CoordinationStore.identifiers_only(contention.writer(path, options))
    
        @staticmethod
        def identifiers_only(db: sqlite3.Connection) -> sqlite3.Connection:
            """A double-quoted name is an identifier, never a string: a missing column fails
            as missing instead of reading back as a literal named after it."""
            for option in (sqlite3.SQLITE_DBCONFIG_DQS_DML, sqlite3.SQLITE_DBCONFIG_DQS_DDL):
                db.setconfig(option, False)
            return db
    
        @staticmethod
        def begin_snapshot(db: sqlite3.Connection) -> None:
            """Acquire one committed read revision before any consumer query."""
            db.execute("BEGIN")
            # BEGIN is lazy. Acquire the snapshot before schema decoders can
            # reclassify BUSY as unsupported data or absent rows.
            SQLiteTableName.read(db.execute("SELECT name FROM sqlite_master LIMIT 1"))
    
        @classmethod
        def _configure_reader(cls, db: sqlite3.Connection) -> sqlite3.Connection:
            try:
                cls.identifiers_only(db)
                db.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
                db.execute("PRAGMA query_only=ON")
                db.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON")
                return db
            except BaseException:
                db.close()
                raise
    
        @classmethod
        def _open_reader(
            cls, path: Path, contention: StoreContention
        ) -> sqlite3.Connection:
            return cls._configure_reader(
                contention.reader(path.resolve().as_uri() + "?mode=ro")
            )
    
        @classmethod
        def _acquire_snapshot(cls, db: sqlite3.Connection) -> sqlite3.Connection:
            try:
                cls.begin_snapshot(db)
                return db
            except BaseException:
                db.close()
                raise
    
        @classmethod
        def read_snapshot(
            cls, path: Path, contention: StoreContention = DEFAULT_STORE_CONTENTION
        ) -> sqlite3.Connection:
            """Open and acquire one consistent read-only snapshot with SQLite's busy handler."""
            return cls._acquire_snapshot(cls._open_reader(path, contention))
    
        @classmethod
        def recovering_snapshot(cls, path: Path) -> sqlite3.Connection:
            """Acquire evidence after SQLite is allowed to recover an existing hot journal."""
            uri = path.resolve().as_uri() + "?mode=rw"
            return cls._acquire_snapshot(cls._configure_reader(cls.writer(uri, uri=True)))
    
        @staticmethod
        @contextmanager
        def reading(
            path: Path, contention: StoreContention = DEFAULT_STORE_CONTENTION
        ):
            """Own a configured read connection whose consumers bound each snapshot."""
            with CoordinationReadUnavailable.checking():
                with closing(CoordinationStore._open_reader(path, contention)) as db:
                    yield db
    
        @staticmethod
        def observed(path: Path) -> StoreFile:
            """Never let a read-only SQLite open create a WAL shared-memory sidecar.
    
            WAL-mode SQLite can create -shm even when opened with mode=ro. Refuse such a
            database *before* opening SQLite; rollback-journal mode is the current
            coordinator configuration. Do not create directories, chmod, or recover a
            hot journal. A concurrent WAL conversion is outside this schema contract.
            """
    """SQLite connection and busy policy have one production owner."""
    
    import ast
    import asyncio
    import threading
    from pathlib import Path
    
    import pytest
    
    from agent_comms.coordination_database import CoordinationStore, StoreBusy
    from agent_comms.coordination_errors import CoordinationReadUnavailable
    from agent_comms.coordination_session import CoordinationSession, system_clock
    from agent_comms.coordinator import Coordination
    
    PACKAGE = Path(__file__).parents[1] / "src" / "agent_comms"
    CONNECTION_OWNER = PACKAGE / "coordination_database.py"
    
    
    def test_sqlite_connections_and_busy_policy_have_one_owner():
        direct_connections = []
        timeout_arguments = []
        for path in PACKAGE.rglob("*.py"):
            tree = ast.parse(path.read_text(), filename=str(path))
            for node in ast.walk(tree):
                if isinstance(node, ast.arg) and node.arg == "lock_timeout":
                    timeout_arguments.append(f"{path.relative_to(PACKAGE)}:{node.lineno}")
                if not isinstance(node, ast.Call):
                    continue
                if (
                    path != CONNECTION_OWNER
                    and isinstance(node.func, ast.Attribute)
                    and isinstance(node.func.value, ast.Name)
                    and node.func.value.id == "sqlite3"
                    and node.func.attr == "connect"
                ):
                    direct_connections.append(f"{path.relative_to(PACKAGE)}:{node.lineno}")
                if any(keyword.arg == "lock_timeout" for keyword in node.keywords):
                    timeout_arguments.append(f"{path.relative_to(PACKAGE)}:{node.lineno}")
        assert direct_connections == []
        assert timeout_arguments == []
    
    
    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_scoped_reader_releases_for_owner_commit(tmp_path):
        path = tmp_path / "coordination.sqlite3"
        with CoordinationStore(path):
            pass
        acquired = threading.Event()
        release = threading.Event()
    
        def read(store):
            with store.session.read():
                store.session._connection.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM participants").fetchone()
                acquired.set()
                assert release.wait(2)
    
        def commit(store):
            store.participants.register(
                "reader-release-owner", "Reader Release Owner", "owner-thread"
            )
    
        read_task = asyncio.create_task(Coordination.run_read_async(path, read))
        assert await asyncio.to_thread(acquired.wait, 2)
        write_task = asyncio.create_task(Coordination.run_async(path, commit))
        await asyncio.sleep(0.05)
        try:
            assert not write_task.done()
        finally:
            release.set()
        await asyncio.gather(read_task, write_task)
    
    
    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_nonwaiting_reader_reports_named_store_busy(tmp_path):
        path = tmp_path / "coordination.sqlite3"
        def read(store):
            with store.session.read():

        ):

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    @pytest.mark.parametrize("failing", [False, True])
    async def test_resident_operation_releases_unfinished_transactions(tmp_path, failing):
        path = tmp_path / "coordination.sqlite3"
        def unfinished(store):
            store.session._connection.execute("BEGIN")
            if failing:
                raise ValueError("callback failed")
        async with Coordination.worker(path):
            for run in (Coordination.run_async, Coordination.run_read_async):
                if failing:
                    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
                        await run(path, unfinished)
                else:
                    await run(path, unfinished)
                assert not await run(path, lambda store: store.session._connection.in_transaction)
    
    
    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_resident_cancellation_joins_operation_before_retirement(tmp_path):
        path = tmp_path / "coordination.sqlite3"
        begun, release, finished = threading.Event(), threading.Event(), threading.Event()
        def operation(store):
            begun.set()
            assert release.wait(2)
            store.participants.register("joined", "Joined", "joined")
            finished.set()
        async with Coordination.worker(path):
            pending = asyncio.create_task(Coordination.run_async(path, operation))
            assert await asyncio.to_thread(begun.wait, 2)
            pending.cancel()
            await asyncio.sleep(0)
            assert not pending.done()

        """
        import os

        from support.native import owner_server, start_private_native_wire
    
        os.environ["AGENT_COMMS_AGENT_MODELS"] = "openrouter/fake"
        comms = start_private_native_wire(workspace.roots.wire)
        owner = owner_server(comms)
        try:
            session = (await owner.new_session(cwd=str(workspace.project))).session_id
            async with workspace.app(size=size) as ui:
                agent = ui.detached_agent()
                agent.coordination = comms.configuration.answer(session)

                if arrange is not None:

                conversation = ui.conversation
                conversation.set_reactive(type(conversation).agent, agent)
                conversation.bind_agent(agent)
                conversation.agent_ready = True
                await conversation.goal_observation.refresh()
                await ui.step()
                yield ui, agent, owner, session, goal
        finally:
            await owner.shutdown()
            assert self.view.prompt._ask is None
            self.app.save_screenshot(str(self.root / "toad-disconnected.svg"))
