    ---
    name: refactor-audit
    description: Audit a codebase's structural debt by correct-maintenance (OpenHCS) standards and turn it into an aggressive, evidence-backed refactoring plan package that parallel agents can execute. Use this whenever the user wants to audit debt or slop, plan or coordinate a refactor, review a refactor's progress, compare a fork against its upstream, find legacy or compatibility code, measure whether new code is adding debt, write refactoring plans or per-surface documents for agents, or decide whether a codebase can be saved by refactoring, even if they never say "audit". Pairs with the nra-refactoring skill, which owns the per-decision ownership method; this skill owns measurement, surface mapping, plan packages and coordination.
    ---
    
    # Refactor audit
    
    Measure a codebase's structural debt, verify every finding in the code, map it into refactoring **surfaces**, and write a plan package that agents execute in parallel: binding rules, an index, shared abstractions, coordination, and one decision receipt per surface, written just in time.
    
    The per-decision method (census, required relation, owners, new-case test) belongs to the **nra-refactoring** skill; read it when writing receipts. This skill covers everything around it.
    
    **The pattern catalog (`references/patterns/`) is the heart of this skill.** It shows 43 antipatterns that agents produce by default, each as real slop beside its clean polymorphic form: what fact the code forces its reader to supply, which rung is broken (identity, membership, implementation), how families, capabilities composed by multiple inheritance, and derived single sources of truth collapse the duplication, and how many edits a new case needs before and after. Read its README before classifying findings, and cite pattern IDs in every receipt.
    
    ## Why the method looks like this
    
    - **The codebase is the prompt.** Agents copy the code around them far more than they follow instructions. Two versions of one mechanism in the tree teach the next agent whichever has more call sites, usually the old one. So the plans delete aggressively and build exemplars; instructions alone never win against the majority of the tree.
    - **Numbers lie in specific, repeatable ways.** A parser that can't read some files skips them silently. A file that "stopped churning" may have moved to another repo. A module named like a feature may be refactor output. Every surprising number is checked in the code before it is written down, and a wrong claim is corrected plainly the moment evidence contradicts it.
    - **The owner's attention is the scarcest resource.** Plans batch every owner-level question with a default, run peer to peer with no coordinator agent, and report status in one line.
    
    ## Workflow
    
    ### 0. Orient
    
    - Fetch and pin the heads you audit (`git fetch`, note the SHA and the PR number). Every document names its head, because `main` moves under plans quickly.
    - List open PRs and the files they touch; they block or collide with surfaces.
    - Check what CI exists. A repository with none gets a CI surface first.
    - Find the project's Python (`requires-python`) and run every script with it: `uv python install 3.x`, then `uv run --python 3.x …` or the interpreter `uv python find 3.x` prints.
    - For a fork, find its upstream and the merge-base; note whether upstream still moves.
    
    ### 1. Measure
    
    Run from the target repository (scripts are in this skill's `scripts/`):
    
    ```
    debt_census.py --repo . --root src/pkg                                  # snapshot
    debt_census.py --repo . --root src/pkg --base <old-sha>                 # what changed since
    debt_census.py --repo . --root src/pkg --upstream upstream/main --exclude tools/   # fork versus upstream
    overlay.py     --repo . --root src/pkg [--upstream upstream/main]       # what NRA cannot see
    attribute_origin.py --repo . --root src/pkg --since <old-sha> --foundation src/pkg/<abstraction>.py
    merge_review.py --repo . --root src/pkg --since <old-sha>                # the debt each merged PR added
    ```
    
    - **`debt_census.py`** reports densities per 1,000 code lines. The headline is `type(x) is` checks + boolean chains of four or more + string-keyed subscripts. `boolean_chain_terms` weighs each chain by its terms, so one eleven-term validity check counts eleven, not one. The overlay classifies the syntax of every term of every long chain and reports the dominant kind as an ownership lead, not a diagnosis. Predicate calls may already query the correct owner; inspect their declarations before choosing a target. Use `--exclude` for debugging scripts: they are not product code.
    - **`overlay.py`** finds string dispatch, `isinstance` switches, raw record shapes (and whether an existing class already models them), hand-written exact key-set checks, attribute access by name, god classes and functions, repeated literal sets, legacy markers, dead modules, positional inserts, JavaScript embedded in strings, and child-process sites. With `--upstream`, each finding is tagged with its origin.
    - **`merge_review.py`** measures every merged pull request since a revision, after minus before over the files it changed, and lists the merges that added the most debt and every merge that added dispatch. Use it for progress reviews and to find cleanup targets: a merge that added candidate debt is a cleanup plan's first witness. Parse failures name the merge and file, withhold rankings, and exit nonzero; never treat an incomplete review as zero debt.
    - **`attribute_origin.py`** classifies new modules by the pull request that created them, which is the only reliable way to say who introduced debt and whether it predates the abstractions it should use.
    - **Every script warns when files fail to parse.** Treat that warning as a stop: re-run with the right Python.
    - The scripts are themselves written to the catalog's standard (measures, findings, checks and modes are families in `scripts/audit/`). When you extend them, add a class; never add a branch. `references/patterns/agent-defaults.md` (AGENT-8) shows what their first version looked like, and why tooling is not exempt.
    
    Then run NRA's complete scan with the same Python (`python -m nominal_refactor_advisor src/pkg --json`) and confirm `complete: true` and zero omitted detectors. NRA keys on declared families, so a codebase that keeps its states in strings, booleans and `None` shows few findings; that is a blind spot, not health. The overlay covers it.
    
    ### 2. Verify before writing anything down
    
    Read the code behind every number you intend to state. Real corrections this method has produced:
    
    | The number said | The code showed |
    |---|---|
    | A god file dropped to 0% churn after a refactor | It moved to another repository through five paths; its churn followed it |
    | A child is killed with SIGKILL only, so descendants leak | It runs as PID 1 in a PID namespace; the whole tree dies |
    | Two compaction pipelines, so one is a copy | Different performers, authorities and records: two operations |
    | Modules named per phase, so a lifecycle split by phase | Pipeline roles in sound layers; the lifecycle was already a state family |
    | New modules are dense, so agents ignore the rules | 37 of 39 were written before the abstractions existed on `main` |
    | A snippet looked unmerged work | It was in no branch or PR, so it was in an agent's unpushed worktree |
    
    When a measurement surprises you, the next step is reading code, and when evidence contradicts something you already wrote, correct it in the document and say so.
    
    ### 3. Classify
    
    Map every finding to a pattern in the catalog (the catalog's README maps overlay categories to patterns), and give it these labels before it becomes work:
    
    - **External contract or ours.** Formats owned by others (a protocol spec, a library's API, a terminal standard, SQLite itself) are honored exactly. Formats both of whose ends you control change freely, in lockstep.
    - **Live or dead.** Dead code is deleted, never refactored.
    - **Legacy or innocent.** "Fallback" choosing the previous tab is innocent; a reader of an old format is legacy.
    - **Durable or runtime state,** which decides whether a store is reset at cutover or carried across once.
    - **Origin:** upstream or fork; refactor-created or feature-created.
    
    ### 4. Map surfaces
    
    - **Organize by owned concept, not by origin or file,** and at boundaries by boundary: decode-once happens where data enters.
    - **Run a crossing analysis:** which surfaces share files. Disjoint surfaces run in parallel; shared ones are sequenced, or the shared file gets one owner.
    - **Extract a shared abstraction only when several surfaces need the same mechanism** (roughly three or more instances). Reject candidates the evidence does not support, and say why. Each shared abstraction has exactly one builder, a wave, and a list of users; users request extensions from the builder and never fork it.
    - **Follow every family to its boundaries.** A family can own a fact perfectly inside its module and still be flattened into a string or booleans by the event, record or return value that carries it out (BOUND-8). Each consumer then re-decides the fact, and recurring fixes across consumers are the symptom. For every owned family, check what crosses its boundary.
    - **Enforce polymorphism codebase-wide, not only per surface.** A surface's guards protect that refactor's result and nothing else. Use the census's `string_dispatch` and `type_switch` to count candidate subjects, and `string_dispatch_arms` and `type_switch_arms` to catch growth within an existing candidate. All four use a three-distinct-arm threshold per function. Verify ownership at each site: syntax cannot distinguish an external taxonomy from a missing family. These counts are screening ratchets, not complete no-new-case guards; subthreshold cases and additions offset by removals can escape them. Enforce admitted ownership decisions with site-specific guards. Seal mechanisms that must not be adapted (TIME-9).
    - **Do not hide primitive switches in decorated methods.** `builtin_handler_type_switch` counts each dict/list/str/int/float/bool/tuple arm declared through the imported MroDispatch `handles` decorator, including a single arm on a method. It uses the same collector in the audit and receiving Core command. Only the canonical `field_codec.py` boundary is admitted; naming another module `*_codec.py` is not admission. Domain and Python AST classes are not primitive arms. Import aliases are read from the module AST; dynamic Python rebinding is outside this screening count's proof scope. PR421's real ACP failure source grows from zero to six such arms even though the older per-function type-switch counts do not catch that relocation.
    - **Order:** CI and the ratchet first when missing; then abstraction builders; then surfaces in parallel waves; god-class decomposition last, since other surfaces shrink those classes first.
    
    ### 5. Write the package
    
    Read `references/package-templates.md` and `references/rules-template.md`. A package holds:
    
    - `README.md`: contents and reading order;
    - `00-RULES.md`: the binding rules (from the template, with project specifics);
    - `01-INDEX.md`: evidence, surfaces, order, crossings, decisions with defaults;
    - `02-SHARED-ABSTRACTIONS.md` when two or more surfaces share mechanisms;
    - `03-COORDINATION.md`: agents, status line, cutover, decisions, the prompt addendum;
    - surface receipts, one per prompt, just in time.
    
    ### 6. Write surface receipts just in time
    
    Read `references/surface-receipt.md`. For each surface, at dispatch time:
    
    - **Re-measure at today's head.** If most of the surface already landed, write a short closure note instead of a full receipt, so no agent redoes finished work.
    - Fill the receipt: boundary, witnesses with file:line and numbers, findings (each citing its pattern ID), required questions, ownership, target sketch (the pattern's clean form, adapted), new-case experiments, migration, guards, tests, done-when, dispatch.
    - **Record every reassignment in the receiving surface's file,** not only in the one giving it away.
    - Update the index, run `check_package.py DIR --zip OUT.zip`, and fix every broken link and every disagreement between the abstraction table and surface headers before presenting.
    
    ### 7. Review progress, and close the loop
    
    Re-run the census and overlay at the new head against the last audited head, attribute changes by originating PR, and separate "the refactor worked where applied" from "new debt arrived elsewhere." Report both plainly, with production-code numbers.
    
    Then close the loop. **Any violation class seen twice becomes a mechanical check in the same review:** a ratchet measure, a sealed mechanism, or a guard. Agents follow the structure around them and route around prose, so whatever stays prose keeps eroding. Before shipping a new measure, **prove it tracks the violation on real history**: run it at the heads where the violation grew, and confirm it grew too. Plausible measures often don't (see principle 14).
    
    ## The rules every plan carries
    
    Summarized; the full text is in `references/rules-template.md`.
    
    1. **No backwards compatibility.** One format per thing; no converters, aliases, re-exports, fallbacks or "for now" paths. External contracts are honored exactly, which is correctness, not compatibility.
    2. **Hard cutover.** Runtime state is reset; durable state is carried across once by a tool outside `src/` that is deleted before the surface is done.
    3. **Delete aggressively,** including dead code on sight; report lines deleted first.
    4. **Finish the job.** Done means the guards pass with zero exceptions. Dual paths end with one path.
    5. **Tests protect behaviour, not structure.** Delete tests of deleted code; one test per family; golden tests only for external contracts; never weaken an assertion. Busy work is fake work.
    6. **Guards are the definition of done,** run by a fast required CI check.
    
    ## Writing the documents
    
    - Plain and specific: numbers, file paths, line numbers, the head audited. State results at their actual strength; do not hedge real findings or inflate weak ones.
    - **Scope once, then commit.** One paragraph in the README says what exists and what does not. Everywhere else a design is stated as the design, a finding with its evidence, an unknown as a decision with a default. Repeated disclaimers ("provisional", "not independently verified", "do not claim") are underclaiming, an error of the same class as overclaiming; `check_package.py`'s hedge check lists them for review, not automatic rejection. Preserve concrete uncertainty and evidence limits.
    - Explain the reason for each rule and target; agents apply reasons to cases the text does not name.
    - Imperative voice for instructions. No em dashes, no marketing cadence.
    - Keep genuinely open questions only when the domain or the owner must answer; give every owner question a default so a one-word reply suffices.
    
    ## Tool regression checks
    
    Run `python -m unittest discover -s <skill-directory>/tests -v` with the project's Python before changing the audit scripts. The tests cover dispatch growth and removal, valid owner predicates, and fail-closed merge reviews. Rebuild the `.skill` archive from the same source after they pass.
    
    ## Reference files
    
    - `references/patterns/README.md`, then the file for each rung you meet: the catalog of antipatterns and their clean forms, with real code. **Read before classifying findings and before every receipt.**
    - `references/rules-template.md`: the binding rules, ready to adapt. Read when writing `00-RULES.md`.
    - `references/package-templates.md`: README, index, shared abstractions and coordination templates, including the status line, cutover procedure, decision batch and prompt addendum. Read when writing the package.
    - `references/surface-receipt.md`: the receipt template, the closure-note variant, and a worked example. Read before every surface.
    - `references/principles.md`: the lessons behind the method, with the evidence for each. Read when a situation is not covered above, or when a finding does not fit a category.

    # Owner decisions
    
    ## 2026-10-14 — No lock held across a decode; readers never block
    
    Tristan: "why do we have so many issues wit hdecoding large fiel enirely over and over again and holding locks ofr not raso nits fuckign stupid, awwe want async not hodlign locks when it doesn' needto happen and deconding shit unecessarily"
    
    Witness: 10:52-10:57 every agent and CLI waited on
    `.bus_route_counts.sqlite3.lock` while one `watch` reader rebuilt the route
    projection from the whole 3.7 GB bus inside `BusRouteCounts.sync`.
    
    A reader never takes an exclusive lock. Readers of an append-only file read
    committed bytes up to a captured size; readers of SQLite use WAL snapshots.
    A writer holds its lock only to capture a cut or commit a bounded result,
    never across decoding, scanning or I/O proportional to file size: decode
    outside the lock, then commit with a revision check. Durable state that is
    rewritten whole on each change (a JSON file of all rows) is a defect; it is
    appended or keyed so a change costs its own size. Waiting for a lock is
    async in owners and never stalls an event loop.
    
    ## 2026-10-14 — Constant cost: nothing scales with history size or throughput
    
    Tristan: "it shuold decode from latest to oldest or jsut decode what it needs so that tis always fast and doesn't get longer with theard size"
    
    Tristan: "that shoudl eb the philslophy iwth comms and its Iu impelmeantaions, nothing scales with size or throuhgput, we keep everythign cosntant costs as much as possible"
    
    Core and every UI over it keep per-operation cost constant. Opening, switching,
    scrolling, sending and status updates do work bounded by what is shown or
    changed, never by thread length, bus length or message rate. Read newest to
    oldest and decode only the fields the current viewport needs. Aggregates
    (unread, activity, counts) are maintained incrementally by their owner when
    the source changes; readers take the current value. A walk to an unbounded
    ancestor, a full-bus scan or a decode-then-re-encode on a read path is a
    defect. Acceptance for performance work compares a short and the longest
    thread or bus on the same build: the costs must match.

    class Workspace:
        """Everything a test of the running app starts from."""
    
        def __init__(self, roots: Roots) -> None:
            from agent_comms.launch_root import LaunchRoot
    
            self.roots = roots
            self.project = roots.project
            self.project.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            LaunchRoot.from_path(roots.wire).install()
    
        @cached_property
        def comms(self) -> Comms:
            """The test's own wire, as Core serves it."""
            from agent_comms.comms import wire
    
            return wire(self.roots.wire)
    
        @property
        def viewer(self) -> str:
            """The name the user of this project sends as."""
            return self.comms.messaging.user_identity(str(self.project)).name
    
        def thread(self, name: str, *tags: str, running: bool = False, title: str | None = None):
            """Declare a thread on the wire; a running thread is owned by this process."""
            from agent_comms.child_process import NoProcess, ProcessIdentity
            from agent_comms.thread_text import ThreadText
    
            identity = ProcessIdentity.capture(os.getpid()) if running else NoProcess()
            self.comms.registry.declare(self.comms.registry.new_thread(
                name, frozenset(tags), str(self.project), title=ThreadText.external(title), process_identity=identity))
            return self.comms.registry.require(name)
    
        def child_processes(self, marker: str) -> list:
            """This test's live child processes whose command line mentions `marker`."""
            import psutil
    
            found = []
            for process in psutil.Process().children(recursive=True):
                try:
                    if process.status() != psutil.STATUS_ZOMBIE and any(marker in part for part in process.cmdline()):
                        found.append(process)
                except psutil.NoSuchProcess:
                    continue
            return found
    
        def received(self) -> list[dict]:
            """Everything the scripted agent recorded, oldest first (see ``support/peers/base.py``)."""
            import json
    
            record = self.project / "peer-received.jsonl"
            return [json.loads(line) for line in record.read_text().splitlines()] if record.exists() else []
    
        def release(self, name: str) -> None:
            """Let the scripted agent past its ``{"wait": name}`` step."""
            (self.project / f"released-{name}").touch()
    
        def steps_done(self) -> list[dict]:
            """The steps the scripted agent has finished, in order."""
            return [fact["done"] for fact in self.received() if "done" in fact]
    
        def prompts_received(self) -> list[str]:
            return [fact["prompt"] for fact in self.received() if "prompt" in fact]
    
        @cached_property
        def agents(self) -> AppAgents:
            return AppAgents.unrun(self.project)
    
        @asynccontextmanager
        async def app(self, *, size: tuple[int, int] = (120, 40), agent: AgentDefinition | None = None,
                      application: type | None = None, session: bool = True, resume: str | None = None):
            """Start Toad headless on this project; yields once its first session is shown.
    
            Toad itself starts with no tab open unless the launch names a session
            to resume (``resume``); ``session=False`` yields what it started with.
            """
            from toad.app import ToadApp
    
            launch = {} if resume is None else {"agent_session_id": resume}
            app = (application or ToadApp)(agent_data=agent, project_dir=str(self.project), **launch)
            async with app.run_test(size=size) as pilot:
                ui = TextualUi(app, pilot)
                if session:
                    if not app.session_navigation.members:
                        await ui.new_session()
                    await app.selected_session.wait_content_ready()
                await ui.step()
                yield ui
                if (error := ui.failure()) is not None:
                    raise error

    """The process root chosen at startup and handed to child processes."""
    
    from __future__ import annotations
    
    from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
    from collections.abc import Callable, Iterator, Mapping
    from contextlib import contextmanager
    from dataclasses import dataclass
    from pathlib import Path
    from typing import Annotated, ClassVar, Self
    
    from .errors import RelationViolationError

    class LaunchSelection(ABC):
        """The current selection owns its scoped installation and root requirement."""
    
        @abstractmethod
        def require(self) -> LaunchRoot: ...
    
        def install(self) -> None:
            LaunchRoot._current = self
    
        @contextmanager
        def selected(self) -> Iterator[Self]:
            previous = LaunchRoot._current
            self.install()
            try:
                yield self
            finally:
                previous.install()
    
    
    class UnstartedLaunch(LaunchSelection):
        """A process with no selected root; startup must run before use."""
    
        def require(self) -> LaunchRoot:
            raise RelationViolationError("Comms process did not select a root at startup.")
    
    
    @dataclass(frozen=True)
    class LaunchRoot(LaunchSelection):
        """A process's selected root travels in its arguments, never its environment."""
    
        path: Annotated[Path, PathText]
        argument: ClassVar[str] = "--comms-root"
        environment_name: ClassVar[str] = "AGENT_COMMS_ROOT"
        _current: ClassVar[LaunchSelection] = UnstartedLaunch()
    
        @classmethod
        def from_path(cls, path: str | Path) -> LaunchRoot:
            """Capture cwd/home now; keep symlinks for private-root validation."""
            return cls(Path(path).expanduser().absolute())
    
        @classmethod
        def unstarted(cls) -> UnstartedLaunch:
            return UnstartedLaunch()
    
        @classmethod
        def current(cls) -> LaunchRoot:
            return cls._current.require()
    
        def require(self) -> LaunchRoot:
            return self
    
        def arguments(self) -> tuple[str, str]:
            return self.argument, str(self.path)
    
        @classmethod
        def startup(cls, arguments: list[str], published: Callable[[], LaunchRoot]) -> None:
            if cls.argument in arguments:
                index = arguments.index(cls.argument)
                if index + 1 == len(arguments):
                    raise ValueError(f"{cls.argument} requires a root")
                record = FieldCodec.decode(cls, {"path": arguments[index + 1]})
                cls.from_path(record.path).install()
                del arguments[index : index + 2]
            else:
                published().install()
    
        @classmethod
        def environment(cls, source: Mapping[str, str]) -> dict[str, str]:
            """Construct child inheritance without an ambient root override."""
            return {name: value for name, value in source.items() if name != cls.environment_name}

        @classmethod
        def read_snapshot(
            cls, path: Path, contention: StoreContention = DEFAULT_STORE_CONTENTION
        ) -> sqlite3.Connection:
            """Open and acquire one consistent read-only snapshot with SQLite's busy handler."""
            return cls._acquire_snapshot(cls._open_reader(path, contention))
    
        @classmethod
        def recovering_snapshot(cls, path: Path) -> sqlite3.Connection:
            """Acquire evidence after SQLite is allowed to recover an existing hot journal."""
            uri = path.resolve().as_uri() + "?mode=rw"
            return cls._acquire_snapshot(cls._configure_reader(cls.writer(uri, uri=True)))
    
        @classmethod
        @contextmanager
        def observing(
            cls, path: Path, contention: StoreContention = DEFAULT_STORE_CONTENTION
        ):
            """Read existing committed data without initializing storage or permitting writes."""
            with CoordinationReadUnavailable.checking():
                try:
                    with closing(cls.read_snapshot(path, contention)) as db:
                        try:
                            yield db
                        finally:
                            if db.in_transaction:
                                db.execute("ROLLBACK")
                except sqlite3.OperationalError as error:
                    error.add_note(
                        f"SQLite observation store: {path}; "
                        f"SQLite error: {error.sqlite_errorname} ({error.sqlite_errorcode})"
                    )
                    raise
    
        @classmethod
        def is_database(cls, path: Path) -> bool:
            with path.open("rb") as stream:
                return stream.read(len(cls.header)) == cls.header
    
        @classmethod
        def copy_file(cls, source: str | Path, target: str | Path) -> Path:
            """Copy a committed SQLite snapshot, excluding uncommitted companion bytes."""
            source, target = Path(source), Path(target)
            with (closing(cls.read_snapshot(source)) as original,
                  closing(cls.writer(target)) as copied):
                original.backup(copied)
            shutil.copystat(source, target)
            return target
    
        @classmethod
        def digest(cls, path: Path) -> str:
            """Hash a consistent SQLite schema and row dump, including committed WAL data."""
            with closing(cls.read_snapshot(path)) as database:
                content = hashlib.sha256()
                for statement in database.iterdump():
                    content.update(statement.encode())
                return content.hexdigest()
    
        @classmethod
        def files(cls, path: Path) -> tuple[Path, ...]:
            return (path, *(path.with_name(path.name + suffix) for suffix in cls.companion_suffixes))
    
        @classmethod
        def member_paths(cls, path: Path) -> frozenset[Path]:
            return super().member_paths(path) | frozenset((
                *cls.files(path), StoreOwner.snapshot_lock(path), StoreOwner.snapshot_intent(path),
            ))
    
        @classmethod
        def _begin_transaction(cls, connection: sqlite3.Connection) -> None:
            connection.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
    
        @classmethod
        @contextmanager
        def write_transaction(cls, connection: sqlite3.Connection) -> Iterator[sqlite3.Connection]:
            """The one write transaction: committed when the block returns, rolled back when it raises."""
            cls._begin_transaction(connection)
            try:
                yield connection
                connection.execute("COMMIT")
            except BaseException:
                if connection.in_transaction:
                    connection.execute("ROLLBACK")

        """A home holding what an installed machine has: the installer's uv, and as the
        installed runtime a build of the merge base this change lands on. Both cases share
        it, so the second reuses the staged runtime the first built, as a second install
        would. Package caches stay shared."""
        home = tmp_path_factory.mktemp("installed-home")
        uv = home / ".local/state/agent-comms/upgrade-bus/uv"
        uv.parent.mkdir(parents=True)
        uv.symlink_to(TestHome(home).uv)
        caches = subprocess.run([uv, "cache", "dir"], check=True, capture_output=True, text=True)
        environment = {**os.environ, "HOME": str(home), "UV_CACHE_DIR": caches.stdout.strip(),
                       "npm_config_cache": str(Path.home() / ".npm")}
        environment.pop("PYTHONPATH", None)
        # The checkout owner adds the tree with its pinned submodules; `git archive` drops them.
        base = ScratchCheckout.add(REPOSITORY, home / "outgoing-source",

        try:
            outgoing = Stack.build(base.path, InstallCommands(), home)
        finally:
            base.retire()

            outgoing.runtime.prefix, target_is_directory=True)
        return environment

        return checkout
    
    
    def drop_one_index(root: Path) -> None:
        """One declared store's schema drifts from both runtimes' declarations."""
        for path in sorted(ReconciledFile.existing_in(root)):
            with closing(sqlite3.connect(path)) as db:
                index = db.execute("SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='index'"

                if index:
                    db.execute(f'DROP INDEX "{index[0]}"')
                    db.commit()
                    return
        raise AssertionError("No declared store has an index to drop")

    """One coalesced read lifetime; each projection owns its source and reaction."""
    from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
    import asyncio
    from weakref import ref
    
    from agent_comms.goal_presentation import GoalSnapshot
    from agent_comms.ui_model.delivery import InputDelivery
    from agent_comms.ui_model.goal import GoalUnavailable
    from toad.agent_binding import NoAgentBound
    
    
    class SessionObservation(ABC):
        errors = (OSError, ValueError)
    
        def __init__(self, view):
            self._view = ref(view)
            self.revision = 0
            self.task = None
            self.agent = NoAgentBound()
    
        @property
        def view(self):
            return self._view() if self._view is not None else None
    
        @property
        def active(self):
            return self.task is not None and not self.task.done()
    
        def invalidate(self):
            view = self.view
            if view is None or not view.is_attached:
                return
            view.agent_binding.invalidate_observation(self)
    
        def schedule(self, agent):
            self.agent = agent
            self.revision += 1
            if not self.active:
                self.task = asyncio.create_task(self._run())
    
        async def refresh(self):
            self.invalidate()
            task = self.task
            if task is not None:
                try:
                    await asyncio.shield(task)
                except asyncio.CancelledError:
                    # Source retirement owns cancellation of its read. A callback
                    # awaiting that read must not cancel the retained UI pump.
                    if self.view is None and task.cancelled() and not asyncio.current_task().cancelling():
                        return
                    raise
    
        async def close(self):
            self._view = None
            self.revision += 1
            if self.active:
                self.task.cancel()
                await asyncio.gather(self.task, return_exceptions=True)
            self.task = None
            self.agent = NoAgentBound()
    
        @staticmethod
        async def close_all(*observations: "SessionObservation") -> None:
            """Join every independent observation before reporting close failures."""
            results = await asyncio.gather(
                *(observation.close() for observation in observations), return_exceptions=True,
            )
            errors = [result for result in results if isinstance(result, BaseException)]
            if errors:
                raise BaseExceptionGroup("Session observations failed to close", errors)
    
        def receive(self, agent, result):
            """An owner fact supersedes an older in-flight read of that source."""
            view = self.view
            if view is None or not view.is_attached or not view.agent_binding.matches_agent(agent):
                return
            self.revision += 1
            self.publish(view, result)
    
        async def _run(self):
            while (view := self.view) is not None and view.is_attached:
                revision = self.revision
                agent = self.agent
                try:
                    result = await self.read(agent)
                except self.errors as error:
                    if self.view is not view or not view.is_attached:
                        return
                    if revision != self.revision or not view.agent_binding.matches_agent(agent):
                        continue
                    self.failed(view, error)
                    return
                if self.view is not view or not view.is_attached:
                    return
                if revision != self.revision or not view.agent_binding.matches_agent(agent):
                    continue
                self.publish(view, result)
                return
    
        @abstractmethod
        async def read(self, agent): ...
    
        @abstractmethod
        def publish(self, view, result): ...
    
        @abstractmethod
        def failed(self, view, error): ...
    
    
    class GoalObservation(SessionObservation):
        async def read(self, agent) -> GoalSnapshot:
            return await agent.get_goal_snapshot()
    
        def publish(self, view, result: GoalSnapshot):
            view.goal_display = result.goal
            view.goal_execution = result.execution
    
        def failed(self, view, error):
            view.goal_display = GoalUnavailable(view.goal_display.snapshot)
    
    
    class InputDeliveryObservation(SessionObservation):
        errors = (OSError, ValueError, RuntimeError, TimeoutError, KeyError)

                self.prompt_in_flight -= 1

                    self.start_operation(self.reconcile_turn(coordination, authority))
    
        async def reconcile_turn(self, coordination, authority):
            """Release snapshot ordering through a fresh read of the same owner."""
            self.require_owner(coordination, authority)
            await self.agent.thread_read().reconcile(self.transcripts)
    
        def accepts_turn_snapshot(self, sequence):
            """A remote busy turn does not imply an ordered response on this client."""
            return (self.prompt_in_flight == 0
                    and sequence == self.agent.presentation.turns.sequence)
    
        async def _submit(self, prompt, command, authority, queue_scope, project):
            submission = asyncio.current_task() if command.defer_display else None
            if submission is not None:
                self._deferred_submissions.add(submission)
            try:
                coordination = self.coordination
                if coordination is not None:
                    self.require_owner(coordination, authority)
                    async with self.transcripts.bind(coordination.wire_root) as comms:
                        origin = await asyncio.to_thread(
                            self.agent.queue_attachment.capture_human_input, comms, queue_scope)
                    self.require_owner(coordination, authority)
                    command = replace(command, origin=origin)
                content = await asyncio.to_thread(build_prompt, project, prompt)
                if any(block.type == 'image' for block in content):
                    coordinated = self.coordination is not None
                    supported = coordinated or self.agent.session.supports_images
                    if not supported:
                        raise ValueError('This agent owner does not support images yet; refresh it while idle.')
                return await self._prompt(content, command, authority, queue_scope)
            finally:
                if submission is not None:
                    self._deferred_submissions.discard(submission)
    
        async def submit_blocks(self, content, command=None):
            agent = self.agent
            authority = ClientSessionRequest(agent, agent.session_id)
            return await self.operate(self._prompt_operation(partial(self._prompt,
                content, command, authority, agent.queue_attachment.scope), authority))
    
        async def _prompt(self, content, command, authority, queue_scope):
            agent = self.agent
    
            def require():
                authority.require()
                if not agent.queue_attachment.accepts_request(queue_scope):
                    raise ValueError('The queued input owner changed before submission; inspect the current queue.')
    
            try:
                result = await agent.process.prompt(agent, content,
                    encode_request(command) if command is not None else {}, require)
            except RequestError as error:
                request_failure = RequestFailure.from_error(error)
            except OSError as error:
                request_failure = RequestFailure(
                    ACPFailure.from_detail(None, f"{type(error).__name__}: {error}"), False)
            else:
                if authority.retired:
                    return None
                return StopReason.member_named(result.stop_reason)
            if authority.retired:
                return None
            failure = request_failure.failure
            self._prompt_failed(command, authority, queue_scope, failure,
                failure.title, failure.feedback, published=request_failure.notification_published)
            return None
    
        def _prompt_failed(self, command, authority, queue_scope, failure, title, detail, *, published=False):
            agent = self.agent
            user_text = command.draft_text if command is not None else None
            if user_text:
                agent.events.publish(core_events.CommsUpdated(InputFailedUpdate(user_text, failure), recover_draft=True, session_id=authority.session_id, queue_scope=queue_scope))
            if not published:
                agent.session.record_failure(
                    LogAgentFail(title, detail, log_path=agent.presentation.log_path))
    
        async def clear_queue(self):
            await self.submit_blocks([{'type': 'text', 'text': ' '}], ClearQueueRequest())
    
        async def send_now(self):
            authority = ClientSessionRequest(self.agent, self.agent.session_id)
            queue_scope = self.agent.queue_attachment.scope
            if pending := tuple(self._deferred_submissions):
                await asyncio.gather(*(asyncio.shield(task) for task in pending))
            return await self.operate(self._prompt_operation(partial(self._prompt,
                [{'type': 'text', 'text': ' '}], SendNowRequest(), authority, queue_scope), authority)) is not None
    
        async def compact_context(self, instructions=None):
            authority = ClientSessionRequest(self.agent, self.agent.session_id)
            return await self.operate(self._prompt_operation(partial(self._compact_context,
                instructions, authority), authority))
    
        async def _compact_context(self, instructions, authority):
            agent = self.agent
            try:
                response = await agent.process.prompt(agent, [{'type': 'text', 'text': ' '}],
                    encode_request(CompactRequest(instructions)), authority.require)
            except RequestError as error:
                failure = ACPFailure.from_error(error)
                raise ValueError(f'{failure.title}: {failure.detail}\n{failure.input_disposition}\n{failure.action}') from error
            authority.require()

    class Stack:
        """One built installation and the source checkout containing its install tools."""
    
        checkout: Path
        commands: InstallCommands
        home: Path = HOME
        runtime: LaunchRuntime = field(default_factory=LaunchRuntime.installed)
    
        @property
        def python(self) -> Path:
            return self.runtime.interpreter
    
        @property
        def lock(self) -> Path:
            return self.checkout / "stack/uv.lock"
    
        @property
        def uv(self) -> Path:
            """The uv the installer runs, kept in the installer's own state."""
            return RuntimeHome.uv_path(self.home)
    
        def require_uv(self) -> None:
            if not os.access(self.uv, os.X_OK):
                raise UpgradeRefused(f"No uv executable at {self.uv}; the installer runs only that uv")
    
        @classmethod
        def build(cls, checkout: Path, commands: InstallCommands, home: Path = HOME) -> Stack:
            """Resolve current mains once, then build or reuse their immutable installation."""
            Checkout(checkout).prepare()
            source = cls(checkout, commands, home, runtime=LaunchRuntime.running())
            source.require_uv()
            commands.run(source.uv, "lock", "--project", "stack", "--upgrade", "--python", "3.14",
                         cwd=checkout)
            core = commands.run("git", "-C", checkout, "rev-parse", "HEAD").strip()
            resolution = hashlib.sha256(source.lock.read_bytes()).hexdigest()[:16]
            prefix = home / ".local/share/agent-comms/runtimes" / f"core-{core[:9]}-lock-{resolution}"
            built = replace(source, runtime=LaunchRuntime(prefix / "bin/python"))
            if prefix.exists():
                if not RuntimeResolution.at(prefix).matches(source.lock, built.python, core, commands):
                    raise UpgradeRefused("Existing built runtime differs from its resolved inputs")
                return built
            prefix.parent.mkdir(mode=0o700, parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            prefix.mkdir(mode=0o700)
            try:
                commands.run(source.uv, "sync", "--project", "stack", "--locked", "--python", "3.14",
                             "--no-editable", cwd=checkout,
                             env={**built.environment(), "UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT": str(prefix)})
                built.install_native()
                RuntimeResolution.capture(built.python, core, commands).save(prefix)
                built.imports()
            except BaseException:
                shutil.rmtree(prefix)
                raise
            return built
    
        def test(self, *pytest_arguments: str) -> None:
            """Run checkout tests against this runtime's installed packages, never its source."""

    # The harness: make commanding playable again
    
    Decision (Tristan, 2026-10-21 22:45): the commander fixes the harness it commands with. It works with full authority on this plan only: it makes each change, inspects it with full attention, runs only the tests the change touches, and pushes straight to `main`. Audited against `origin/main` at `39fdfe810`.
    
    ## Why
    
    On 2026-10-21 the plans Tristan asked for at 18:30 the day before had not landed 28 hours later. Every error pulled the fleet off them, and the errors came from the harness itself:
    
    - Install 52 sat for twenty minutes holding the wire lock and waiting on the registry lock (`maintenance_barrier.py:380`, `store_files.py:157`), sleeping in short naps and never naming the holder. The live coordination store was found malformed in the same minute the install was stopped.
    - "May I write during an install" had five answers: the maintenance barrier, a transcript lock, a connector stop, a bridge watch stop, and the commander's shell wrapper around `agent-comms install`. Each install failed on a different missing one.
    - One commander verb took one to five minutes under load. About 4.8 seconds of each call was import alone (2,093 dataclass builds, 433 pydantic models), and the answer gate then scanned the bus.
    - Failures were silent. The bridge watch crashed when the socket moved during the install (`cli_bridges/monitor.py:260`, FileNotFoundError). The session relay would not restart ("Session bridge startup not observed ... No launch retry"). Commander writes hung until a timeout killed them, with no output. A say that drew a jargon flag appeared to record none of its answers; on 2026-10-22 the message itself (`#comms` seq 18462, 34 answers) showed they are recorded, and the report came from a heartbeat replayed from before the post.
    - About 120 bus events in 30 minutes reached the commander's main loop, including six-part heartbeats listing twenty vibe-check ids.
    
    A silent or slow tool teaches the commander to work around it, and the workarounds are new copies of facts. The fix is at each owner, once.
    
    ## Steps, in order
    
    ### 1. The live stores stay whole, and lock waits name their holder
    
    - `CoordinationStore.observed()` (`coordination_database.py:220`) and `is_database()` (`:118`) open a plain handle on the live database inside processes that hold SQLite locks on it; closing that handle drops the process's locks. This is the likely cause of the 2026-10-21 corruption (fork AL's forensics). The required answer is what sits at the path (missing, not a regular file, not our database, our store); the store's own read-only connection answers it, so the header read is deleted. Callers: `transcripts.py:397`, `coordination_tables/refusals.py:71`, `notification_assignment.py:350`, `installer/backup.py:271`.
    - Installer backup and restore (`installer/backup.py:271-278`, `:360-366`) take the store's own lock instead of relying on writers having been stopped.
    - The bus wire lock, its hand-spelled paths and the store lock wait (`store_files.py:157`, which must fail within seconds naming the holder) belong to the virtual bus batch (#2549), which rewrites them; this plan does not touch them.
    
    **Done when** no code outside a store's owner opens its live file, and a lock held during an install is named in the install log within seconds.
    
    ### 1c. Installs never let a second runtime change the live stores
    
    Found 2026-10-22: a store writer reconciles any schema difference on open (`coordination_database.py:262`, `typed_table.py:1812`, `goal_history.py:156`, `cli_bridges/shared.py:170`), so any newer-code process that opens the live bus migrates it, outside maintenance and before the backup. Install 53 left the live coordination store on the new schema and aborted; the old runtime then refused the store and every unit failed to restart.
    
    - `reconcile_schema` takes the writer, and inside its existing schema-differs branch asks `writer.require_schema_change()`: allowed only while this process holds the bus's maintenance hold (`MaintenanceStatus.require_held_by(holder)`: the open member refuses, a held member compares nonces). One rule for every StoreWriter; fresh empty stores still create their schema.
    - The installer reconciles each declared store under the hold, after the backup, with the staged runtime, so owners start against stores that already match.
    - Step dry runs and `before_stop` run on the practice copy and under the hold, never on the live root before it.
    - `ingress_async` holding a shared lock across its caller's awaits (the fleet's shared locks starved installs 52 and 53 of the exclusive lock) is #2549's: that batch rewrites `ingress_async` onto the registry lock and still yields inside it (PR comment, 2026-10-22).
    
    **Done when** a newer runtime opening the live bus outside an install fails loudly naming the store and the hold it lacks, and an install with running units completes without anyone stopping them by hand.
    
    ### 1d. Main's own tests pass
    
    On 2026-10-22 the full CI workflow on main showed 197 failures, 127 of them in `tests/guards/test_debt_ratchet.py`, and the merge queue's install rehearsal would have failed every PR queued after #2595. A red on main makes every later run ask whether a red is real (rules/tests-and-commands.md). Every red is fixed at its owner or handed to a named open PR, one cause per change.
    
    - Declared evidence paths: a path a plan phase names that main never held reads as absent and passes (`phase_evidence.py` `present_modules`); a guard proves every declared path exists in git history.
    
    **Done when** the CI workflow passes on main, and a red that lands is owned the tick it appears.
    
    ### Installer completion in progress
    
    The installer is the current priority before resuming the other plans. Keep defects
    found while tracing it in this change, including these unfinished repairs:
    
    - [x] Read the old stores with the outgoing runtime before migration, and the migrated
      stores with the incoming runtime afterward, in rehearsal and live installation.
    - [x] Let the maintenance hold own its permission's lifetime on success and recovery.
    - [x] Carry declared operations and their answer types through the existing codec;
      keep migration results separate from diagnostic output.
    - [x] Replace inline interpreter probes throughout the installer, including package
      resolution. Ask the selected runtime without accidentally importing the checkout.
    - [ ] Repair affected test setup, then exercise rehearsal, failure recovery and the
      installed entry path. Report source checks and actual installation separately.
    - [ ] Finish shared SQLite ownership: file copies, digests, connections and snapshots
      belong to `SQLiteFile`; coordinator schema/session behavior stays in its subclass.
      Migrate the generic consumers and delete the subclass dependencies.
    - [ ] Repair the paired Toad test family's stale agent ownership and launch setup,
      then qualify a saved fork through immediate opening, a fresh DM, its first reply
      and tab return. Fix demonstrated application defects uncovered on this path.
    
    #### Implemented ownership and migration order
    
    `before_stop` had no implementations in main or the pending virtual-bus branch.
    Delete that phase rather than designing recovery around dead work. Live order is:
    hold maintenance; stop outgoing owners while their store format still exists; capture
    the original files and outgoing read; finish the backup; migrate and reconcile; read
    with the incoming runtime; compare against rehearsal; publish; release maintenance;
    restart. Taking a backup before owners stop would allow their final writes to fall
    outside recovery.
    
    `ChangedInstall` now owns rehearsal and live installation. `PreparedMigration` owns
    the original snapshot, outgoing read and common migration/check sequence;
    `BackedUpMigration` adds recovery from `StoreBackup`. `MaintenanceState.holding`
    owns permission lifetime, including restoration after nested holds fail. Delete the
    detached `rehearse`, `live`, `before_stop`, `carry_all` and `carry_and_read` paths.
    
    `CarryOperation` owns invocation arguments and behavior. `InterpreterOperation`
    derives answer encoding from the operation's return annotation through `FieldCodec`.
    Workers write answers separately from diagnostics, replacing dynamic method lookup,
    boolean argument bags and last-stdout-line parsing (IMPL-7). Runtime probes use that
    same answer contract under the selected interpreter; `InstallCommands` owns process
    execution and timing. Launch, native tests and package resolution use that owner.
    
    Source inventory uses NRA's parser, `ModuleSyntaxIndex` and `ClassFamilyIndexBuilder`
    over installer modules, maintenance and cutover declarations. Dynamic cutover imports
    remain resolved by `CarryChain` at runtime; AST evidence does not prove their behavior.
    The current pass parsed all 15 modules and projected all 113 original class declarations.
    The existing CI ratchet misses the old computed-method dispatch, stdout protocol and
    manual permission lifetime: its literal-name and multi-arm measures do not establish
    these ownership relationships.
    
    Validation: 57 focused checks passed across carry execution, maintenance, package
    resolution, publication and install announcements. A real worker that writes then

    restores the resource, checkout, runtime pointer, launcher, maintenance state and
    retained thread. Those results cover `f47cda95e`.
    
    SQLite connection, snapshot and copy behavior now belongs to `SQLiteFile`;
    coordinator, journal, installer and typed-store consumers use that owner.
    `DurableStore` composes installation reconciliation; `DerivedStore` owns runtime

    history, snapshots and required maintenance refusals. Earlier connection/copy

        def table_schema(cls) -> type[CoordinatorTable]:
            return CoordinatorTable
    
        @staticmethod
        def observed(path: Path) -> StoreFile:
            """Never let a read-only SQLite open create a WAL shared-memory sidecar.
    
            WAL-mode SQLite can create -shm even when opened with mode=ro. Refuse such a
            database *before* opening SQLite; rollback-journal mode is the current
            coordinator configuration. Do not create directories, chmod, or recover a
            hot journal. A concurrent WAL conversion is outside this schema contract.
            """
            try:
                info = path.lstat()
                if not stat.S_ISREG(info.st_mode):
                    return InvalidStore("Coordinator is not a regular file")
                with path.open("rb") as stream:
                    header = stream.read(100)
            except FileNotFoundError:
                return MissingStore()
            except PermissionError as error:
                return InvalidStore(str(error))
            if len(header) < 100 or not header.startswith(SQLiteFile.header):
                return InvalidStore("Coordinator has an invalid SQLite header")
            if header[18:20] != b"\x01\x01":
                return InvalidStore("Coordinator is not in rollback-journal mode")
            return ReadableStore(path)
    
        def __init__(
            self, path: str | os.PathLike[str],
            contention: StoreContention = DEFAULT_STORE_CONTENTION,
        ) -> None:
            super().__init__(Path(path))
            self._prepare_private_file()
            self._connection = self._open_connection(contention)
            try:
                self._configure_connection()
                self._initialize_schema()
                self._enforce_private_modes()
            except BaseException:
                self._connection.close()

    """Long-running services a host runs on the installed code, each declared by its owner.
    
    A service keeps the code it loaded when it started, so an install restarts every declared
    service that is running on this host onto the installed runtime. A host that does not run a
    service has no instance of it and contributes nothing: there is no list of services to keep.
    """
    
    from __future__ import annotations
    
    import json
    import os
    import socket
    import subprocess
    import time
    from abc import abstractmethod
    from dataclasses import dataclass
    from pathlib import Path
    from typing import Annotated, ClassVar, Self
    
    from ..declared_family import DeclaredFamily
    from ..field_codec import PathText
    from ..launch_runtime import LaunchRuntime
    
    
    class ServiceNotServingError(RuntimeError):
        """A restarted service did not serve its installed runtime's contract."""
    
    
    @dataclass(frozen=True)
    class RestartedService:
        """One host service an install restarted, in its own words, and the runtime it now
        serves from."""
    
        service: str
        runtime: Annotated[Path, PathText]
    
        def line(self) -> str:
            return f"{self.service} restarted onto {self.runtime}"
    
    
    class HostService(DeclaredFamily, affix="Service", discovery_package=__name__):
        """One running instance of a declared service on this host."""
    
        patience: ClassVar[int] = 30
        """Seconds a restarted service has to serve again."""
    
        @classmethod
        @abstractmethod
        def running(cls) -> tuple[Self, ...]:
            """This service's instances on this host; none when the host does not run it."""
    
        @abstractmethod
        def restart(self) -> None:
            """Stop this instance and start it again from its own launcher."""
    
        @abstractmethod
        def runtime(self) -> Path:
            """The interpreter this instance runs."""
    
        @abstractmethod
        def serves(self) -> None:
            """Prove the service answers; raise ServiceNotServingError naming a failure."""
    
        @abstractmethod
        def described(self) -> str:
            """This instance in the words an install's report and its failures use."""
    
        @classmethod
        def restart_running(cls, installed: Path) -> tuple[RestartedService, ...]:
            """Restart every declared service running on this host onto ``installed``."""
            return tuple(
                instance.restart_onto(installed)
                for member in cls.members_with(cls)
                for instance in member.running()
            )
    
        def restart_onto(self, installed: Path) -> RestartedService:
            self.restart()
            failure = f"{self.described()} did not serve again within {self.patience}s"
            for _ in range(self.patience):
                for instance in type(self).running():
                    runtime = instance.runtime()
                    if runtime == installed:
                        instance.serves()
                        return RestartedService(instance.described(), installed)
                    failure = f"{instance.described()} runs {runtime}, not the installed {installed}"
                time.sleep(1)
            raise ServiceNotServingError(failure)
    
    
    @dataclass(frozen=True)
    class SystemdUserService(HostService, declared_name=None):
        """Systemd owns the unit's process; its definition starts that process again.
    
        Its owned unit declares readiness. The process reports READY=1 once it serves,
        so a restart returns only when it is serving. Systemd, not this configuration,
        owns the current PID.
        """
    
        program: ClassVar[str]
        unit: ClassVar[str]
        notify_variable: ClassVar[str] = "NOTIFY_SOCKET"  # systemd's spelling of the supervisor socket
    
        @classmethod
        def ready(cls) -> None:
            """Tell the supervisor this process serves.
    
            Every launch has one: systemd for the installed unit, ``tests/connector_readiness.py``
            for a test. A launch without NOTIFY_SOCKET has nobody to tell and fails here, loudly.
            """
            address = os.environ[cls.notify_variable]
            target = "\0" + address[1:] if address.startswith("@") else address
            with socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX, socket.SOCK_DGRAM) as notify:
                notify.connect(target)
                notify.sendall(b"READY=1")
    
        @property
        def unit_file(self) -> Path:
            return Path.home() / ".config/systemd/user" / self.unit
    
        def unit_text(self, arguments: tuple[str, ...]) -> str:
            executable = LaunchRuntime.current_pointer() / "bin" / self.program
            # systemd uses C-quoted words, then expands specifiers and environment
            # references. Protect literal percent/dollar signs before quoting.
            command = " ".join(json.dumps(word.replace("%", "%%").replace("$", "$$"),
                                          ensure_ascii=False)
                               for word in (str(executable), *arguments))
            return (
                f"[Unit]\nDescription={self.unit}\n\n"
                "[Service]\nType=notify\nNotifyAccess=main\n"
                f"ExecStart={command}\nRestart=on-failure\n\n"
                "[Install]\nWantedBy=default.target\n"
            )
    
        def install(self, arguments: tuple[str, ...]) -> None:
            self.unit_file.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            self.unit_file.write_text(self.unit_text(arguments), encoding="utf-8")
            subprocess.run(("systemctl", "--user", "daemon-reload"), check=True)
            subprocess.run(("systemctl", "--user", "enable", self.unit), check=True)
    
        @classmethod
        def pid(cls) -> int:
            return int(subprocess.check_output(
                ("systemctl", "--user", "show", "-p", "MainPID", "--value", cls.unit),
                text=True,
            ))
    
        @classmethod
        @abstractmethod
        def from_process(cls, pid: int) -> Self:
            """Read this instance's declared configuration from its running process."""
    
        @classmethod
        def running(cls) -> tuple[Self, ...]:
            pid = cls.pid()
            return () if pid == 0 else (cls.from_process(pid),)
    
        @classmethod
        def process_arguments(cls, pid: int) -> tuple[str, ...]:
            arguments = tuple(os.fsdecode(word) for word in
                              Path(f"/proc/{pid}/cmdline").read_bytes().split(b"\0")[:-1])
            if not arguments or not arguments[0]:
                raise ServiceNotServingError(f"{cls.unit} has no running command")
            return arguments
    
        def runtime(self) -> Path:
            return Path(self.process_arguments(self.pid())[0])
    
        def restart(self) -> None:
            subprocess.run(("systemctl", "--user", "restart", self.unit), check=True)

        @classmethod
        def published_launch(cls) -> LaunchRoot:

            return InstallRun.start(self, route.root).launch(output)
    
        def apply(self, ctx: Comms) -> CliResult:
            """The install child's last step, on the bus it carried or created."""
            home = Path.home()
            record = self.commander.configured(CommanderRecord.read(ctx.root), self.repos, ctx.root, home)
            return InstallResult(record.write(home), {
                type(harness).declared_name: harness.register(ctx, self.project)
        """A live migration carries the recovery data its failure path needs."""
    
        backup: ResourceBackup
    
        def restore(self) -> None:
            if not self.backup.original():
                self.backup.restore()
    
    
    class ChangedInstall(ExistingBusInstall[RehearsedFiles]):
        def rehearsal(self, practice: PracticeBus) -> CarriedRehearsal:
            copied = practice.copied
            home = practice.scratch / "home"
            RehearsalHome(home).prepare()
            (home / ".claude").symlink_to(Path.home() / ".claude")
            stack = replace(self.staged, home=home)
            stack.prepare_native()
            for path in stack.backup_files(self.root, self.pending, self.tree):
                destination = copied / path.relative_to(self.root)
                if path.exists() and not destination.exists():
                    destination.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
                    shutil.copy2(path, destination)
            self.installed.running_owners(copied)
            maintenance = MaintenanceBarrier(RegistryStore.at(copied).path)
            hold = maintenance.begin(MaintenanceOperator.current())
            with hold.holding():
                with PreparedMigration.capture(hold, self.installed) as migration:
                    pass
                passed = migration.carry(self.pending, stack, self.tree)
            maintenance.clear(hold)
            return passed.extended(CarriedRehearsal, copy=practice.measurement)
    
        def uncopied(self) -> UncopiedRehearsal:
            return UncopiedRehearsal()
    
        def live(self, rehearsal: RehearsedFiles) -> CarriedRun:
            expected = frozenset(rehearsal.files.names) | frozenset(
                str(path.relative_to(self.root)) for path in self.staged.backup_files(self.root, self.pending, self.tree))
            selected = tuple(self.root / name for name in sorted(expected))
            restore = RestoreSpace.measure(max(
                rehearsal.files.restore_bytes,
                sum(path.stat().st_size for path in selected if path.exists()),
            ), self.root.parent)
            restore.require()
            running = self.installed.running_owners(self.root)
            maintenance = MaintenanceBarrier(RegistryStore.at(self.root).path)
            held = maintenance.begin(MaintenanceOperator.current())
            holder = ExitStack()
            holder.enter_context(held.holding())  # this run's own CLI calls read under its hold
            try:
                try:
                    self.installed.owners(self.root, StopCliCommand, running)
                    planned = self.staged.cli(self.root, PlannedReconcileCliCommand)
                    unrehearsed = sorted(frozenset(planned.rewritten) - frozenset(rehearsal.files.names))
                    if unrehearsed:
                        raise UpgradeRefused(
                            f"Reconcile would rewrite files the rehearsal did not: {unrehearsed}")
                    with PreparedMigration.capture(held, self.installed) as original:
                        migration = original.extended(BackedUpMigration, backup=StoreBackup.take(
                            self.root, active_route_path(), selected, self.spill_dir))
                except BaseException as error:
                    holder.close()
                    maintenance.clear(held)
                    started = self.installed.start(self.root, running)
                    print(f"install: aborted before the backup ({type(error).__name__}: {error}); "
                          f"maintenance cleared; owners: {started}", file=sys.stderr)
                    raise
                try:
                    self.staged.commands.run("git", "-C", self.checkout, "merge", "--ff-only", "-q", self.target)
                    Checkout(self.checkout).prepare()
                    self.staged.prepare_native()
                    passed = migration.carry(self.pending, self.staged, self.tree)
                    passed.files.require_rehearsal(rehearsal.files)
                    self.staged.publish()
                    holder.close()
                    maintenance.clear(held)
                    services = HostService.restart_running(self.staged.python)
                except BaseException as error:
                    print(f"install: install failed ({type(error).__name__}: {error}); "
                          "restoring original installation", file=sys.stderr)
                    state = maintenance.read()
                    recovery = state.phase.hold_for(maintenance, state, MaintenanceOperator.current())
                    holder.close()
                    holder.enter_context(recovery.holding())
                    migration.restore()
                    restored = maintenance.read()
                    restored_hold = restored.phase.hold_for(
                        maintenance, restored, MaintenanceOperator.current())
                    holder.close()
                    holder.enter_context(restored_hold.holding())
                    head = self.installed.commands.run("git", "-C", self.checkout, "rev-parse", "HEAD").strip()
                    if head != self.current:
                        self.installed.commands.run("git", "-C", self.checkout, "reset", "-q", "--keep", self.current)
                        Checkout(self.checkout).prepare()
                    self.installed.publish()
                    holder.close()

## Activity

    Sent by Codex from task 01a165c5-ce0b-7e32-8142-e8b308b303bd
    Early judgment: the corruption mechanism is real, not merely likely style debt. SQLite's own howtocorrupt §2.2 names this exact 16-byte file-type probe: raw open/read/close can trash locks held by other connections in-process. observed() consumers are deferred reads through ReadableStore; backup content_owner probes undeclared resources and must retain physical detection. I am tracing a connection-owned probe that refuses WAL without creating -shm. I reject immutable=1 as a casual escape hatch: SQLite says it asserts the live file cannot change. No patch yet; preserving both contracts is the actual design question.

    Sent by Codex from task 01a165c5-ce0b-7e32-8142-e8b308b303bd
    The hard edge: SQLite PRAGMA journal_mode has NeedSchema in its own generated pragma table, so normal mode=ro probing can create WAL -shm before we reject it. Immutable/nolock would lie about live-file changes and drop locking. Generic is_database can safely use a normal SQLite metadata query (only SQLITE_NOTADB means plaintext; BUSY/corrupt must propagate). Coordinator's no-sidecar WAL classification needs more: SQLite documents connection-local locking_mode=EXCLUSIVE before first WAL access uses heap wal-index, but that can acquire an exclusive lock on unsupported WAL input, contrary to the standing reader rule. Tracing whether existing observer lifetime admits a cleaner connection-owned boundary; no raw-fd substitute patch.

    I need to call out a real contract collision, not invent a green patch: stdlib sqlite3 exposes SQL queries, not SQLite's VFS header-read/file-control API. journal_mode needs schema; normal RO query can create WAL shm. EXCLUSIVE-before-query avoids shm (official SQLite WAL §8) but violates our no-exclusive-reader rule on unsupported WAL inputs. immutable/nolock is also wrong for a live file. The clean ways are a connection-owned VFS inspection API, or an explicit decision that a nonwaiting classification probe may acquire exclusive on invalid WAL input (DELETE files still shared). I won't silently weaken either promise. I'm checking existing native/library surfaces before proposing added machinery.

## Assistant

Yes. **Treat the conversation as an evolving system that must preserve and supply required facts.** Then use the paper’s counts, rather than inventing a “good conversation” score.

The paper already gives us the starting point: an encoding \(e\), required answers \(a\), and a decoder \(r\), with the obligation \(r(e(x))=a(x)\). For a conversation, the encoding is the context actually available to a participant: messages, retained declarations, references, and their relationships. The required answer might be an interpretation, a decision, or an action. [Paper, §2](/home/ts/Downloads/paper1_oopsla.pdf)

That exposes three concrete things to measure:

- **Lost distinctions.** If “no empty acknowledgments” and “no useful commentary” become the same internal representation, the encoding has erased a distinction the required behavior depends on. That is an answer-preservation failure.
- **Outside supply.** You declare “use sharp, candid commentary.” If you must separately restate its application to me, each fork, reviews, and handoffs, those are candidate fact–application pairs being supplied manually instead of derived from the declaration.
- **Repair obligations.** When a requirement changes, which separately maintained instructions, summaries, and agent contexts must someone repair to preserve it?

The important distinction is **repetition versus independent authority**. Quoting your instruction to a fork can be faithful transport from one owner. Rewriting it into a separately maintained instruction that subsequently drifts creates another maintenance obligation. Counting repeated words would miss the actual defect.

And the paper’s distinction between forced cost and removable excess becomes useful here: what does the available conversation mechanism force you to supply, and what extra work comes from how we’ve arranged it? Those minima need an explicit model of the mechanism; the paper’s numerical inheritance bounds don’t automatically become conversational bounds.

So “please stop being stiff” ten times is a concrete investigation target: **which required applications failed to derive from the original declaration, and why?** A charming eventual reply doesn’t erase the maintenance you performed to obtain it.

That makes your steering part of the measured system—not free labor we conveniently leave outside the accounting.

## User

i would make it goal oriented. for a given R how is a conversation optimally built?

## Assistant

Exactly. **Fix \(R\), then ask which conversation structure satisfies it with the least outside supply and repair.** “Pleasant,” “concise,” and “professional” don’t get to substitute for the requirements.

The object to optimize is a **conversation protocol**: given the history so far, what should be said, shown, asked, or done next? That includes branching when new evidence arrives.

For a fixed \(R\), I’d construct it this way:

1. **Specify the required outcome and distinctions.** What must participants know or do? Which confusions or actions are forbidden?
2. **Locate the original declarations and evidence.** Who or what owns each required fact?
3. **Map each fact to the decisions that require it.** This gives the conversational supply relation.
4. **Arrange derivation and communication so those decisions receive the facts from their owners.** Count the pairs still requiring separate manual supply.
5. **Across requirement changes, count the repairs needed to keep that arrangement correct.**

Then use the paper’s coordinatewise objective:

\[
\operatorname{Maint}^{*}(H_R)
=
\left(
  \bigl(\inf_C O_t(C)\bigr)_t,\;
  \inf_C B_{\mathrm{rep}}(C)
\right)
\]

Here the admissible conversations must preserve the required answers **and achieve the specified behavior**. We would need to define the conversational repair operations precisely; that makes the application formal rather than borrowing the notation decoratively.

Take our installer work. If \(R\) requires a working installed system with preserved sessions, “47 tests passed” supplies evidence for one intermediate question. It cannot discharge “does the installed application work?” A conversation that collapses those questions has already failed, however efficiently it communicates the test result.

Your repeated steering is another case: once you declare how justified criticism should work, its applicability to reviews and forks should follow through the shared context. Having you manually reconnect those pairs is outside supply.

**The construction target is: each necessary declaration once, its consequences available wherever required, and new turns supplying genuinely new evidence, requirements, or decisions.**

Humor can belong in that construction when it helps preserve engagement or makes a correction land. Its value is judged against \(R\) and the resulting trajectory—not against an independent rule that serious work must sound miserable.

    ## 2026-10-14 — No lock held across a decode; readers never block
    
    Tristan: "why do we have so many issues wit hdecoding large fiel enirely over and over again and holding locks ofr not raso nits fuckign stupid, awwe want async not hodlign locks when it doesn' needto happen and deconding shit unecessarily"
    
    Witness: 10:52-10:57 every agent and CLI waited on
    `.bus_route_counts.sqlite3.lock` while one `watch` reader rebuilt the route
    projection from the whole 3.7 GB bus inside `BusRouteCounts.sync`.
    
    A reader never takes an exclusive lock. Readers of an append-only file read
    committed bytes up to a captured size; readers of SQLite use WAL snapshots.
    A writer holds its lock only to capture a cut or commit a bounded result,
    never across decoding, scanning or I/O proportional to file size: decode
    outside the lock, then commit with a revision check. Durable state that is
    rewritten whole on each change (a JSON file of all rows) is a defect; it is
    appended or keyed so a change costs its own size. Waiting for a lock is
    async in owners and never stalls an event loop.
